## The pipeline

```
tracker.api / create → tracker.scaffold → client drops into the household inbox → tracker.filer → tracker.scanner → tracker.reminder (on DRAFT_WEEKDAY) → tracker.view (the last step of every pass) → a person sends the draft
```

RECORD_FILENAME is runner.AFTER_INSTALL_FILENAME (one spelling; runner cannot import this module). _schedule answers scheduling.REFUSED_DRIVE with 186's sentence as a failure. _check says an OSError by errors.said (its class), the record's and the store's own errors whole. Merge review fixes: move_left_behind treats CHECKPOINT_UNIT (checkpoint, its journal, a .damaged copy, by checkpoint's constants) as one - a journal without its checkpoint beside it, or a home holding any part, moves nothing (LEFT_BEHIND_JOURNAL_ALONE); move_schedule_here asks settings.program_drive_refusal() first and changes nothing when it refuses; every OSError said by class (the check, the claim, the registration, the mover) is also kept whole with errors.keep on the local debug log. Pilot P21: run(start=None, every=None) registers the choice saved in settings.json at every door; a named start/every is checked and saved first; off removes this computer's task and leaves the designation alone; a refused saved choice is a recorded failure (PREFERENCE_KEY) and registers nothing; the record holds the preference and launch() runs the step again when it differs. Pilot P47: one run at a time - run() and launch() hold after-install.lock beside the record (locking.acquire_lock, so a lock whose process ended is taken over) from before the saved choice is read until the record is written, waiting up to LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS and otherwise changing nothing (STEP_BUSY); every task it removes is noted on the debug log with why. The rename's carry-over (P155 Q2, pilot/SPEC-rename.md section 3): _carry_over_settings() runs first in _run(), before the settings are read - from the packaged program only, it copies settings.json byte for byte from settings.earlier_settings_path() when this program has none (an in-place upgrade finds one file; an existing file wins), verified by SHA-256, the earlier file left, its path checks inside its own error handling so an access error is SETTINGS_CARRY_FAILED; _replace_earlier_task() runs right after _schedule() and, from the packaged program only (_installed_program(), the seam its tests set; from source it says EARLIER_TASK_FROM_SOURCE and asks Task Scheduler nothing, so a checkout never deletes an installed copy's task), removes the task named settings.EARLIER_PRODUCT_NAME through scheduling.remove_task(task_name=...) - that name only, never the production task - unless the schedule failed this run, when it is kept. Each says one sentence every run (SETTINGS_* and EARLIER_TASK_*), kept in the record's 'carried' list and leading the printed lines; read_record() reads a record without it as nothing carried. A failed copy or removal is in 'failed', so no identity is recorded and the next launch runs the step again; a carry-over that is not a failure raises no notice. P198 (F6, pilot/SPEC-F6-schedule-after-reinstall.md): launch()'s _unchanged() asks _task_missing(record) last - only when the record's schedule is scheduling.REGISTERING (this computer claimed or registered it, and the designation already matched), one scheduling.task_query() (schtasks /query) on the designated computer; anything but exit 0 runs the step - a refusal's exit code kept on the debug log once per start (QUERY_REFUSED), an OSError (a schtasks that cannot start or runs past its 60 s limit) kept whole and said by the step as SCHEDULE_UNREACHABLE - whose /create /f registers the task again or says SCHEDULE_FAILED - so a task an uninstall or a person deleted comes back at the next start, and a computer the designation does not name, or a schedule that is off, is never asked. P218 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md, S3): the setup door's last job, _ready_the_overview(root, reason, check), makes the Overview ready - only for REASON_SETUP, a saved root not refused and a store file present; it calls store.close() first, so this process lets go of its store and checkpoint before another process reads, then runner.fill_firm_cache(str(root)); never a failure; its sentence (OVERVIEW_READY / OVERVIEW_NOT_READY, AfterInstall.overview_sentence) is the last of lines, before any failure. The launch, root and Repair doors leave the Overview to the app, which asks one at once. The pilot installer reaches this door through api_entry's setup mode (Q1). P214: CHECKPOINT_UNIT names the checkpoint's -wal and -shm, and _CHECKPOINT_SIDE_FILES moves nothing when a journal, log or shared memory is found without its checkpoint. installer_exit_code (behind INSTALLER_CODES_FLAG, passed only by api_entry's setup mode) tells the pilot installer when the step could not finish (10) or the Overview could not be prepared (11); exit_code is untouched, so Setup.bat and the app's doors still count an unprepared Overview as no failure.
- **`tracker/api.py`** — The JSON command layer the desktop app talks to; COMMANDS is the list, and the module docstring is pinned to it. Since decision 104 it owns the request-list editor's words (EDITOR_* labels, RULES_SAVED, NOTHING_CHANGED, LEARNED_NOTE) and the edit command that saves the list and the engagement's details as one recorded event. Decision 113 added the unlearn command and the editor's two words for taking a taught keyword back (UNLEARN_LABEL, UNLEARNED_NOTE). Decision 130: create, rollover, edit, assign, hand-over (both households), dismiss, unfile and restore refresh the client README of the household they changed through filer.refresh_household_readme(), once the action has succeeded - a refused action refreshes nothing. Since decision 193 every reply carries warnings and every error a failure {sentence, kind, seq, identifier} beside the unchanged error, decided once in _failure_of() (a worded refusal in its own sentence, anything else by class, its traceback to the error log only); watch (a lock and its pass's progress, no store) and cancel-pass (Stop, for a pass this app started) are its commands. watch accepts the folder a lock was reported in, a return or a household (the review's S1), and a failed redraw after a pass keeps its counts whatever it raised (M2).
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.api`

  - note: Every command prints one JSON object and returns an exit code - errors are JSON too, never a traceback. This is the only module the Electron app knows about. The create path validates rows with the same sentences the manifest's validation uses, and never leaves a half-built engagement behind: create_engagement() validates whole before a line is written, and on any later failure _undo_create() removes the folder first and then drops the store row in its own try, so a store that cannot be reached masks nothing and keeps no folder. list/priors use the same discovery as the scheduled run; create and rollover record the details a person sent from the app (client/link/due) (rollover carries client, sender, firm and reminders, never last year's link or due); assign files a parked document by a person's choice and re-scans. unlock clears a stale lock; state carries the lock; templates carries each form's tax year and create names a new-client engagement from client, year and form when no name is given. create takes the tax year (calendar default) and shifts catalog rows to it; rollover writes Rolled From so the prior retires; priors report superseded_by. Since decision 203 Sort & Scan is run-now (PASS_COMMAND), which hands runner.main the scheduled job's own arguments plus no draft, the progress lines and the household (runner.run_now_arguments) - the app's button and the scheduled job make the same pass. The clients root comes from tracker.settings (settings, set-root, install-schedule commands); the new-return dialog never writes Engagement Name, and reads the firm from settings.firm(). install-schedule works in the packaged app too. ENGAGEMENT_FLAG with nothing after it, or an empty folder, gets the same sentence as no flag; once a root is set the folder must lie under it. assign takes the lock twice on purpose (file, then re-scan). _vocab() hands the renderer every word it shows - the app carries no Python vocabulary of its own. Decision 55: containment is checked whenever a root is set (since decision 176 by the path's own parse, since decision 188 door.return_dir). Decision 67: a blank name falls back to the client's name sanitised. Decision 68: _tax_year() bounds the year on create and rollover alike, through manifest.check_tax_year() (decision 72). Decision 75: a pass made from the app is on the record the scheduled run leaves - _record_pass (removed by decision 203) appends the run log's line and redraws the status page. Decision 76: dismiss records that no request asks for a parked document and does not re-scan; _vocab() carries the decision under the key 'dismissed', not the word. Decision 77: unfile sends one filed document back for review. Decision 82: state's index rows carry evidence as data (_evidence_payload()). Decision 84: state carries 'review' - tracker.review.triage() over the rows state has already loaded, serialised by _triage_payload(). Decision 86: create records the dialog's catalog choice in the details; _state() ships it (_info_payload() is asdict() over EngagementInfo). Decision 89: _state() ships view: {state, path} from tracker.view.view_state(). Decision 91: paths['view'] is an .html file and _vocab()['view'] carries the button's own label. Decision 102: standing_rules() fills rule 2 from records.THE_RECORD; _state() calls filer.ensure() before reading the rows, so showing an engagement stays a read. DECISION 104: the edit command takes {items, engagement} from the editor, converts each row with manifest.item_from_fields() (each refusal naming its row), refuses any engagement key outside records.ENGAGEMENT_EDITABLE by name, and saves through manifest.save_rules(), replying with what changed, what was removed, which details moved, whether anything was recorded, and the warnings; a detail sent blank is cleared and one left out keeps its recorded value; a refusal is the usual error sentence and nothing is recorded. _state() gained 'rules' (the person's rows as stored - WITHOUT the keywords filings taught, so the editor never turns a taught word into a typed one), 'learned' (those keywords, keyed by the row's identifier) and 'warnings' (manifest.check_rules()); 'engagement' is the details from the record; paths lost the workbook. _vocab() gained 'columns' (each column's key, header and help from manifest.COLUMNS and COLUMN_HELP) and 'editor' (every word the editor shows, the details' fields with which are editable, the yes/no words, the two one-character values and the floors the number inputs take their minimum from); the check command and the Carried Forward sheet's name left with the things they named. DECISION 112: _state() reads store.document_seqs() once and hangs each row's sequence number beside it - on every 'index' row and on every 'review' item (_triage_payload takes the mapping) - never inside the row, because it is the record's bookkeeping and not a fact about the document. _cmd_assign, _cmd_dismiss and _cmd_unfile read spec['seq'] through _seq_of() and refuse a spec without one by NO_SEQ (a ManifestError): the app is always drawn from state, so a caller with no version is a caller with no view. _cmd_assign also computes the shortlist itself - _shortlist_now() reads the index, finds the row with filer.find_parked() and asks review.shortlist_for() over load_manifest() - and hands the identifiers to the filer, which imports neither; its payload gains 'overrode_shortlist'. This module is L4 and imports both, so the computation belongs here; the seq check under the lock is what makes a row that moved in between never get the handed-in shortlist written. DECISION 113: the unlearn command takes {identifier, keyword} from the editor, records one keyword_unlearned through manifest.unlearn_keyword() and then re-scans the engagement the way assign does (its own lock; a ScanLockedError becomes scan_note), because the request's rules just moved and a copy that passed only on that word should regress now rather than on Saturday. _vocab()['editor'] gained unlearn_label and unlearned_note - the button beside each taught keyword and the sentence after it - and the renderer types neither. Decision 117: _info_from_spec() and _info_payload() read records.DATE_FIELDS rather than naming the due date, _vocab()['editor']['date_fields'] tells the editor which boxes are dates, and rollover.with_default_dates() fills a blank Filing Deadline and Due Date from the form's own table on create and on rollover - so the reminder's ladder works without a person typing a date, and what a person typed is never written over. settings and set-root carry the firm's phone beside its name, and _vocab()['settings'] carries that box's label, its sentence and the number as recorded; _reminder_payload() takes the index rows state has already read, so the card shows the parked-file hold the draft day will. DECISION 110: _state() gains 'moved', its own list beside 'review' rather than a column on the index - one entry per FILE_MOVED row with the row's sequence number, the home the record put the copy at, where its bytes are now (None for a row whose bytes are nowhere under the firm's folder) and, only where the copy sits directly in Prepared under a name that belongs to a request (decision 168), which request that is, matched by scaffold.assign_files(), the same answer the filer and the scan read. The restore command is _cmd_restore(), the third review action beside assign and unfile and the only new one: it takes the row's seq like the others and returns what the put-back found (moved_home, copied_from_original, already_home, parked_as) beside the rewritten row. _vocab()['review_labels'] carries the card's every word - RESTORE_LABEL, KEEP_LABEL, SEND_TO_REVIEW_LABEL, MOVED_HEADING, MOVED_SUMMARY and MOVED_NOWHERE, the word for a copy that is nowhere - so the renderer types none of them, and _shortlist_now() finds a moved row too, because keep-it-here goes through the same assign command and the same picker. DECISION 114: _vocab()['review_labels'] carries the review card's second rendering too - ACCEPT_LABEL, SKIP_LABEL, OPEN_IN_LIST_LABEL, the two words the toggle between the renderings shows (CARD_MODE_LABEL, LIST_MODE_LABEL) and CARD_POSITION, the pattern the card's position line is filled from. The heading over the card's suggestion is SUGGESTED_HEADING, the list's own: one queue, one word for a suggestion. No command is added and no payload changes - the cards are a rendering of the 'review' list this module already ships, and Accept is the assign command the list's File it makes. Decision 123: that function is no longer defined here - it moved to tracker.rollover, beside the carry rule that clears the dates, because the module's command line built engagements without it; create and rollover import it and are otherwise unchanged. Decision 118 added the reminder and approve commands and everything the Reminder card shows. reminder reads the record and the draft file and regenerates the letter in memory at whatever stage the toggle stands on - no lock, nothing written, and a held reminder answers with no letter at all; approve takes the engagement lock, refuses a stale panel by the fingerprint of the text it showed, writes the shown text (or approves an edited file as it stands), sets any other draft aside and records one draft_approved event. _vocab() carries the card's every word, the four stages with the palette key each carries and where each spends its emphasis, and page.PALETTE itself, so the renderer types neither a word nor a colour; state's paths now name the draft file, because the shell opens only paths this map holds. Decision 126 added two commands and the sharing words: roll-household rolls every ticked return of a household's open year through rollover.roll_household() and answers with the rolled, the skipped with their sentences, the retired by their labels and the state of the first return it made; mark-shared records one sharing_confirmed event on the household's record under its lock, refusing while the inbox link is blank (SHARE_LINK_FIRST) because that is the one part of the checklist the tracker can see was done. SHARING_CHECKLIST, SHARING_HEADING, SHARING_NOTE, MARK_SHARED_LABEL, SHARED_ON_LINE, NOT_YET_SHARED_LINE and ROLLOVER_UNTICKED_NOTE are the API's words; create hands the filled checklist back with a household's FIRST return and with no other, and state['household'] carries shared_on and the same filled lines until it is given. propose-spellings is the twenty-third command and a read: it proposes the spellings a document might print one name in and records nothing, because what a return matches on is what a person ticked (decision 128). create refuses a return with nobody on it. Decision 129 added the feed words (FEEDS_LABEL, FEEDS_LINE, FED_BY_LINE, ADD_FEED_LABEL, FEED_WARNING, RETURN_WARNING, HAND_OVER_LABEL, NOT_FED), the feeds field on edit-household, the feeds and fed_by the household card is drawn from, and assign's optional target - which hands the document to a return the drop folder feeds and refuses any other by name. The review of that build added the hand-over modal's own two words (HAND_OVER_RETURN_LABEL, HAND_OVER_REQUEST_LABEL), which the page had been borrowing from the household heading and the editor's title, and gave _cmd_scan a walk of the practice (_the_practice), so Run now sorts against the feed list exactly as the scheduled pass does rather than against the household's own returns alone; since decision 132 a root that cannot be walked is the runner's NO_PRACTICE, the reply's run error, and nothing is sorted. HANDED_OVER_LINE (review_labels.handed_over) is what the page says after a hand-over: the row here is released. Decision 131: _state() carries 'room' (room_for over the list it already loaded), 'room_note' (ROOM_SHORT filled, or '' - information the return's page shows, never a warning) and appends only ROOM_PARKS to the warnings; set-root answers 'short_of_room' - every working return short of room under the new root, in label order, with its numbers and filled sentences (one walk; the one time room is measured outside a pass) - and records the root regardless; the editor's save (_cmd_edit) refuses with PATH_TOO_LONG a CHANGED or new row whose canonical path passes 260, and never a row the person did not touch; install-schedule writes the job from settings_dir() and replies 'settings'. _vocab()['room'] holds the heading and the two sentences. - **`tracker/checkpoint.py`** — The record checkpoint (decision 159): what THIS machine last saw of every return's record - per record key, the count of lines it wrote or accepted and the chain head through them (ledger.chain_link's number), a durable intent - the chain each line a writer is about to append will have (Intent, expect(), intent()) - the clients root the checkpoint belongs to (claim_root / move_root), and the lines seen from other machines (table foreign_lines) until a person acknowledges them. One SQLite file, CHECKPOINT_FILENAME (record-heads.db), beside the store (path_for), CHECKPOINT_VERSION 1; an older file is set aside, a newer one refused, and one that will not open is refused by name (UNREADABLE) and never set aside by itself. foreign_lines_refused() is the one switch for whether a line from another machine is refused. CLI: python -m tracker.checkpoint <store> state | acknowledge <key> | move-root <root>.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.checkpoint`
  - constants: `CHECKPOINT_FILENAME` = 'record-heads.db', `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` = 1, `BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 5000, `SET_ASIDE_SUFFIX` = '.v{version}.old', `NEWER_FILE` = "{path} was written by a newer version of the app (version {version}; this one knows {known}). This machine has a newer version of the app's {what}; install that version again.", `LEFT_BEHIND` = "No record checkpoint was made: the one an earlier version kept is still at {old}. Move it into {home} (the runbook's decision-186 upgrade step); until then nothing is written.", `UNREADABLE` = "{path}: the app cannot read this machine's record checkpoint ({why}). Set the file aside by hand (runbook §6); the next pass seeds it again from the records - the moment of trust.", `BUSY` = "{path}: this machine's record checkpoint is busy - another run is using it ({why}). Nothing was changed; the next pass tries again. Do not set the file aside for this."
  - used by: `tracker/after_install.py`, `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/page.py`
  - writes: `artifact:record-heads.db`
  - reads: `artifact:record-heads.db`
  - tested by: `tests/test_checkpoint.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`, `tests/test_store.py`, `tests/test_tripwire.py`
  - note: Exists because the store is rebuilt from the record and so trusts whatever it is built from: the link in every line detects an accidental reorder, loss or edit, but a rewrite that recomputes the links is caught only here, and neither stops a writer who controls this machine. The store does the proving (store._prove_against_checkpoint) and holds one connection to this file a command (store._held_checkpoint, closed by store.close(); P214), reached through store._beside(); this module only keeps and hands back keys, counts, heads and hosts, and imports nothing of the package (its __main__ alone reaches page.tolerant_console) - tests/test_layers.py pins both. Never synced: it describes one machine. Survives deleting the store, which is the point. advance() clears the intent only once the count reaches its end, so a reader applying part of a writer's batch cannot clear the writer's intent; a line of this machine past the count is its own only when Intent.owns() it - exactly the promised bytes, so a line forged later into the same place is refused (review of part 3, M1). Per machine, not per firm, so several arbitrated writers could each keep their own: part 1 of SPEC-159 (the designated machine, viewer mode) is not built and waits on the multi-writer study, and Jason's C-1 (a) of 2026-09-26 names a foreign line every pass rather than refusing it - foreign_lines_refused() returns False and cites that. What it does not buy is in its docstring and row 159: no protection from a writer who controls this machine, no proof to a third party; a secret key was rejected. The moment of trust: a first sight, a new machine or an accepted recovery seeds it from the record as it then is. The rebase review's MF1/SF1: every statement goes through _Connection/_Cursor (the checkpoint's one choke point, as store._Connection is the store's), so any sqlite3.Error leaves as CheckpointUnavailable(CheckpointError) with code = the engine's error name and busy = SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED: BUSY ('try again, do not set it aside') or UNREADABLE ('set it aside by hand'). store.prove_the_root lets it through unconverted, so runner._pass codes it PASS_CHECKPOINT_BUSY / PASS_CHECKPOINT_UNREADABLE (never PASS_ROOT_NOT_CLAIMED) and serves no household, and the API says it in its own sentence; store._beside turns one met mid-catch-up into that return's StoreError. P214 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): the file is kept in SQLite's write-ahead log at synchronous = FULL, set on every connection by _write_ahead() at the end of _opened (journal_mode persists in the file, synchronous does not); a switch another connection refuses is no error and leaves the file in its own mode. CHECKPOINT_WAL_FILENAME and CHECKPOINT_SHM_FILENAME name its -wal and -shm, which the last writing connection's close removes.
- **`tracker/containers.py`** — Opens an email or a zip a client dropped, in memory, and hands back what was attached (decision 143): open_container(bytes, extension) gives each attachment's own name (safe_name(), a basename that cannot leave its folder) and bytes, and each part skipped with why (an inline picture, the message's own text, an attachment by reference or an OLE object); NotOpened carries the sentence a container parks with (reasons.CONTAINER_LOCKED, CONTAINER_DAMAGED, CONTAINER_EMPTY, CONTAINER_LIMIT). is_container() decides by the extension alone (.msg, .eml, .zip) - never magic bytes, because an .xlsx is a zip too.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.containers`
  - constants: `MAX_DEPTH` = 2, `MAX_ATTACHMENTS` = 200, `MAX_TOTAL_MB` = 250, `MAX_RATIO` = 100, `MAX_SKIPPED` = 200, `NAME_MAX` = 255, `LIMIT_PACKING` = "a file inside is packed in a way only a person's zip program opens", `SKIP_INLINE` = 'inline image, shown in the message rather than attached', `SKIP_BODY` = "the message's own text, never saved", `SKIP_REFERENCE` = 'attached by reference: it holds a link, not the document', `SKIP_OLE` = 'an embedded object that would have to be run to be read', `SKIP_EMPTY` = 'attached with nothing in it', `SKIP_FOLDER` = 'a folder entry', `UNNAMED` = 'attachment {n}', `KIND_EMAIL` = 'an email', `KIND_ZIP` = 'a zip'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/errors.py`, `tracker/layout.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`
  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/filer.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/page.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_containers.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/child_readers.py`, `tests/test_errors.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`
  - note: Writes nothing, decides nothing about a folder and holds no file open: the filer checks the size ceiling, open_bounded() opens the container, and the filer writes what comes back. Decision 154: open_bounded(path) runs open_file() - read the file, open_container() - in the reading's child (content_check.in_a_child, the stop for a file, 600 s), handed over by reference through _CHILD_OPENER; the child hands back the Opened (plain data), a refusal's sentence, or the file's OSError, and open_bounded raises NotOpened for a refusal, the stop (READING_STOPPED) or a crash after 'started' (READING_CRASHED), and returns None for a child that never started (the filer records nothing and reopens it next pass). The suite opens in its own process unless content_check.READ_IN_A_CHILD is on. Three parsers on untrusted input: the standard library's email (policy.default; the one module under tracker/ that may import it, for parsing only - tests/test_layers.py names the exception and proves in a subprocess that importing this module reaches no mail client or network module beyond the socket and urllib the standard library's own helpers pull in), zipfile streamed through a counting read (never extract or extractall; names decoded as the zip marks them), and olefile for .msg (BSD-2-Clause, pinned; opened with DEFECT_INCORRECT raised; its sector-chain loops are bounded by the stream's size and its directory walk refuses a re-referenced entry). The limits are constants here, each with a test at its edge: MAX_DEPTH 2, MAX_ATTACHMENTS 200, MAX_TOTAL_MB 250 counted from the bytes actually produced, MAX_RATIO 100 per zip member, and MAX_SKIPPED 200 parts left inside (each is named on the record's line); a name on the record is cut to NAME_MAX, 255. The whole container is opened before anything is written, so a limit leaves nothing behind. A container nested past the depth, or one inside that will not open, is handed back whole as an attachment carrying its sentence (Attachment.parks) and parks as a container of its own; an embedded .msg message past the depth has no bytes to hand back and stops the whole container. An unnamed part is 'attachment N' plus the extension its Content-Type names, from a fixed table (mimetypes reads the Windows registry, so two machines would name one part two ways). The CLI lists what a container holds and writes nothing. Decision 178: a zip holding any member packed other than content_check.PACKINGS parks from its directory as CONTAINER_LIMIT (LIMIT_PACKING) before a byte is unpacked; WinZip's AES stays CONTAINER_LOCKED. Decision 176: safe_name() drops every Unicode format character, so a right-to-left override cannot dress a program as a PDF in the firm's review folder. Decision 188: safe_name strips the layout's one invisible set (layout.is_invisible) instead of category Cf alone, keeping white space and control characters for the illegal-character rule; the module no longer imports unicodedata. Decision 190: CONTAINER_DAMAGED names errors.error_class(); _said() (class plus the first 120 characters of the message) is gone, because 120 characters is an SSN. Decision 190: NotOpened carries code (given, or the Said sentence's), Attachment carries the code its parks sentence was said with, open_file hands the child's sentence back as a Said, and the nested-limit check compares the code. safe_name delegates its character stripping to layout.recorded_name (decision 190), so a control character is now dropped rather than turned into '_'.
- **`tracker/content_check.py`** — Tier 3: extract text (pdfplumber / openpyxl / plain text, OCR for a scan or a photo) and test it against the row's keyword and date rules. extract() is the one reading of a document, used by the router and the scanner alike; ContentCache keeps the verdicts - in the store, per engagement, since decision 107.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.content_check`

  - note: The cache stores verdicts only - pass/fail, the reason, and the Evidence behind them, all of it the firm's own words. Extracted client text is never persisted. Only the first MAX_PAGES pages of a PDF are read, text or OCR - the identifying words are up front and a long ledger used to stall a run. Verdicts are keyed by the file's content digest and the row's rules fingerprint (CACHE_VERSION, carried on every row; a row at another version is ignored and dropped), with a per-path memo of size/mtime/digest so an unchanged file is not re-hashed: the same bytes are read twice in this system, once as a drop the router routes and once as the working copy the scanner checks, and a verdict the router reached is the verdict the scanner finds. extract(ocr=False) hands a scan back with needs_ocr set so the router can try the file's name first; extract_by_ocr() finishes the reading. The CLI (python -m tracker.content_check <engagement> <file>) prints what the document says and which rows accept it, writing no cache. DECISION 107 - THE CACHE LEFT THE SYNCED FOLDER: ContentCache(engagement_dir) loads the engagement's memos and verdicts from the store's two tables (store.cached_verdicts()) once, works in memory as it always did, and save() writes what it learned and forgot through store.remember_verdicts() - one immediate transaction of the store's own, under the engagement lock, never store.record(), because a verdict is a derivation of the bytes and the rules and not an event; a pass killed mid-save leaves the previous rows. ContentCache() with no engagement is memory only (the CLI's, a test's) and its save() touches nothing. The engagement must already be in the store or the constructor refuses by name. The JSON cache file that used to sit in the engagement folder is never read; RETIRED_CACHE_FILENAME survives only for the filer's tidy-up, which removes it. THE STEP-0 RE-RUN'S FINDING: decision 105 had kept a two-form split's second verdict in the cache alone, so a rebuilt store read the second copy the ordinary way and failed it - the cache was carrying a decision, not a derivation. own_forms(text) is now the one reading of which forms a page counts as its own (the set of self-named forms when MULTI_FORM_FAMILIES or more families print their own name, else None; the constant moved here from the router, which re-exports it for one release); _check_uncached() reads through it, so the scan's miss verdict is the router's kept verdict for every page, split included, and a delete-and-rebuild leaves every status byte-identical. _evidence_from_json() takes a tuple as well as a list, so a verdict read back in the pass that kept it carries its evidence. Decision 55: contains_keyword() treats a hyphen-joined form variant as part of the form's name (1098 never matches 1098-T); a verdict that is the machine's (no OCR, OCR failed) is transient and never cached. Decision 57: FORM_VARIANTS is the one list of each form's real variants; _JOINER is what may sit between a number and its variant or a keyword's words; the text-layer floor is per page; CACHE_VERSION 3. Decision 60: _seams() lets a keyword typed w2 find W-2; no letters or digits means no keyword. Decision 62: says() is contains_keyword() as content evidence - a form number counts only within TITLE_CHARS; _seams() reads plurals, keeps numbers out of amounts, takes any apostrophe. Decision 63: dominant_forms() - a form number counts in the text when it is in the title or is the number the document mentions most; form <anything> is a form number. Decision 64: dominant_forms() weighs a mention by its shape - a form names itself with its year or revision and another form in a sentence. Decision 66: the title is weighed the same way (_title_forms(); _REFERENCE_BEFORE marks a form quoted after attach/forms/see/of/on/and/or), a number outside FORM_VARIANTS is a mention only after Form, a keyword's words sit on one line or wrap as a heading from a line's start (_WRAPPING_JOINER, _LINE_START), a sheet's cells are tab-separated within a row; CACHE_VERSION 5. Decision 67: what comes before a form is read before what follows it (attach Form 1098 (2025) is a reference); a title naming _LIST_OF_FORMS or more forms names none; the title window is measured on the lower-cased text; _LINE_START admits a bullet, a pipe or a rule. Decision 68: _LIST_OF_FORMS counts families (_FAMILY), so a consolidated 1099 is one family's document; _REFERENCE_BEFORE stays on one line. Decision 69: a form number set off by a dash is a reference (_REFERENCE_AFTER), a dash before the year is still dated (_SELF_AFTER), and _REFERENCE_BEFORE reads across a line break again. Decision 73: says() weighs where a plain keyword is said, not only that it is there - an occurrence that is a menu line's title (_menu_tails: a form number and the title a dash or a comma sets off from it are one reference) or what an ask-word asked for (_asked_for: attach, provide, send, see and their kin, governing the rest of their own sentence and the line a request wraps on to) is the page talking about a document rather than being one, and one occurrence that is neither is enough. A dash-set-off form that heads its line with a year beside it, where the title window holds no second such line and no ask precedes it, names itself (_titles_its_own_line), so a payer's substitute form is not read as a checklist. A form number after a comma continues a list (_LIST_CONTINUES), and enclosed/enclosure/enclosures/re: join _REFERENCE_BEFORE, which now reads a colon between the word and the form. any_keyword_matched() answers the router's question 'did this row's keywords match, apart from the year?'. CACHE_VERSION 6. Decision 82: a verdict keeps the evidence behind it. Evidence(rule, term, where, page) is the one shape - EVIDENCE_RULES (required, any, date, filename, refused) and EVIDENCE_PLACES (title, first_page, footer, deep) are the named values, imported by the router, the index and the app's vocabulary and retyped nowhere. The Evidence record, those two lists and the cell format that format_evidence() writes and parse_evidence() reads now live in tracker/records.py (decision 100) and are re-exported here for one release; what stays here is the reading of a document that produces them. says() became a thin wrapper over _says_where(), which reaches the same verdict by the same reading and also says where the word was found (_where_said(): the title window first, then a page's last _FOOTER_LINES non-blank lines, then the rest of page 1, then deep), so no placement moved. evaluate_rules() puts an Evidence per matched rule on ContentResult.evidence, on a failing verdict too, and the reason sentence is untouched; the date rule records the row's Period, not the regex it derives and not a word of the document. format_evidence()/parse_evidence() are the one owner of the index cell's compact form (term@where:page rule, candidates joined by '; '), and the page is left off when it is 0. CACHE_VERSION 7, because a version-6 verdict read back would claim a verdict with no reason behind it. Decision 85: a form heading its own line with its printed title after its number and its year after the title names itself, at the weight a bare number-then-year mention carries - _names_itself() is the one predicate, and it holds both shapes a printed title wears (a dash between number and title, decision 69/73's; or nothing between them, _SELF_TITLED). The IRS's 2024 and 2025 W-2 revisions print one copy to the page, so Copy B's only "W-2" is the foot's "W-2 Wage and Tax Statement 2025 Department of the Treasury" and the form said nothing about itself before this. The year must be a year and not a date's tail ("Form 941 04/30/2025" on a CP 575 is a filing deadline), and a page heading two such lines is a menu, as it is for the dashed shape - _lists_forms() counts both. CACHE_VERSION 8, because a cached verdict from before it would say a one-copy W-2 is nobody's form. Decision 90: a keyword may name alternatives and join the phrases one of them wants together, read through manifest.keyword_alternatives() - says() takes the first alternative whose every phrase is said and places the evidence at its leading phrase, contains_keyword() reads a file name the same way, and a keyword holding neither character is one phrase exactly as before. CACHE_VERSION 9, because a verdict cached before it read the '|' and the '+' as words to look for. Decision 109: ContentCache.digest_of() is now the one memo for every hash of a file under Prepared/ - the filer's sweep and its proof of each copy it makes, a person's filing as the scan reads it, and the scan's own de-duplication - so a second and a third pass over an unchanged tree cost stats rather than reads. Nothing under the tree a client is shared is ever memo'd: decision 68 reads every preserved original each pass by design, and that is the one reading the measure allows. The scan's prune() now keeps every file under Prepared/, so a parked copy's memo and a stray's survive the pass that learned them. DECISION 127 - PHOTOS, AND THE PAGE UPRIGHT: extract_text() returns None for an IMAGE_EXTENSIONS file on purpose (an image never has a text layer) and extract() reads that as 'this is a scan' rather than 'no extractor', so a photo takes the scanned-PDF path exactly - needs_ocr with ocr=False, extract_by_ocr() otherwise, which dispatches _ocr_pdf for a PDF and _ocr_image for a photo. _ocr_image() undoes the phone's EXIF rotation first (ImageOps.exif_transpose), then reads. (Decision 127 turned every page upright with Tesseract's OSD and a four-way score; decision 169 removed both with Tesseract - see below.) The file on disk is never touched, because a photo is an original. CACHE_VERSION 10, because a verdict reached at 9 may have been reached on a page nobody turned. Extraction.seconds carries how long each reading took (extract() times _extract() and stamps it), which decides nothing - no reading is capped, timed out or abandoned; the router carries it into the pass. reasons.NO_TEXT_LAYER now says 'PDF or photo'. Decision 137: extract() never opens a file past validators.MAX_READ_MB (reasons.TOO_LARGE, a kept verdict); a .csv/.tsv/.txt is read to validators.TEXT_READ_CAP_MB and Extraction.cut says so, and a failing verdict on a cut text ends with reasons.TEXT_CUT. OCR renders each PDF page at render_scale() - min(RENDER_SCALE, sqrt(PIXEL_BUDGET / page area)) - so no page passes 40 Mpx, and a photo is held to the same budget before decoding (JPEG draft, else reduced on decode; Pillow's guard stays on). A Date Pattern is compiled and run line by line (date_pattern_at), lines over DATE_LINE_MAX skipped, bounding a backtracking typo. A picture past Pillow's own decompression-bomb limit raises TooLargeToRead and is a kept reasons.TOO_LARGE verdict, not a retry. Decision 137 Part B (B1.2): the safety stop - READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS (60) and READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS (600), a photo one page - is a _SafetyStop set for each extract_by_ocr() reading; since decision 169 (ruling 5) no page starts past it (_SafetyStop.page() checks before each page), a PDF page's render counts against it, and ReadingStopped becomes a kept reasons.READING_STOPPED verdict, not retried until the file changes. _clock is named so the suite moves it. Review fix (F7): a Period-derived date pattern runs over the whole text as before; only a staff pattern runs line by line. Part B review fixes: the stop's sentence says '1 minute'; extract()'s docstring states what the stop covers in-process (between pages) and what only the child's end covers (a page being read, the text layer, one render). DECISION 150 - A READING RUNS WHERE IT CAN BE STOPPED: extract_bounded() is what the pass reads through (router.read_once and _check_uncached); it runs open_and_read() - validators.open_test() (tier 2's open test) then extract() - in a spawned child (_read_in_a_child, the child itself in tracker/ocr.py since decision 169, over multiprocessing's Pipe: a named pipe on Windows, never a socket) and waits at most reading_stop_seconds() - READING_STOP_DOCUMENT_SECONDS for a file, READING_STOP_PAGE_SECONDS for a photo. On time the child's Extraction is returned as is; over time _end() ends the child's whole tree (taskkill /T on Windows, the child's own process group elsewhere) and the reading is abandoned() - the same kept READING_STOPPED verdict B1.2 gives; a child that ends without answering, or whose reader raised, is reading_failed() - reasons.READING_CRASHED, firm-side, kept. B1.2 stays inside the child. The child writes nothing; since decision 169 neither does the reader (no temporary file), so ocr_scratch is gone. READ_IN_A_CHILD is True in the tracker and turned off for the suite by tests/conftest.py (its fakes live in the test's process); _CHILD_READER is what the child runs, open_and_read() by default, so tests/child_readers.py can hand the child a reader that blocks or dies. A cached verdict never starts a child; the benchmark and the CLI call extract() directly. The child never outlives its pass (the designer's ruling on the build): its lifeline and its job object moved with it to tracker/ocr.py in decision 169, which says how. The review's ruling: the open test's verdict rides back as Extraction.opened; the router hands it to every row's check_file(open_test=...) and keeps it under OPEN_TEST_FINGERPRINT by digest; the scanner's check_files asks open_verdict(), which answers from that kept verdict or reads the file in a child and holds the reading in memory (ContentCache.hold_reading, never saved) for the content check that follows; HEIC_NOT_SUPPORTED is the machine's and not kept. The child says 'started' before it touches the file: no word before the stop, an end before it, or a Process that cannot start is could_not_start() - reasons.READER_UNAVAILABLE, transient, nothing kept - and readers_that_could_not_start() is what the runner's pass (and the app's Run now) turns into one warning. Decision 141: FIRST_PAGE_PHRASES (a notice's header phrases - notice date, tax year, tax period, irs, internal revenue service) count only when first said on page 1, so a bill whose back page talks about a notice is not one; only the catalog's notices row uses them. CACHE_VERSION 11. Decision 154: in_a_child(path, job, stop=..., **kwargs) is the one child mechanism, and _read_in_a_child() is the reading's use of it; it gives (answer, None) on time or (None, the Extraction that says why - abandoned(), reading_failed() or could_not_start()), so the opening of an email or a zip (containers.open_bounded) runs in the same child, under the same stop, lifeline and job object. Since decision 169 it hands the job to tracker.ocr.run_in_child() - the pass's one long-lived child - and words the ocr.Outcome it gets back; it no longer makes a process of its own. Decision 155 added ContentCache.remember_digest(): a digest proved on a working copy's temp is remembered for the copy's name after the rename (same size, same modification time), so the proof is still one read. DECISION 169 - RAPIDOCR IS THE READER: _ocr_pdf() renders each page at render_scale() and hands it, in RGB, to ocr.read_page(); _ocr_image() hands the EXIF-upright photo the same way. Nothing turns a page (ruling 6 as re-ruled: RapidOCR keeps a sideways page's words; the turning rule arrives in ocr._upright_lines() as the amendment '169, upright'). ocr.ReaderUnavailable - a model missing or broken - is None from the reader, so reasons.NO_TEXT_LAYER, transient, now worded 'the reader could not run on this machine'. The pages are still joined with a line break, never PAGE_BREAK (SPEC-127.2X D9.2). pytesseract, _tesseract, _upright, _four_way, _score_of, _for_scoring and their constants are gone, and ocr_scratch with them (the reader writes no temporary file - SPEC-169 section 6). CACHE_VERSION 12: every verdict on a scan or a photo was the old reader's. Decision 178: a reading is bounded in what it hands back, whatever it reads. READING_CHAR_BUDGET (TEXT_READ_CAP_MB counted in characters) bounds every reading - the workbook and PDF readers stop at it, _extract cuts past it and marks the reading cut. PACKINGS (stored, deflated) is the only zip packing a reading unpacks: a workbook packed otherwise fails with UnknownPacking (a ValueError of its own, raised with UNKNOWN_PACKING, decision 190), and containers refuses such a zip. _line_of finds a line's ends by the nearest break of any kind - forward by one search, back over a window that doubles until it meets a break, and a mention on the line last found reuses it - linear where it was quadratic. Decision 190: EXTRACTION_FAILED and OCR_FAILED hold the class only (OcrError carries the class as its one argument, read by OcrError.error), Extraction.error is the class or the firm's sentence for a child that ended, and in_a_child() hands a failed child's message and trace to errors.keep(), never to a log line. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 A-F9): _clock, the child's _SafetyStop clock, is ocr.awake_clock, so time the machine slept is never counted against a reading. Decision 189 (the judgment worker): the reader child judges as well as reads. judge(path, questions) makes the open test and the reading, then answers every question the pass asks: each row's verdict (evaluate_rules with own_forms, which is also decision 94's split), both router leads (required_matched, any_keyword_matched), self_named_forms, own_forms, carries_a_1099b_section, and the name check (names.check_name, reached at call time). It hands back a Judgment that carries no word of the document. The pass calls judge_bounded (in the child, or in-process when READ_IN_A_CHILD is off). judgment_of is the pure judgment for callers that already hold an Extraction (the backtest, via route_file(reading=...)). The answers are the pre-189 values call for call, so CACHE_VERSION did not move (claim 3.g). Rows are keyed by RowQuestion (the five rule fields), not the rules fingerprint, which omits period and date_pattern_derived; the cache still keys by fingerprint. dominant_forms and self_named_forms run once per judgment. OCR text is cut to READING_CHAR_BUDGET. ContentCache holds Judgments, not texts. Judgment.extraction.transient is the SPEC-156 seam. extract_bounded remains for callers that want the words; the pass does not call it. Decision 189 (ruling 2.2, the integration): ContentCache.deadline carries the household's deadline while the sort or the scan takes files, and before_a_judgment() raises OutOfTime at the cache-miss point, just before a judgment job would start (open_verdict, _check_uncached, and the filer's two read_once calls) - never at a hit, so a household past its time still takes every kept verdict. Runtime: no new artifact. Decision 187's review (M2): a Date Pattern runs over the whole text only when it equals manifest.derived_date_pattern(item.period), recomputed; the record's date_pattern_derived flag is a claim, and anything else runs line by line through date_pattern_at. Decision 190: ContentResult and Extraction carry code, set where each Reason is said; open_verdict returns a Said and keeps the code in the cache; CACHE_VERSION 13. P216 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): ContentCache._key is str(settings.resolved(file.parent) / file.name).lower() - the held answer for the folder and the file's own name, the same string a whole resolve gives - and the whole resolve for a link. The reader is untouched.

A command line on a machine with no saved root reads the root off the typed path's position (four levels up for a return, two for a household) and holds it to the same rule; relative paths are the caller's to make absolute (from the working folder at a shell, from the root in the API). Which household is this, and may this path exist: layout; the guard is tests/test_layers.py::test_no_under_the_root_decision_survives_outside_the_layout. - **`tracker/errors.py`** — What an error is called where a person can see it (decision 190): error_class(exc) is the class, and for an OSError its errno's symbolic name (FileNotFoundError (ENOENT)), or for a class that sets SAYS_ITS_CODE (decision 189's StoreUnavailable, RecordNotWritten) its code, never the message and never a path - the one definition of how an error is said, which decision 189 first wrote as content_check.said_as_class; said(exc, firm_written) keeps the tracker's own sentences whole; keep(where, exc_or_text, name=) writes the whole message and trace to the debug logger DEBUG_LOGGER ('tracker.debug') at WARNING, which propagates to 'tracker', so the words land in decision 193's one local debug log while settings.error_log holds it; in a reading child keep_for_the_parent() collects instead and take_kept() hands them to the pass; console() is the one root console, with the debug logger filtered off it.   - note: Layer 0, standard library only, nothing of the package. A class name and not a shortened message because 120 characters is an SSN: no length is short enough to be safe, and a class name is written by a programmer. Every reason's {error}, the router's 'could not read it', the filer's and runner's catch-alls and the app's unexpected error name the class; the record's own errors (ManifestError, StoreError and the others) keep their text. Part 4 (decision 190): the logger propagates to 'tracker', so inside settings.error_log('tracker') a kept message lands in tracker-errors.log beside the store in the data home, and keeps a NullHandler, so with no log attached Python's last-resort handler prints nothing; a hand-run scan's console comes from errors.console(), which filters it off, and nothing ever reaches runs.log. A reading child keeps nothing itself: its keeps travel back in ocr.Outcome.kept (at most KEPT_PER_ANSWER, then a count) and ocr.Session keeps each. tests/test_errors.py fails if any module but settings attaches a file handler, imports logging.handlers or names a log file (runner's runs.log named with its reason), and if any basicConfig, any StreamHandler or a handler on the root logger appears under tracker/ outside errors.console() (the landing review's SF2). tests/test_errors.py guards that no module under tracker/ puts a caught exception's words beside its class or into a reason's {error}, with the record-side exceptions named once. said(exc, firm_written) is the one rule for a row or a page that may name either kind: the caller's own errors (the filer's FIRM_WRITTEN, the runner's and rollover's ManifestError) whole, anything else by its class (the review's M1 and S3). It also fails on a class spelled inline - x.__class__.__name__, type(x).__name__ or x.__name__ of an exception an except bound - anywhere under tracker/ but errors.py, so an OSError is never said twice, once without its errno (the rebase review's M1). And it fails any log line under tracker/ that carries a caught exception's words, a traceback, exc_info or log.exception: under the scheduled job no handler is configured and Python's last-resort handler prints every warning to the console window (D-6), so a log line says errors.error_class() and the firm's own words, and the words (and a client's file name) go to keep(); content_check's two ReaderUnavailable lines, the machine's words, are the named exceptions. Landed on 159: the checkpoint's CheckpointUnavailable sets says_its_code, so error_class says it with its engine code; locking, ledger and store import errors at call time only (their layer rules), and test_errors.FIRM_WRITTEN names CheckpointError, CheckpointUnavailable and RolledNotAllRetired as the firm's own sentences.
- **`tracker/filer.py`** — Sorts the household's one inbox across every return of its open year (decision 125): moves each original out of it into the client's folder for the year, untouched, copies a renamed working file into Prepared/... or 00 - Needs Review, and records every move in the engagement's own record - the journal and the store together, in one transaction per decision. Owns read_index(), which answers from the store, and ensure(), which brings the store up to the journal and says whether it is current. Decision 130: received_for() reads each return's index and request list once and returns what the client README acknowledges as plain data (Filed/File Moved = Received once per request satisfied, by request label - an also-filed copy names a request only by its exact folder name or identifier + LABEL_SEPARATOR, else Other document; Needs Review = Under Review, counted by day; nothing else shown), and refresh_household_readme() - the one call the pass, the rollover and every app action make - reads scaffold.readme_returns() once for both received_for() and scaffold.write_readme(), under a per-household README lock (README_LOCK_FILENAME in the private household folder; busy past README_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = skip with a log line), and never raises. Since decision 128 the pass also asks whose each document is, between the request lists' acceptances and the exactly-one rule.
