  - note: Content-hash de-duplication makes re-runs no-ops. _sort_one() decides one preserved original's fate against a _SortContext built once per run (the request list, the index so far, folders, claimed names, the run's caches). The verdicts the router reaches while sorting are written to the engagement's verdicts in the store (content_check.ContentCache over store.remember_verdicts(), keyed by content; decision 107), so the scan that follows finds them under the working copy's name and never reads the document twice; a dry run saves nothing. The tidy-up at the end of a real pass also removes the retired JSON cache file and any temp file beside it (_remove_the_retired_cache(), by RETIRED_CACHE_FILENAME) - nothing reads it, and the removal is said once on FileReport.attention (RETIRED_CACHE_REMOVED) - on the console, in the app's warnings and counted on the practice page - for that pass only. Originals are moved byte for byte under their own names and never altered. Each drop is handled on its own: a drop that cannot be moved is left in place for the next run, a drop that fails after it was preserved is recorded as Needs Review with the error, and the record is written in a finally block so nothing moved into the year's folder is ever unrecorded. Runs under the engagement lock - its own when it is called alone, the pass's when runner.run_engagement() is holding one - taken before the request list, the record or the drop folder is read. Files the client drops straight into the visible year folder are filed and indexed in place; a re-sent document whose working copy vanished from Prepared/ is re-filed rather than called a duplicate; a Document renamed in the editor keeps its earlier copies, found by identifier (assign_files), and names the next by its new short name; empty client folders are cleared after sorting. assign_review_file() is the person's counterpart to file_household_drops(): moves the parked copy under the canonical name (or copies from the client's folder for the year if it is gone), rewrites the index row as Filed with the ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON reason, records the keyword a person typed in the same call, all under the engagement lock. The IndexEntry record and INDEX_LAYOUT live in tracker/records.py (decision 100). HISTORY, kept as history: until decision 102 the index was a workbook rewritten whole on every pass, and decisions 54, 56, 58, 59, 61, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69 and 72 are thirteen readings of what that cost - a snapshot sidecar that outlived its workbook, a deferred write, a stale workbook, a header row a sort had moved, a renamed tab, a column inserted at A; what survives of them here is the reading of bytes (replaced_in_pbc() decides by bytes alone; _copy_whole() leaves no half-written copy; every move is a rename in _move_whole(), because shutil.move copied a held-open drop truncated into the year's folder; what lies behind a junction is not a drop; a name Windows cannot open is reported every pass; a row recorded without its bytes is tied to them only while its working copy and its original agree, UNTIED_IN_PBC; a recorded original that has left the year's folder is said every pass, MISSING_IN_PBC, and where a stray carries its bytes the row follows the file, MOVED_IN_PBC; REPLACED_IN_PBC and UNTIED_IN_PBC are FileReport.attention, not errors; a parked path a later row records is the later row's; assign reuses an earlier attempt's copy first and leaves an annotated parked copy, saying so). Decision 76: dismiss_review_file() rewrites a parked row NOT_REQUESTED with the DISMISSED_BY_PERSON reason and moves nothing; _find_parked() takes a dismissed row too, so filing it is the undo. Decision 111: a re-send is judged by the earlier row's decision - the content hash says which row holds those bytes and that row's decision says what this drop is. A filed row with its copy in place, a row parked for a person, and a row whose copy is not where the record put it all make it a Duplicate, and the sentence names which (DUPLICATE_OF_FILED, DUPLICATE_OF_PARKED, DUPLICATE_OF_MOVED, and DUPLICATE_OF_UNCOPIED of a row with no working copy to name: saying 'already filed as' of a parked copy told the Index a document still waiting was done); a filed row whose copy is gone is decision 24's re-file; a row a person set aside is routed like any other drop - Not requested is a decision about one document on one day, not a standing rule - and files where exactly one request now accepts it, else parks with a FRESH copy of its own (never _existing_copy, or filing one row would carry the other row's file away), the reason quoting the earlier decision whole (RESENT_AFTER_SET_ASIDE) so the row is triaged, counted by reminder.count_needs_review() and read by a person. Decision 77: unfile_document() is the way back - the working copy returns to 00 - Needs Review under the client's own name, the row is rewritten NEEDS_REVIEW with the UNFILED_BY_PERSON reason, and the engagement is re-scanned (outside the lock, which the scan takes for itself); a working copy that is no longer the row's bytes is left and said out loud (LEFT_FILED). Decision 82: IndexEntry.evidence is the last column, written through records.format_evidence() and read back through records.parse_evidence(); a person's decision leaves it alone. Decision 87: every decision is appended to the record through tracker/ledger.py by one rule, _rows_changed(), read off the rows themselves. DECISION 102 - THE INDEX MOVED INTO THE RECORD: read_index() takes the engagement folder and reads the store's documents table, in the index's own order, after store.follow_the_journal(); _record() is the one write, every event a decision produces in a single store.record() call, and the rollback that puts a moved file back asks _the_record_holds(). The migration that read a legacy folder's index workbook into the journal once, and the request-list import of decision 103 that read the sheet once a pass and journalled its differences, both LEFT WITH DECISION 104 and are set aside outside the tree in Retired - Excel manifest: ensure() is now the store's top-up and the three words that say whether it describes the engagement, it writes nothing in the folder, and every caller drops the flag that used to keep a dry run from migrating. clients_root_of() is store.root_for() under its old name. _storable() keeps only the refusal of a name UTF-8 cannot hold (the journal is UTF-8 JSON); a control character in a POSIX name files again, because the refusal of one existed only because a workbook is XML. A person's filing records its keyword in the SAME store.record() call as the row (_record()'s also), because the filing and what it taught are one decision. THE DELIBERATE CYCLE: _rescan() imports tracker/scanner.py at call time so a person's filing is scanned the moment it lands, and the scanner imports this module's index reader at call time; neither runs at load. DECISION 112 - A PERSON'S ACTION IS JUDGED AGAINST THE RECORD IT WAS MADE ON: assign_review_file(), dismiss_review_file() and unfile_document() each take seq=, the row's sequence number as the person saw it, and _refuse_if_stale() compares it with store.document_seqs() immediately after the row is found - inside the lock, before a byte is read or a file is touched - raising StaleRowError (a FilingError, so the API's one except turns it into the app's sentence) with STALE_ROW, which names what the record now says. seq=None is a caller with no view (a script, a test) and skips the check; the by-name refusal is asked first and is a different question. assign_review_file() also takes shortlist=, the identifiers the evidence pointed at, computed by the caller that drew the card: a pick off a non-empty shortlist writes OVERRODE_SHORTLIST into the row's reason after the ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON prefix (the scanner's acceptance still keys on startswith) and comes back on AssignResult.overrode_shortlist; an empty shortlist is never an override. This module does not import tracker/review.py - that would be a second call-time cycle beside the deliberate one - which is why the shortlist is handed in. find_parked() and find_filed() are public for the same reason (the underscored names kept for one release), so the API finds exactly the row this module will act on. DECISION 109 - EVERY WORKING COPY IS PROVED AGAINST THE RECORD EACH PASS: _prove_working_copies() is one walk of Prepared/ per pass, under the pass's lock, between the PBC sweep and the known-bytes map, and it has four outcomes and only these. A copy where the record put it holding the row's digest is proved and nothing is written. A copy that is absent or holds other bytes, whose bytes turn up at a path no row names, makes its row FILE_MOVED - a decision on the document, never a Status (the owner's rule, 2026-09-19) - with home kept in prepared_location and where the bytes are now in a sentence (MOVED_SENTENCE, MOVED_GONE_SENTENCE), read back by moved_to() through records.as_pattern(); the scanner reads that row and writes the request's note. Where more than one file no row names holds those bytes, the row keeps the wanderer it already names (_spend_a_stray()'s preferred): the copy that sorts first is not the copy a person moved, and decision 110's put-it-back follows the sentence. A FILE_MOVED row whose every claimed location holds its bytes again is FILED once more (NEEDS_REVIEW where the row names no request - which of the two parked decisions it was is not guessable), MOVED_BACK_SENTENCE. A file named for a request (assign_files, decision 168) or in the review folder that no row names and no row's bytes match is UNRECORDED_COPY on FileReport.attention, every pass, counted where it sits. THE RECORD DECIDES AND NOTHING MOVES: the fingerprint identifies, a person acts (decision 110's buttons), and a quiet pass appends nothing - one ledger.COPY_MOVED event per move, in either direction, named through _LEDGER_EVENT_FOR and _record()'s decided. A row without its bytes is never swept (decision 65) but still names its copy, so that copy is not called unrecorded; a placeholder is never read; a Duplicate row is not followed. _copy_whole() now proves its target against the digest it was made from and raises CopyMismatchError - decision 17's could-not-be-filed row - rather than leaving a copy nobody checked; every caller passes what it knows, and the pass's callers pass the ContentCache too, so the memo the proof leaves is the scan's hit. DECISION 110 - RECOVERY IS THE PERSON'S: restore_working_copy() is the answer to a FILE_MOVED row that needs no other place for the file to go - the bytes return to where the record put them, by moving the wanderer moved_to() names when it still holds them and by copying from the client's original when nothing under the firm's folder does - and the row goes back to what it was before it wandered, FILED where it names a request and NEEDS_REVIEW where it does not. It never overwrites (a file already at home that is not this document stays exactly where it is; this document's copy goes to review under the client's own name and the row parks naming both, PUT_BACK_REFUSED), never deletes (a home that already holds these bytes leaves the wanderer where it is for a person to remove, PUT_BACK_ALREADY) and never guesses (the row's sequence number first, every byte it is about to move second, the move third, and a refused record puts back exactly what moved). Every location the row claims is put back, not the Prepared Location column alone: the sweep names the first location that failed, and a page decision 94 filed under several requests has a copy in each, each remade from the one just put back. One event whatever the click found, ledger.RESTORED_BY_PERSON, because the row it carries says which. The other two answers are the actions that already existed: keep-it-here is assign_review_file() on a moved row, where the copy that moves is the wanderer and the request may be the folder's own or another the person picks; send-it-to-review is unfile_document(), where the wanderer is the copy that goes back and a row whose bytes are nowhere is copied from the original. Both refuse a row with copies under several requests by name (SEVERAL_COPIES_REFUSAL) and point at put-it-back. find_parked() and find_filed() take accepting=, the decisions the action will have beyond the ones they were written for, so those two reach a FILE_MOVED row and dismiss_review_file() still refuses one by name (decision 76); find_moved() is their shape over FILE_MOVED itself. DECISION 119 - AN INTERRUPTED MOVE IS FINISHED FROM THE RECORD, NEVER GUESSED: before the first file operation of any decision - a pass's copy, a person's filing, unfiling or put-back - _intend() appends ledger.MOVING under the lock, keyed by the row's own ledger key, carrying the operations in order with the digest each end should hold, the row the decision will record, the event that will complete it, who decided and (for a drop's own move, which has no row yet) the day the run began; _do_op() is the one place a plan is carried out, by the decision and by the recovery alike, so a move a recovery makes is the move the decision would have made. _finish_interrupted_moves() runs at the start of every pass, under the lock, after the index is read and before the digests of rows recorded without them are filled in, before the client's folder is read for strays and before the sweep - so a person's half-made filing is finished and recorded as theirs rather than swept up as a copy somebody dragged. Each operation is checked by bytes and finished where reality matches; the intent's row is then recorded as the intent said, with the events that travelled with it, dated the day the person decided. Where a destination holds other bytes nothing there is touched and the row parks with reasons.INTERRUPTED_MOVE naming it (interrupted_at() and interrupted_note() read the sentence back for the scanner, as moved_to() does 109's); where neither end holds the bytes the row parks with INTERRUPTED_MOVE_LOST; either way the copy a person acts on is the one waiting in review if there is one, else a fresh one from the client's original. _refuse_if_a_move_is_open() refuses all four person actions while an intent is open here, before 112's freshness check, because the next pass - or Run now - finishes it. A refused record rolls back as it always did and appends ledger.MOVE_ABANDONED so the next pass does not finish forward a move the record would not take. RECORD_PRESERVE_INTENTS is the one switch: the pass's own move into the client's folder is already finished by decision 23, and its intent buys only the received date. _plan_working_copy() took over from the filer's old one-step copy helper: deciding where a working copy goes and making it are two steps now, because what will happen has to be written down before it does. refuse_a_path_past_the_limit() lives here since decision 126: the deepest thing a return ever holds is a working copy this module writes, and both creation (tracker.api) and the household rollover (tracker.rollover, at a layer below the API) measure it before a folder is made. The name tier (decision 128) runs inside file_household_drops: one reading per drop, then check_name() per accepting return against that return's own people. A named request keeps its acceptance only where the name confirms, an unnamed one keeps it where the name is merely absent, and any return whose page names somebody on another return of the household is dropped. What is left goes to the exactly-one rule; a list the name emptied parks in the home return with reasons.NAME_NOT_ON_PAGE, NAMES_ANOTHER_RETURN or NO_PEOPLE_ON_FILE, in that order. A filing by hand may teach one spelling, recorded as one rules_changed event inside the filing's own transaction exactly as a taught keyword is. A list the name emptied parks in the first return that ACCEPTED the document (decision 125's home), the first return by folder order only where nothing accepted it at all. Both of decision 111's re-send roads - a row a person set aside, a filed row whose working copy is gone - are name-checked the same way inside _sort_one() before they file, or the check could be walked round by sending a document twice. Decision 129 widened the sort from the household's own returns to its feed list, and decision 132 re-specified it: file_household_drops(inbox, originals, own=, fed=) takes the two lists by name, judges own returns first (the bytes are asked of the records in that order - the record closest to the drop decides - while the locks were taken in the global one), a document nobody may file always parks in a home return (_the_home), and every filing goes through _file_into() - ONE SHAPE FOR THE PASS AND A PERSON: one intent in the TARGET's record, keyed on the row's final location, ops [move original -> resting] (only where the household differs, which since decision 204 is only a person's hand-over) + [copy resting -> each working copy], then the row (FILED for the pass, ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON for a person) and its also events; nothing ever writes into another return's record. DECISION 204 (revising 132): THE PASS NEVER FILES ACROSS HOUSEHOLDS, on a first arrival or a re-send (_decide_across and _sort_one alike). A document only a return in another household is left with parks at home: OPENED_NOT_ACROSS (an attachment), UNNAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS (names nobody; the picker), or NAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS (names that return's person; _NameStage.spelling keeps the firm's matched spelling for the reason, _named_across) with the row's waits_for cell (_waits_for: records.format_waits_for of the return's household and name, routing.filed_to and the Also Answers, each filtered to that list as _file_it filters them). _ReturnRun.dropped_in, _rests_at's second move and runner.FILED_INTO_FED are gone; _file_it's original rests where the inbox move left it. hand_over(also=, answers=, waiting=) is the only road across: requests_taking() is the one list-and-N/A check (the API's card offer uses it too), one copy per request (decision 94) and the filtered answers cell (146) on the taking row, waits_for cleared; waiting=True is the one click - under both locks, after the seq check, _refuse_unless_it_waits_for() refuses (NOT_WAITING or a claim mismatch) unless the row is still NEEDS_REVIEW with NAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS and its claim names the target by waiting_target() (layout.name_key on household and return, decision 188) and exactly these requests and answers. hand_over() is two intents in two records, each finished by its own household's pass with no lock it does not hold: the home's release intent first (remove the parked copy, then ledger.RELEASED with RELEASED_TO as its reason - the row leaves the index, the dropping household keeps no row), then the taking return's filing through _file_into(), its row, the home's remove and the release. A kill after the release intent alone costs the person's click (the original, named by no row, is a stray re-sorted where it lies). A PASS LEAVES ALONE AN ORIGINAL ANOTHER RECORD'S OPEN INTENT NAMES (the lead's ruling R-1): _named_by_another_records_intent() - asked only when a stray is found - reads every return of the practice (positionally, each followed to its journal first, no lock) for an open intent naming that path with those bytes as a step's source, and such a file is never re-sorted, parked or recorded - but it is said, LEFT_FOR_ANOTHER_RETURN on the first own return's attention every pass it happens (ruling R-3), so an intent that never finishes never leaves an original unmentioned; so the taking return's recovery always finishes the move and each half of a hand-over is finished by its own household's pass. _decide_across() records a reading's seconds on first (the first own return, the run the inbox's own notes ride - SPEC-127.1 9.2). Decision 127: FileReport.slowest holds the run's SLOWEST_READINGS longest readings as (name, seconds), recorded by FileReport.timed() off Routing.seconds after each drop is routed - after the fact, so nothing is ever cut short for being slow. Decision 131: THE ROOM A RETURN HAS - room_for(engagement_dir, items) -> Room(need, least, floor, parks, short, limit), from the list alone (no disk, no store, no lock): need is creation's figure (refuse_a_path_past_the_limit is now need > MAX_PATH_LENGTH), least the deepest path at shortest_name_for() (identifier, period, ' (99)', extension), floor the review folder plus 'x (99).<ext>', parks the rows whose shortest name passes their extension's limit, short how far the deepest canonical copy passes the limit for ITS extension (layout.limit_for). prepared_name_for(..., room=) CUTS THE DOCUMENT PART to fit the room the exact destination folder leaves - identifier, period, numbered suffix and extension never cut, the suffix counted in the same loop - and raises NoRoom (a FilingError whose sentence is PATH_NO_ROOM) when not even the shortest form fits; room=None is the canonical name exactly. _plan_working_copy, a person's filing and hand_over pass a room; the pass parks a NoRoom document with PATH_NO_ROOM (the last reason the filing branch gives; the request that accepted it is its candidate), a person is refused with it and nothing moves. _unique_path(..., room=) cuts a review copy's stem the same way (_review_copy_path: a reader's limit never stops a park - it falls back to Windows's, which the pass's floor has proved); original_name stays the client's whole name; an original is never cut. The sentences HOUSEHOLD_NO_ROOM, ROOM_SHORT and ROOM_PARKS live here beside PATH_NO_ROOM. THE REVIEW'S FIXES: every sentence names the limit as that kind of copy's ('the 218 characters a .xlsx copy may have'), never 'Windows allows'; PATH_NO_ROOM_IN names a fed return by label when its request has no room and the document parks at home; EVERY review copy - _park_it, the recovery's _a_copy_to_act_on, unfile_document, restore_working_copy's refused put-back - is named through _review_copy_path(review_dir, name) -> (path, note), whose note is REVIEW_COPY_PAST_READER when a workbook's copy was fitted to 260 past a reader's 218; _unique_path(room=) cuts a name whose suffix is not an extension as one stem, and below one character raises NoRoom with REVIEW_NO_ROOM (never a request's label); _a_copy_to_act_on returns (location, sentence) and a copy it cannot make leaves the row naming NO copy; _plan_working_copy and assign_review_file find an existing copy by its bytes BEFORE measuring a name; no request folder is made until every copy of a filing is named (_do_op makes the parent); _stem_of's cap cuts the label, never the period. Decision 137 (L2): _move_whole() takes the folder its walk started from (within=) and asks the link question again of every folder from the source up to it immediately before os.rename; a link anywhere raises MovedThroughALinkError (an OSError, so every caller already says "left in place"). Decision 137 Part B (M2): _decide_across() filed into a return in another household (_across_households, against the dropping household's own first run) only when the name tier CONFIRMED the page (decision 204 closed that road too: a confirmed page parks with NAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS); a document kept only because its request is unnamed parks at home with reasons.UNNAMED_ACROSS_HOUSEHOLDS. Within one household decision 128's table is unchanged, and a person's own filing across (File it) is untouched. Review fix (F5): the link check (door.through_a_link since decision 188) judges only the folders between its root and the path, and refuses a path that is not under the root. Part B review fixes: _across_households() reads run.home (the dropping household's own), never a fallback run; a B2 park's Evidence names the return and request that wanted it (_with_the_wanting_return, keyed '<label> / <identifier>'); _sort_one() returns the run its row goes into, and an unnamed re-send a return in another household already holds parks at home with the same sentence. Decision 150 (the designer's ruling on the re-review): _not_read(reading) - a reader that could not start (reasons.READER_UNAVAILABLE, transient) - makes _decide_across() and _sort_one() return None, and _sort_all() records nothing for that drop: no index row, no Needs Review row, nothing kept. A drop already moved rests in the year's folder with no row, so the next pass reads it again as a stray (the shape of unfinished_drops); the pass's one READER_COULD_NOT_START warning is its only trace. A machine's fault leaves nothing permanent. Decision 143: _sort_all() opens an email or a zip after its move and fingerprint and before the decision (_open_container): the container is recorded OPENED in the first own return, its journal line (ledger.OPENED) carrying each attachment and each part skipped (the run's opened map, merged into the event by _rows_changed's extra); each attachment is written atomically under layout.opened_dir_of() by _take_out() (reused by bytes after a kill, numbered past other bytes, cut to fit) before the container's row exists, then decided by _decide_attachment() through _decide_across() with _SortContext.container set so every row it writes, and the intent before it, names the container. The first own return is recorded last, so a kill between two returns' transactions leaves the container a stray to reopen. An attachment never files into, or writes a row in, another household (_decide_across parks it at home with reasons.OPENED_NOT_ACROSS, and asks only the returns _may_hold() allows whether they hold its bytes, so no Duplicate row reaches another household's record - the review's B1; hand_over refuses it). replaced_in_pbc() is asked of _Opened as well as the year's folder (the review's B2). _unaccounted_in_opened() says every pass what sits under _Opened that no row names. FileReport.opened lists the containers; DUPLICATE_OF_OPENED is a re-sent one. Decision 150 over 143 (the restack): an attachment is read through _decide_across and so in 150's child; one whose reader could not start gets no row (_decide_attachment returns False), and then neither does its container - its opened entry is withdrawn and its folder put in _ReturnRun.reopen, so _unaccounted_in_opened says nothing of it - and the next pass reopens the container as a stray, reuses each file by its bytes, skips each attachment a row names and reads the one that waited. Decision 144: _parts_of() reads RequestItem.short_name, so prepared_name_for() and shortest_name_for() name a copy <identifier> - <short> - <period>, 131's cut cuts the short name first, and room_for() measures the short names - under the firm's own 35-character root none of the owner's 39 intake returns is refused. Decision 155: _copy_whole() is fsio.copy_atomically() with the digest proved on the temp before the swap (CopyMismatchError, decision 17's could-not-be-filed row), and the proved digest handed to ContentCache.remember_digest() so the proof still costs one read; a killed or failed copy leaves only its temp, never a file under the working copy's name, and the copy is writable. sweep_stranded_temps(household, returns, started) is called by runner.run_household under every return's lock before anything is read: it removes the tracker's own temps (fsio.TEMP_NAME's exact shape, born before the pass, left by this process or one locking.pid_alive() says is gone) under each return's folder, under the household-year's _Opened and beside the README in the inbox under the README's lock, never a path any row of these returns names (a parked copy keeps the client's name, an attachment its own) and never through a link (fsio.is_link, which replaced the filer's own _is_link and _LINK_TAGS) - never in a client year folder, never a client's .tmp - and never raises. UNRECORDED_COPY's advice no longer assumes a client's document (audit E8) and never sends one to a client's folder (decision 184): confirm whose it is, then the app or a firm-side folder a person controls; anything else is deleted by hand. Decision 160: received_for() joins a filed row to its request without case (identifier_key) and labels it in the list's spelling, so a respelling by case reads received in the README as in the letter. documents_by_request() counts Filed and File Moved rows per request from the index. rename_request() gives a request another identifier in one act in decision 119's shape: checks under the lock (open intents, the list's version, the list's validation, every copy there with its bytes, no destination taken, path length), then one store.record of the renaming events and one MOVING intent per changed row (then renamed_by_person), then the moves, then the rows; a failed move after the write is finished forward by the next pass (RENAME_UNFINISHED). Case-only, File Moved copies and taken destinations are refused. DECISION 168: every copy is written to Prepared/<name> - the request-folder lookup is gone, prepared_location() says Prepared/<name> for a copy in Prepared itself - and copies_of() narrows _existing_copy() to one request's own copies, so decision 94's page is never reused across requests; room_for() measures Prepared/<name>; _request_of_copy() reads an also-filed copy's request from its own name; the sweep says an unrecorded file named for a request or in the review folder, and a person's folder is the scanner's to name, once. The rename moves copies only, in place, and there is no emptied request folder to remove; an intent written before 168 names folder-shaped paths and is finished as written. A working copy's number takes Prepared's own names, and the Prepared names an open intent will write to (decision 147's context.intended), as taken. Decision 147: iter_drops() returns the inbox in its own order (_inbox_order: the top level first, then each subfolder in case-folded name order, a folder's own files before its subfolders'), so of two files of one name the top-level one keeps it; a drop from a subfolder carries CAME_FROM_SUBFOLDER (the path below the inbox, backslashed) at the end of whichever row it gets, through _SortContext.came_from, set around the drop's decision like container and cleared around each attachment's (the inbox move writes no intent, so a kill between the move and the row loses the sentence - the accepted limit). _unique_path() is the one numbering function - the inbox move, hand_over(), review copies and _take_out() all call it (the pass's second move, _rests_at, went with decision 204) - and a name is taken when the disk holds it or a row of the household-year names it (_on_record(), the union unrecorded_in_pbc() reads against; _year_on_record() reads every return of the household-year, the pass's in hand and any return the pass left out (an inactive one; the review's N-1) from its record - the inbox move and _take_out through _taken_in_the_year() and hand_over() directly), or an open intent of the pass will write to it (_SortContext.intended, from _spoken_for_by_an_open_intent(ends=TO), joined by _taken_names()), unless the incoming bytes are that row's own (audit F-1): a different document never lands on a name a deleted original left, so it never becomes that row's next version. DECISION 157 - A MISSING WORKING COPY IS MADE AGAIN, NEVER ASKED FOR AGAIN: the sweep (_prove_working_copies) no longer skips a row whose copy is gone with its bytes nowhere (what was 'decision 3's regression'). For a Filed or parked row, and a File Moved row that already says nowhere whose every claimed place is simply gone (_may_be_made_again), each absent place is made again from the row's original, read in the moment and proved against the row's digest (_the_original_now: proved; unread - a placeholder or a read refused, and nothing is written; gone - absent or other bytes), through _make_again - an intent (then=ledger.COPY_REMADE) and decision 155's whole copy, all or nothing (_take_back and _abandon on a failure, REMAKE_FAILED said) - the row gaining REMADE_SENTENCE (a File Moved row goes back to Filed or Needs Review, _remade) and the pass one attention line; the request's status does not move. Where the original is gone too the row is FILE_MOVED with BOTH_GONE_SENTENCE, said once (both_gone() reads it, behind any person's marks; _moved_part splits a Reason round its moved sentence). A File Moved row whose wanderer vanishes is said nowhere first (MOVED_GONE_SENTENCE, or BOTH_GONE_SENTENCE where the original is absent) and is made again the pass after. Mark missing (mark_missing_again) accepts a row's own identifier on a both_gone() row only: the row keeps its decision and gains MARKED_MISSING, its prepared_location, also_filed and answers come off (marked_missing() is that shape), one answer_withdrawn_by_person line; such a row claims nothing, is left out of _missing_positions (no MISSING_IN_PBC, never followed), received_for and documents_by_request (_counts_as_received), and a re-send of its bytes - or of a both_gone() row's - is re-filed (REFILED_AFTER_GONE). restore_working_copy() dispatches: a FILE_MOVED row to _put_back_a_moved_copy (decision 110, unchanged, but a nowhere row whose original is gone refuses with NOTHING_TO_PUT_BACK), a Filed or parked row with a gone copy (_find_to_put_back, _gone_copies) to _make_a_gone_copy_again - the pass's _make_again, REMADE_SENTENCE and COPY_REMADE, decided by the person; a marked row refuses (MARKED_REFUSAL); keep-it-here and send-to-review refuse a both-gone row with NOTHING_TO_PUT_BACK, and send-to-review proves the original before it writes its intent. A RETURNING ORIGINAL (ruling B7, audit C5, 147's N-4): _sort_all asks _originals_away() (rows whose recorded original is absent, by digest - not an attachment, a marked row or a place an open intent will write) and a drop whose bytes are exactly one such row's goes back to that place by _put_back_home() - one intent (the move, plus the copies of a both_gone() row), no new row, ledger.ORIGINAL_RETURNED, RETURNED_SENTENCE put before any moved sentence (_before_the_moved_sentence), and the MISSING_IN_PBC and both-gone lines this pass said taken back (_ReturnRun.absence_said). _unique_path's exception is gone: a name a row names is taken whatever the bytes, so a same-bytes drop _put_back_home does not take is a Duplicate with a key of its own and no row is ever replaced. Decision 179: iter_drops() skips the inbox's README only when scaffold.whose_readme() says it is the firm's; a client's own file of that name is sorted like any drop, and one it cannot tell just now is left where it is and named in the pass's warnings. Decision 180: _may_touch() says where a step of a return may act - under the return, under its household's year _Opened, and in the client tree under some household's inbox or year folder, this return's household where the step writes - and _intend(), _do_op() and _finish_the_ops() refuse any step outside those places (OP_OUTSIDE) before it is recorded or anything moves - reads may come from any year's _Opened of the household, so a cross-year hand-over of an attachment stands - and the recovery's _a_copy_to_act_on() and _the_trouble() hold a row's pbc_location to the same places; locate() stays lexical and never raises. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 ruling 1): _sort_all() saves every return's verdict cache before it takes each file (a no-op when nothing changed), and file_household_drops() saves them again in the finally, after the rows, so neither a kill nor an exception loses a reading already made. Decision 189 (the bounded household, ruling 2.2): file_household_drops(deadline=) hands the deadline to every return's ContentCache for _sort_all(); past it a file whose bytes a return's record holds is still decided from the record (it reads nothing), and the first file that would need a new judgment stops the sort before it is moved - FileReport.unreached (on the first own return's report) counts what waits, unrecorded, for the next pass. A drop on record that must be routed afresh (a re-file, a re-send after a set-aside) stops at the judgment itself (content_check.OutOfTime from _judged() or _sort_one()), after its move: a stray the next pass sorts where it lies; an attachment stopped so waits, its container is left unrecorded and opened again next pass, and the household is out of time as for an unreached drop (_open_container re-raises OutOfTime to _sort_all; the review's M2). Decision 189 (the judgment worker): the household pass asks one judgment per drop. _judged sends every run's rows and one NameQuestion per run (_name_question) through router.read_once. route_file gets judgment=, and the name tier _by_the_name reads judgment.name(...) instead of calling check_name on text. _not_read reads judgment.extraction (the SPEC-156 seam). _sort_one asks its own return's rows and one name question. Decision 187 (first commit): _may_touch() is a one-line call to layout.place_problem(), the rule's one wording, and OP_OUTSIDE names the code in brackets after the location ('for a step (not-a-place)'). Decision 187 (second commit): _refuse_a_step_outside() reads both ends of a step from ledger.op_ends(); _do_op() also runs _refuse_a_step_through_a_link() before any mkdir - a source that is a link, or any folder between the clients root and either end that is one, raises MovedThroughALinkError (MOVE_THROUGH_A_LINK now says 'nothing was moved, copied or removed'), and _a_copy_to_act_on() holds a row's pbc_location to the same link check (A-7). COPY_UNPROVED: _do_op() and _copy_whole() refuse a copy with a blank digest; _intend() fills each blank copy digest in place through _prove() - from the earlier step of the same intent that brings the source in (its digest or its own source's bytes), else from the source's bytes - or raises COPY_UNPROVED before anything is recorded, which the pass's 'could not be filed' branch takes; the three direct _copy_whole() calls pass 'digest or sha256_of(source)'. Decision 187's review: _refuse_a_step_outside passes removes for a removal (M4); _finish_the_ops asks _refuse_a_step_through_a_link of every step before it reads or removes a byte (M3), and fingerprints a blank-digest copy's source itself so an interrupted intent from before 187 finishes (S3); _prove raises COPY_UNREAD, not COPY_UNPROVED, for a source that is there but cannot be read now (S6). Decision 188: the link check moved to door.through_a_link (imported as through_a_link, its only definition); _do_op asks door.client_write (_through_the_door) for a destination in the client tree and every folder made above it before any mkdir; sweep_stranded_temps asks the door before removing a README temp in the inbox; the walks use layout.parts_below instead of relative_to/relpath; the private tree is layout.private_tree_of. The engagement_dir CLI reads its folder through door.return_dir. Review of 188 (S2): _prune_empty_dirs removes an emptied folder in the inbox only through door.client_write. Decision 204's review: hand_over_copies() names a hand-over's copies (one per request, reusing only that request's own) and refuses NoRoom with PATH_NO_ROOM_IN naming the taking return (S-1); the API's card asks it too. PATH_NO_ROOM_IN also stays live in _decide_across for another of this household's own returns (S-2). Decision 159: holds_the_row() (was _holds_the_row) is public so store.verify() reuses the filer's one read of a file against its row's fingerprint rather than a second fingerprint routine. Decision 190: the OS errors that leave a drop in place and both 'could not be filed' catch-alls name errors.error_class() (an OSError with its errno, never its path), and log.exception became errors.keep(). Decision 190: every row the pass or a person parks carries a code - _park_it requires one - and every filed row the router's; _SortContext.subfolder replaces came_from and fills IndexEntry.subfolder, each part through layout.recorded_subfolder_part (the store's admission rule), and CAME_FROM_SUBFOLDER left the Reason (it is api's label now). _not_read compares the reading's code. DECISION 190 - THE README TEMP IS THE FIRM'S ONLY WHEN IT HOLDS THE FIRM'S TEXT: sweep_stranded_temps() takes a stranded _README.txt temp from the inbox only when _holds_the_firms_readme_text() says so - scaffold.whose_readme() says README_FIRMS, or the file is empty or a start of scaffold.README_FIRST_LINE (a kill before the first line was whole; the review's S5); a client file of that exact shape holding anything else, dead process number and all, is left and counted with the unfinished drops (revising 179's accepted residual). ignored_in_inbox() counts the files is_ignored() leaves alone that unfinished_drops() does not already name, onto the first return's FileReport.ignored - a count, never names. Decision 190 Part 3: a program drop parks before reading (_park_a_program, NOT_A_DOCUMENT, _park_it(copy=False)); a program inside an email or zip is never written to _Opened and its row has an empty pbc_location; _copy_whole marks a review copy of a macro-capable Office file or of any container on its temp before the swap, and a refused mark is MarkRefusedError (no copy, a could-not-be-filed row). FIRM_WRITTEN and errors.said name the filer's own errors whole on a row. Since the review of 190: _sort_one asks is_program before read_once, so a program sent again after it was set aside (or re-filed) parks NOT_A_DOCUMENT unread, with no copy, carrying the resent sentence; _review_copy_path refuses a program (REVIEW_OF_A_PROGRAM, a FilingError). _mark_for_review is the one marking path: _copy_whole marks on the temp, and _do_op marks a working copy before an OP_MOVE into review (an unfile, a refused put-back) - a mark refused moves nothing. Since the re-check of 190: _intend marks that working copy before the intent is written (_mark_a_move_into_review), and _carry_out_a_persons_ops abandons the intent when the first step's copy is refused, so a refused mark records nothing; _finish_interrupted_moves abandons an older open intent whose mark is refused and says so once (INTERRUPTED_MARK_REFUSED), and the pass goes on. A "could not be filed" row for a refused mark ends MARK_REFUSED_STEP, not "file it by hand". Every review lookup (find_parked, find_filed, find_moved, _find_to_put_back) goes through _wanted (an empty handle is NO_HANDLE, never "the first row with no location") and _names_row, which also accepts a location-less row's ledger_key - the api's handle. _shown(location) quotes a client path in a sentence as recorded; the row keeps the raw pbc_location. Decision 192: load_manifest / read_index take follow= (keyword, default True); False skips the journal top-up for a return the store holds - the practice page's alone. RETIRED_EVENTS names what this version reads and never writes: new(), append() and store.record() refuse rules_imported by sentence (RETIRED_EVENT), and a digest an old line carries is simply not read. fold() returns rows in the index's own order, and a row that changed identity keeps the place the one it left held. What keeps it honest is the autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py: after every test a store is built from nothing and held to replay() over these lines - the documents, the statuses and the rules alike. Sits at the bottom beside tracker/locking.py and imports only it: the events are plain dicts, so each writer serialises its own rows with the function in tracker/records.py that owns that shape, and no cycle is created. One os.write of the whole line under O_APPEND then fsync, so a kill mid-append leaves at most a torn tail: read_events() ignores it and the next append() truncates it, and nothing else ever rewrites the file. O_APPEND is atomic for concurrent writers on POSIX and is not on Windows, which is why append() refuses unless locking.lock_is_held() says this process holds the engagement lock. Not SQLite: a database file a cloud client syncs is a corrupted database file. migrated is the one event that carries no row - it named the files decision 102's migration moved aside; nothing writes one since 104, and it stays readable. Rows are keyed by the original's PBC location; a row that followed an original the client moved carries the identity it left (was), so the fold drops the vacated one. fold() passes over an event name it does not know and read_events() refuses a bad line anywhere but the tail. The reminder writes files and takes no lock, so drafted is reserved; runner and api reach the writers through the filer, the scanner and the manifest and make no call of their own. Decision 115 unreserved DRAFTED: written by the pass under the lock it holds and by the reminder's CLI under one it takes, carrying ASKED_KEY (identifiers asked, in order; [] on a quiet week) or HELD_KEY (identifiers that held the draft), and FILE_KEY / FINGERPRINT_KEY when a file was written - identifiers only, never a word of the email; appended only when something moved. day_of() is the one reading of a stamp, the local day it fell on, beside stamp() the one writing. Decision 113 gave it the one fold it never had: KEYWORD_UNLEARNED is the event a person's unlearn writes, Folded.learned is identifier -> the keywords filings taught and nobody has taken back, and _apply_keyword_event() folds both - learn appends the word, or moves it last where it is already there, and unlearn removes it, so a word taught again lands last either way, which is the order the store's own ORDER BY seq gives, its insert carrying the new line's sequence number. The two folds agree by construction and not because no writer here teaches a word twice. The identifier is keyed exactly as each line spells it, because this module sits below records and may not borrow identifier_key (test_layers); the one reader that has to join two spellings of a request, store._check_learned(), folds both sides itself. So the learned table is inside store.check() at last, and the suite's rebuild-and-check fixture proves it after every test. Decision 118 added draft_approved beside drafted: a person read the week's draft in the app and approved it, carrying the stage, the file, that file's header fingerprint and the identifiers asked. Folded by nothing, like drafted - a fact about a week, not a row of the index - and carrying no word of the letter. Decision 126 added sharing_confirmed on the same pattern, in the household's journal: the firm's word that it shared the household with its client, folded by nothing and carrying nothing at all but the stamp, because the tracker cannot see Drive's sharing and must not record what it cannot check. tracker.store._refuse_a_malformed_line() refuses a line of it that carries anything. RELEASE_EVENTS is RELEASED and the retired handed_over_by_person decision 129 wrote, which joins RETIRED_EVENTS: read once, folded as a release of its key, never written. Whoever saves a head beside lines it applied (the store) uses read_with_head(). Decision 137 (A3): _parse_lines() keeps each event's own line bytes, chain_link() is one step of the applied chain (sha256 of the chain so far and the line), and read_with_chain() returns the events, the head and the chain after each line from one read - the store's proof that the lines it applied are still the journal's. The journal's format is unchanged. Decision 143 added the row event OPENED ('opened'), whose line carries ATTACHMENTS_KEY and SKIPPED_KEY beside the row; the fold keeps the row only. Decision 160 added the row event RENAMED_BY_PERSON ('renamed_by_person'): a person's rename re-wrote the row - its copies renamed in place (moved into the renamed request folder before decision 168), or only its identifier changed; each closes one intent the rename wrote. Decision 157 added two row events: COPY_REMADE ('copy_remade' - a gone working copy made again from its original, by the pass or by a person's Put it back, closing its intent) and ORIGINAL_RETURNED ('original_returned' - a row's own original back from the inbox, moved to its recorded place, no new row); ANSWER_WITHDRAWN_BY_PERSON also records a person marking a both-gone row's own request missing. Both fold like every row event, so the store's version is unchanged. Decision 180: every ValueError a line raises while it is parsed - a number past the interpreter's digit limit included - is the record's LedgerError with its line. Decision 189 (A-9): an OSError from _write_line() or _truncate_torn_tail() leaves as RecordNotWritten(LedgerError) with code = the errno's name and the fixed sentence RECORD_NOT_WRITTEN - the path (a client's folder) stays on __cause__, so the pass catches it as it catches every LedgerError and one full disk costs one household. Decision 187: op_ends(op) says once which end of a step reads and which writes - (from, read) and (to, write) for a copy or a move, (from, write) for a removal - for the filer and the store's gate. Decision 187's review (S1): day_of catches OSError and OverflowError as well as ValueError, so a stamp Windows cannot give a local day reads as long ago. Decision 188: ACCEPTED_KEY ('accepted') with the one value FOLDER_NAME_ACCEPTED ('folder_name') - a person's word that a folder's name is the name, carried only on the household_changed and rules_changed lines the API's accept-folder-name writes; the store admits it there with that value only. The filer moves and records; the scanner records statuses; the manifest records a person's edit (decision 104) - all under this one lock, one protocol. Dry runs never take it. The descriptor stays open while held (Windows then refuses to delete it, so a stale-looking lock its owner still holds is refused) and release_lock() removes the file only if it still carries this run's token. RUN_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS is the one number for how long a scheduled pass may run: tracker.scheduling renders it as the task's ExecutionTimeLimit and STALE_LOCK_SECONDS is derived above it. One machine per clients root: a lock file synced between two machines is not a lock. lock_status()/clear_stale_lock() back the app's lock notice. Decision 54: pid_alive() - a lock whose owner process is gone is stale at any age. Decision 56: the lock line carries host=; another host's pid is unknowable, never dead. Decision 59: a lock that cannot be deleted on release is marked RELEASED_LINE. Decision 102: the lock is not re-entrant - it is an O_EXCL file - so the steps a pass makes take a lock_held flag and skip taking it, and a writer that may be reached with the lock already held (manifest.save_rules(), the journal's append) asks lock_is_held() rather than taking it twice. Decision 115: the machine's name in the lock line comes from platform.node(), not from the socket module - the same name, and the package imports no network module. Decision 137 (L6): the module docstring states that the stale-lock rules rest on the one-machine rule - another host's lock is left to the age rule, whose promise is this machine's schedule's. Decision 171 (the Drive test's F1 and F2): on Google Drive a contended unlink can report success and leave the file, so release_lock() reads the file back - only FileNotFoundError proves it went, a refused read is looked at again - and treats its own token still there like a refused delete (retry, then RELEASED_LINE); the file is read again before every retried delete; a module-level Counter of the exact tokens this process holds (by token, not path: no second spelling hides a held lock, and a release removes only its own), behind a threading.Lock kept as insurance (the app runs one tracker process per command, no threads), makes a lock naming this process whose text is not a held token a leftover to replace - one process takes the same lock twice in ordinary work (an app command then its _rescan; a fed return in two household passes) - while a held token is still refused; and a PermissionError from the O_EXCL create is changing hands only while something is at the name (retried up to _CHANGING_HANDS_ATTEMPTS times, then EngagementLockedError 'is changing hands'): refused with the name free, once more at once, and then the original PermissionError goes to the caller, a run error, never a quiet skip. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 A-F3): acquire_lock() fsyncs the lock line; LockStatus.owner_gone is the one judgement (made by _status_from() from the very handle decision 159's breaker compares, and asked by the take, lock_status(), clear_stale_lock() and a breaker's abandonment alike): released; unwritten (empty, no pid=) and older than EMPTY_LOCK_SECONDS (60); or this host's and started more than BOOT_MARGIN_SECONDS (120) before boot_time() (GetTickCount64 on Windows, /proc/uptime elsewhere, None and no boot rule when neither reads; the suite replaces it) or its pid gone. Another host's lock keeps the age rule. Decision 159 (part 2): the stale take is atomic through an O_EXCL breaker (breaker_of); an abandoned breaker is cleared by exactly one racer through an O_EXCL marker named for its identity (text, mtime_ns, inode from one handle), markers swept after BREAKER_STALE_SECONDS; an empty text never compares equal on text alone. On Windows a delete refused because another process has the file open for a moment (a racer reading it to judge it) is waited out: the breaker's release retries within the release budget, reading its token before every try, and the stale delete and the abandoned-breaker clear retry briefly; a clear still refused removes its own marker, so a later claim on that breaker can succeed (decision 159, Windows). The write guard is holds(): a token this process took, with a per-take random id, recorded against the lock path it was written to and matched by samefile - lock_is_held() now answers from it, which is 171's 'left for 159'. this_host() names the machine for the record's host key, and is_this_host() is the one comparison of a host (any case, spaces stripped); LockStatus.owner_gone asks it. The race CLI (python -m tracker.locking race <folder>) takes RACE_LOCK_FILENAME, never a return's own lock, and is Jason's live check L1.
- **`tracker/manifest.py`** — The request list: its schema, its validation, and its reading from and writing to the record. Since decision 104 the manifest IS the record's request list - the accountant's columns (COLUMNS, whose headers are HEADERS, each with the sentence COLUMN_HELP gives the editor) and the engagement's details - and there is no workbook. Owns RequestItem, Status, Override, item_from_fields() and validated() (the validation the sheet's loader used to make, as a function on records), load_manifest() and load_engagement_info() (the answers, from the record), create_engagement() and save_rules() (the two writes, each one rules_changed event), check_rules() (the warnings) and summarize(). Since decision 142 a row carries asked (yes by default): every catalog row is on every return, only the asked ones are listed, counted in total and chased, and a row nobody asked for files what arrives for it. Since decision 144 a row carries short_title (blank by default, at most SHORT_TITLE_MAX characters, refused by short_title_problem() otherwise): RequestItem.short_name is it, or derived_short_title() of the document - the name the firm's working folder and copies go by; the client-facing label keeps the full title. A Document written as ISSUER_DOCUMENT ("Schedule K-1 - <entity>", the prefix without case) derives issuer_short_title(entity), K-1 <entity>, however the row was added.

THE OWNER RETIRED THE EXCEL MANIFEST ON 2026-09-19 (decision 104): until then the list was the workbook registry.LEGACY_MANIFEST_FILENAME names, read once a pass and journalled as it changed; now the app's editor is the only way a rule is entered, and every save is one rules_changed event through store.record() under the engagement lock - create_engagement() carries the whole list and every detail (validated before a line is written, so a refusal leaves no folder content and no store row), save_rules() carries exactly the rows that changed, whole and row included (a row's position is part of the rule, so a row moved is a row changed), the identifiers removed and the details that moved, and nothing at all when nothing did. The diff is by the identifier's exact spelling and the folds (ledger.apply and the store's) apply removals before rows and delete by that exact spelling (never SQLite's ASCII-only lower()); _refuse_a_malformed_line() refuses a rules_changed or scanned line of the wrong shape by name before a value of it reaches a table, so an identifier respelled by case is one event - the old spelling removed, the new carried - and never two rows. create_engagement() forgets the store row a folder deleted by hand left before following the new journal. The writes came back here, having left in 103, because the module that owns the schema and the validation must own the writes, or the rows in the journal would be shaped by somebody else; they reach store, ledger and locking at call time, so the module still imports tracker/records.py and nothing else at load time (tests/test_layers.py). item_from_fields() is the one parser of a row from plain values (the editor's JSON, a catalog spec, a test's dict), its refusals prefixed by where - a row number from the API, the identifier from the catalog - and it defaults NO keyword, as the sheet allowed; validated() makes the list-level checks (identifier required and folder-safe, duplicates without case because Windows folders are, the two numbers within MIN_EXPECTED_COUNT and MIN_SIZE_KB_FLOOR, NO_DATE_CHECK made blank, a typed pattern compiled, a blank one derived from the Period with date_pattern_derived set, and last check_narrowing_names()) and numbers the rows 1..n. Every path that stores rules or routes against a catalog goes through it - the two writes, tests/test_irs_forms.py, tests/test_catalog.py, tools/vocab_report.py - so the derived year check the harnesses used to get from a workbook round trip is the same check, made once. A row that comes back from the store says its pattern was derived, and both parsers read that as no pattern typed, so a list read out of the record and saved again records nothing. load_manifest(engagement_dir) answers from the record - the rules from the store's requests table, the four status fields from statuses, the keywords a filing taught from learned_keywords laid over the row's own Any Keywords by _with_the_record() - after store.follow_the_journal(); a folder with no journal is refused by NOT_AN_ENGAGEMENT. check_rules() is the warnings half of what the old manifest check said (a row with no rule, ANY_EXTENSION, a keyword with no letter or digit, a bare family number - decisions 55 and 58) and rides every state the app reads and every pass; there is no problems half, because a list the record holds was validated on the way in. Decision 120 took the atomic write out: the temp suffix, the temp path, the replacement context and the two writers over it are tracker/fsio.py at layer 0 now, and nothing is re-exported from here - this module owns the request list, not how a file is replaced. identifier_problem() refuses identifiers that could not survive as a folder-name prefix. with_statuses() is what the scanner uses to count the rows as it is about to leave them. Decision 62: derived_date_pattern() asks for the month a Period names. Decision 68: a status is matched to its row without case (records.identifier_key()). Decision 72: csv_tuple() takes a list as the list it already is; check_tax_year() is the one bound on a tax year. Decision 86: the details carry the form the list was cut from; create_engagement() takes it as a keyword because it is one fact about the engagement, and a blank never clears one the info carries. Decision 90: keyword_alternatives() lives here beside csv_tuple() because this module owns how a keyword is read - '|' names alternatives, '+' joins phrases wanted together. Decision 93: entity_keyword() is the one normalisation of an entity's name; narrowing_rows() says which rows narrow which and is empty for every shipped catalog; check_narrowing_names() refuses a list where one issuer name sits inside another's. The records it reads and writes - EngagementInfo, StatusUpdate, the rule row's serialisation - live in tracker/records.py (decision 100); RequestItem stays here because it is the schema of the list a person edits. What left with decision 104 - the workbook reader, the template writer, the slimming, the Engagement sheet's reader and writer, the manifest check - is set aside outside the tree in Retired - Excel manifest. Decision 116: the override is recorded with its reason and the second value is Override.NOT_APPLICABLE. override_reason is a rule field (records.RULE_FIELDS, last, so older rows read as blank), COLUMNS gains COL_OVERRIDE_REASON, and validated() refuses Accepted with no reason, the word OVERRIDE_REASON_OTHER itself, and a reason with no override; OVERRIDE_REASONS are the four one-click reasons. Override.RETIRED folds the retired spelling to its successor inside _override() on every read; item_from_record() is the ONE reader of a stored rule row (load_manifest, the save_rules diff's stored side, the API's editor rows), so a journal written before this decision is read as Not Applicable, its bytes are never rewritten, and saving an unchanged list records nothing. override_label() is the word people see - NOT_APPLICABLE_LABEL with the year detect_year() gives the row, or the bare value; the year is never stored. Summary.not_applicable replaces the old count. Decision 113 added the third write, and the only one that does not touch the rules a person typed: unlearn_keyword() takes back a keyword a filing taught one request, under the engagement lock, as one keyword_unlearned event through store.record() - journalled, not simply deleted, because deleting the store's row would be a fact only the database held and the next rebuild would put it back. The pair is refused by name (UNLEARN_REFUSED) when the record never carried it, so a word the row types itself is not unlearnable - that is an edit of the rule, made in the editor like any other - and the line spells the request the way the list does, whatever case the caller typed, because the journal's fold has no case rule of its own. Decision 128 added the twelfth column, Named: whether the document this request asks for carries a name. Blank is yes, everywhere a row is read without one - strict is the rule the owner asked for. Decision 137: WINDOWS_RESERVED_NAMES / is_reserved_name() (L6) - identifier_problem() refuses a device name; create_engagement() and a save_rules() that changes the link refuse a link that is not http(s) (L5, records.link_problem). Review fix (F6): WINDOWS_RESERVED_NAMES also holds CONIN$, CONOUT$ and COM/LPT with a superscript 1-3. Decision 141: JURAT lives here beside the keyword grammar, and asks_for_a_return(item) says a row requires it - the router's one test of a return row; tracker.templates reads JURAT from here. Decision 160: list_head() is the version of the list and the details (a digest of the store's rules and engagement info - not the journal's head, which every pass moves); save_rules(head=...) refuses any other version or none under the lock (refuse_a_stale_list(), LIST_MOVED, NO_LIST_HEAD); recorded_rules() is the person's rules as recorded, without taught keywords; renamed_rules() builds the events that rename a request - one rules_changed (old removed, the row carried whole under the new identifier in its place) and an unlearn plus a learn per taught keyword. save_rules(check=...) runs a caller's refusal under the same lock, after the version and before the diff - the API's documents-held check. Decision 187: the editor's checks are the records value rule's - the moved names are re-exported from tracker.records (the same objects); _whole_number() takes a maximum and refuses with records.COUNT_BOUNDS (never quoting the value); validated() holds the two numbers to count_problem and a typed Date Pattern to records.date_pattern_problem instead of compile-only. Decision 187's review (M6): validated() runs records.rule_row_fault on each row it returns and refuses with the row and the column, so the editor never saves what the store's gate refuses. Decision 190: RequestItem gains note_codes (the record's, never typed), carried from the status by _with_the_record, with note_code_list. Decision 192: load_manifest / read_index take follow= (keyword, default True); False skips the journal top-up for a return the store holds - the practice page's alone. Decision 200: STATUS_LABELS is the one table of what each word the record keeps for a row is shown as (label and one sentence), keyed by the record's word. status_key() is the record's word (the old status_label logic), and status_label() the preparer's. Summary.shown_line is the labelled line the app shows, and Summary.line keeps the record's words for the run log and the CLI; both come from one private builder, _said, so they cannot drift apart. Decision 201: check_narrowing_names refuses equal names too (ISSUER_NAMED_TWICE), except a pair `recorded` already holds untouched, which it returns as a warning; validated(recorded=), save_rules judges it against the held list under the lock and returns RulesSaved.warnings; create_engagement(carried=<last year's rows>) carries a held pair as it was and returns its sentence for the roll's reply (rows a roll adds from the catalog are checked as any write); the rename carries a held pair as it was. P215 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): load_manifest and load_engagement_info still follow the journal every time, then build through store.held_read, so inside a hold the list is built once per record head and built again once the journal moves; nothing is kept once the hold ends.

A spelling is at least two words (records.MIN_SPELLING_WORDS): a family name alone is a whole phrase inside a company's name, so `Park` would confirm `Park Landscaping LLC`'s bank statement as the family's - the two-word rule is kept wherever a spelling is accepted and again in check_name(). Confirmed beats vetoed beats absent, so a joint page naming both spouses is confirmed for both returns and the exactly-one rule decides. Nothing is inferred: the app proposes and a person ticks, no spelling is ever learned from a document, and no fuzzy match is made. The CLI (python -m tracker.names "John A. Park") prints the proposals and records nothing. The matcher is unchanged. A page is folded once (read_names gives NamesOnPage), and check_name(..., page=) searches it for every spelling. It used to re-fold the whole page per spelling (the SPEC-189 second cost).

Device: gpu_pack() is the gpu-runtime folder beside the frozen exe (never from source); none means the processor with no CUDA request at all (onnxruntime-gpu 'offers' CUDA everywhere, so offered is never the test). With a pack, _on_the_card() calls onnxruntime.preload_dlls() on it, builds asking for CUDA, requires each of SESSIONS (text_det, text_cls, text_rec) to have CUDAExecutionProvider first, and runs _self_test() on a line drawn in memory; any failure is the processor plus PACK_UNUSABLE (a run-log line, not a warning). read_page(): any exception from the card's engine is a fault (the card poisons the process - 'CUDA failure 999'): the engine is dropped, the processor's built, the same page read again, processor_only() for the rest of the pass, and a ('gpu-fault', file) note becomes GPU_FAULT_WARNING once in the pass; reset() lets the next pass try the card. _upright_lines() is ruling 6's seam: lines in reading order from the boxes (the harness's lines_from_boxes), never a turn. The child: ReadingChild is one spawned process serving jobs one at a time over three pipes (jobs, answers, lifeline), saying 'started' before each job touches a file, answering with take_notes(); a job it cannot unpickle exits UNREADABLE_JOB_EXIT_CODE (the machine's, before 'started'). _watch_the_pass/_orphaned (the lifeline) and _kill_on_close_job/_close_job (the Windows job object) and _end() (the whole tree) moved here from content_check. Session (reading_session(), run_in_child()) owns the child for a pass - runner.run_registry with settle=True, which with a pack starts the child at once for warm_up() so the run log's first line is settled - or for one app command (api.main); a reading with none open gets a session of its own. It replaces the child after a stop, a crash, a child that never started, a fault on the card and every DOCUMENTS_PER_CHILD (100) documents. content_check.in_a_child() words each Outcome. The CLI (python -m tracker.ocr [photo]) says which reader this machine uses and times one reading. Decision 189 (SPEC-161 A-F9): awake_clock() - QueryUnbiasedInterruptTime on Windows, time.monotonic elsewhere - is the one clock of every part of a reading's stop: ReadingChild.run() and Session._run_once() in the pass, content_check._clock in the child; ReadingChild.run() re-measures what is left after every message and every wake, so a poll the machine slept through is not a stop. Unchanged by decision 189's judgment worker in code: its one reader child now runs content_check.judge (read plus judgment) as the job for every document the pass decides, so the document's stop and the child's memory cap bound the rules and the name check as well as the reading, and the answer crossing the pipe is a small Judgment with no text. Containers (decision 154) still open through the same run_in_child. Decision 190: a job that raises in the reading child is sent back as three parts - errors.error_class(), the message and the trace (Outcome.error, Outcome.message, Outcome.trace) - and the child never opens a log; the pass shows the class and keeps the rest. The warm-up's words are the self-test's and are still said in PACK_UNUSABLE / READER_CANNOT_RUN. Decision 186: nor may anything a reading writes outlive it - each ReadingChild asks settings.scratch_root() before any process starts (no data home: not_started, the machine's), and the child's first act (_take_scratch()) is to sweep folders of dead processes (sweep_scratch(), by locking.pid_alive(), never a live or unknowable one - D-14) and point TMP, TEMP, TMPDIR and tempfile.tempdir at scratch/<its pid>; end() removes that folder once the child is gone, and a killed child's is swept by the next. Not covered: reading_session(in_a_child=False), the suite's in-process reading and the tools that call extract() directly.

DECISION 190 - EACH PAGE CARRIES ITS OWN POLICY: policy() is a Content-Security-Policy meta tag of default-src 'none' plus the SHA-256 (base64, source_hash()) of the page's own inline style and, when it has one, its script; runner and view compute theirs at import from the module constants they write, so the policy cannot drift from the page, and 'unsafe-inline' was rejected because it would let a block the page did not write run too. Decision 109: as_pattern() is here - a note's template turned into the pattern that reads its own sentence back, every word escaped and every {name} the pattern given for it. It came from the scanner, which has read the regression sentence back this way since decision 108, because how a sentence the machine wrote is read is a fact about the shape it was stored in; the filer derives moved_to()'s pattern from the same function, so two readers share one derivation and neither retypes a word. Decision 117: DATE_FIELDS is the one answer to which details are dates - the record's own serialisers, the API's reading of a wizard or editor spec and the editor's choice of box all read it instead of naming due, so the Filing Deadline added beside the Due Date cost one line in each. The API's state hands a rule out in the form edit reads back as the same rule (an any-file-type row as ["*"], not the record's []), so rules sent back unchanged record nothing. Still imports nothing of the package (math and re._parser are the standard library's). Decision 187's second re-check (M1c): _width is the widest match of a pattern's bounded parts (a fixed {n} n times, a lookaround its own width, an open-ended part one), and a pattern whose _ways x _width is over DATE_PATTERN_COST_MAX is refused (DATE_PATTERN_TOO_COSTLY). Decision 188 (part 3): the folder is the identity and the record's labels are a claim. NAME_DISAGREES and _disagreement are gone (overruled with decision 177's warning and 125's 'the record wins'): discover_engagements fills Registry.paused (household -> households.HOUSEHOLD_PAUSED or HOUSEHOLD_PAUSED_YEAR, from households.pause_of over the household's record and its readable returns) and Registry.stopped (TWO_CLAIM for every household whose folder or claimed name is another's by layout.name_key - a copy of a household folder - and HOUSEHOLD_RECORD_MISSING for a household position whose record is gone while its returns hold theirs; those returns are listed as engagements carrying the sentence, so the pass counts them as failed). _walk_root lists the client tree's first level by name with os.scandir (never deeper, never a stat of what is inside) and every Clients folder that is no discovered household's is MISFIT_CLIENT_NO_RECORD; MISFIT_NO_HOUSEHOLD_RECORD is corrected (the app will not set a household up over it). The key refuses; it never identifies. Decision 193: a folder the walk cannot list is said by class and code (errors.error_class, decision 190) in its misfit sentence, the full text kept with errors.keep() only; an empty root is EmptyRoot, a RegistryError the app answers as a practice not set up yet, while any other is said (PRACTICE_NOT_WALKED). P120: household_positions(root) lists the private tree's households as _walk_root does, for the firm cache. Review fold: household_positions leaves out the folders _skip() passes over. P208 (pilot/SPEC-scale-1000.md): held_back asks stopped_households(root), which is discover_engagements(root).stopped from the same walk and the same two rules (_households_kept, _stopped_of, shared with _kept) without reading a return, inside settings.one_reading(). P219 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): engagement_from asks store.has_rules for a legacy folder rather than building its list. Pilot P225: _Priors.by_tail() groups the readable returns by their last layout.ROLLED_FROM_TAIL names, once, and _prior_of's name fallback compares Rolled From only with its own group - every return outside it ends in fewer than three of its names, which the floor refuses, so the answer is the every-pair answer (tests/test_registry.py keeps that rule as a reference). It took 1,999,000 common_tail calls, about 0.9 s a discovery, at 1,000 rolled households after a root move.
