  - note: Validation notes are translated into plain client instructions, never quoted. Rows we have not read yet are held back for a person instead of being asked for (a row with no request folder was too, until decision 168 retired the folder, NO_REQUEST_FOLDER and the scaffold-gap list: triage() returns three lists). A row nobody asked for (decision 142) is skipped before anything else: never asked, never a hold. Each draft carries a fingerprint of its own text so an edited draft is never overwritten. A Partial row whose shortfall is a file we have not read is held back too. Reads the engagement's details from the record for client, link, due, sender and firm (manifest.load_engagement_info(); a folder with no record is a ReminderError naming the journal's file); keyword arguments are one-off overrides for the CLI. Decision 57: write_draft() raises DraftsEditedError rather than overwrite an edited NEW draft; the runner reports BOTH_DRAFTS_EDITED and writes nothing. Decision 62: EXTENSION_ASK names the row's own file types; --write preserves edits. Decision 76: count_needs_review() is still the folder's count less the working copies whose newest index row is filer.NOT_REQUESTED. An index it cannot read leaves every file counted. Decision 103: the draft is built from the record alone; a status only the record holds is what it counts. Decision 115: triage() returns a fourth list, held - a Failed row with no firm-side marker, or a Partial whose shortfall is a refused file, is ambiguous (AMBIGUOUS_HOLD) and one such row holds the whole draft: write_draft() raises ReminderHeldError (HELD_REFUSAL, naming every held row) before touching a file, the CLI prints HELD lines and --write exits 2, and SECTION_FAILED left SECTION_ORDER (unreachable from a pass; client_ask()'s Failed branch kept for an action a person may one day record). A firm-side marker on any outstanding status, Missing included, is the firm's (109's rule stated once). The draft is on the record: drafted_event() builds the ledger.DRAFTED event (asked identifiers, file and fingerprint; or held identifiers), draft_changed() says whether it differs from the last one (or is a new draft week's, when the caller passes the week), record_draft() writes it through store.record() under the caller's lock, last_draft_event() reads the newest (or the newest carrying a key). write_draft(changed_from=...) opens the header with CHANGED_HEADING / CHANGED_ADDED / CHANGED_REMOVED against the last event that carried asked, above the separator. HELD_SUMMARY is the one line the app shows, through api._vocab(). Decision 117: the draft escalates in four stages against the Due Date (STAGE_2_DAYS, STAGE_3_DAYS - constants, the owner's), each with its own subject, intro, deadline paragraph and close; the stage changes the words only - triage() still decides the recipients and the gate holds at every stage - and the sentences name the Due Date and the Filing Deadline and never the arithmetic between two dates a person may have moved. The stage rides in the header above the fingerprint line (STAGE_LINE, so an edit is still never overwritten) and in the DRAFTED event (STAGE_KEY), which draft_changed() compares as a fifth key, so a client who crossed a threshold gets this week's draft even when the asked set did not move; --stage and --today write another stage's or another day's letter. The final notice's phone sentence comes from settings.firm_phone() - the firm's, not the engagement's - and is dropped when that is blank. And the hold of decision 115 gained a second cause: a parked index row whose code (since decision 190; its reason before) is a holding one, and whose shortlist in tracker/review.py names a request still asked for, holds that request (PARKED_HOLD, _parked_holds(), a call-time import of review), because a drop the rules refused at tier 2 never reaches a status and the draft would ask for a document the client knows they sent; draft_reminder() reads the rows itself and the API hands in the ones it has already read. It reads the SHORTLIST and not the row's Candidates cell: candidates are the requests that accepted the file, and a file refused before a word of it could be read - the locked PDF, the headline case - has none, so the draft and the review card now answer 'what does this parked file point at?' the same way. Decision 118: the letter is a structure before it is words. _compose_letter() builds a Letter (greeting, progress, intro, sections, drop lines and link, the deadline paragraph as runs, close, sign-off) and Letter.text() is the body the file carries, so the plain text, render_html()'s inline-styled body for the clipboard and the shape the app draws its preview from are three renderings of one thing and cannot say different things. The deadline paragraph is cut into runs by formatting the stage's own sentence with sentinels round the target, the filing deadline and the consequences sentence - never by searching the finished sentence for a date, which an engagement name could also contain. STAGE_COLOURS, HOLD_COLOUR, LETTER_INK name keys of page.PALETTE and STAGE_EMPHASIS says where each stage spends its colour and its weight; render_html() reads that table and the API ships it, so the letter, the clipboard and the card apply one ladder. render_html() is rendered on demand and never written to disk - the .txt stays what the pass writes. approved_event()/last_approved_event()/is_approved_this_week()/is_protected() are the approval a person makes in the app: until the next draft day the pass treats the approved file exactly as it treats one somebody edited (write_draft(approved_since=...) puts the regenerated draft in the .NEW file instead), and set_aside_other_draft() renames any draft standing beside it by SET_ASIDE_DRAFT_PATTERN rather than deleting it. Imports tracker.page at load time for esc() and the palette, which is L3 -> L0. An approval holds against every writer, not only the pass: is_approved_this_week(since=None) asks only whether this is the approved file, so the command line - a layer below the runner, and unable to learn the draft week - lands its --write draft beside an approved one rather than over it, and the pass, which knows the week, is the one caller that spends the approval. pasted_text() gives the letter between the header's rule and FOOTER_RULE: the staff-side footer write_draft() may add is the machine's note to the person, as the header is, and firm-side sentences must not be one paste from a client. DECISION 133 - THE REMINDER WAITS FOR THE SORT: unsorted_in_inbox() counts the distinct paths the filer's iter_drops, unfinished_drops and unreachable_drops (imported at call time, as the rest of this module reaches the filer) return for layout.inbox_of() of the return - its OWN household's inbox only; an inbox in another household that also feeds it (decision 132) is not read, a known limit. draft_reminder() stores it as ReminderDraft.unsorted, and is_held is now bool(held) or unsorted > 0, so the pass, the command line and the app hold alike and write_draft() refuses before touching a file; held stays the rows. held_refusal() says INBOX_HOLD when files wait, HELD_REFUSAL when rows hold, both joined by '; '; INBOX_HELD_SUMMARY is the app's line (api vocab inbox_held_line). P134: unsorted_files_in_inbox() gives each counted path's own name, sorted, from the same walk, and unsorted_in_inbox() is its length; the API's reminder card carries it as unsorted_files for the sheet to list. A hold records a drafted event with held and no file, so the next pass that sorts the inbox drafts the same day. Decision 137 (L5): a recorded link that is not http(s) (records.link_problem) is left out of the letter and ReminderDraft.link_dropped says so (LINK_DROPPED), above the footer and on the CLI; saving one is refused by the manifest and the household writers. Decision 140: _parked_holds() asks reason.holds, not 'not firm_side'; a firm-side reason that holds (SHOWS_ITS_FORM_NUMBER) says CONFIRM_HOLD with the reason's firm note and no client ask, so neither the held line nor the draft ever says the client's file was wrong; a client-side hold keeps PARKED_HOLD word for word. _parked_holds() returns FirmSideFlags; a confirm hold carries confirm=True, and held_refusal() refuses those rows with CONFIRM_REFUSAL ('held until a person confirms the parked file (open it in Needs Review)') beside HELD_REFUSAL for the rest. Decision 190: client_ask, _firm_side_reason and _ambiguous_reason read the notes' codes (RequestItem.note_code_list, reasons.first_of / FIRM_SIDE), and _parked_holds reads the row's code (BY_CODE, HOLDS) - never the note or the Reason, which carry the client's file names and subfolders. A parked row with an empty code (written before 190) holds where its shortlist names a request, asked with GENERIC_ASK. DECISION 190 - AN APPROVAL COVERS THE TEXT APPROVED: approved_event() also records ledger.TEXT_FINGERPRINT_KEY, letter_fingerprint() of the file - the letter as a person reads it (pasted_text, split_pasted, shown_text(), the one composition of subject and body the API fingerprints too); approval_state() answers APPROVED_NOTE while it matches, APPROVED_THEN_EDITED ('approved, then edited') after an edit, and '' for none, another file, a spent week or another draft on that name; an event from before 190 without the key reads APPROVED_THEN_EDITED (not an approval, so the person approves again, but never '' - the review's S1). is_approved_this_week() is approval_state() == APPROVED_NOTE; is_protected() is edited, or approval_state() not '', so an edited file and a pre-190 approval's file both stay protected and a regenerated draft goes beside them. THE HEADER NAMES THE FIRM PHONE: ReminderDraft.phone carries the number it was composed with and phone_line() puts FIRM_PHONE_LINE, FIRM_PHONE_UNUSED_LINE (set, but this stage offers no call) or NO_FIRM_PHONE_LINE above the rule, so the body fingerprint and is_unedited() are unchanged. Since the review of 190: unusable_files(parked) lists the still-parked NOT_A_DOCUMENT rows by recorded name, and the letter asks about each under SECTION_FAILED ("RECEIVED, BUT WE COULD NOT USE IT", kept by decision 124) in NOT_A_DOCUMENT.ask - EXTENSION_NOT_ALLOWED's words - without holding; ReminderDraft.unusable carries them. _still_parked reads a set-aside row by its code (DISMISSED_BY_PERSON_CODE), never the start of its Reason. Since the re-check of 190: the stage, the subject's count and the progress line come from the request lines alone; has_outstanding is lines or unusable, so a letter that only asks about a program is written by the runner and editable on the app's card, at no stage (NOTHING_OWED, the SECTION_FAILED block and the drop paragraph, no deadline). Decision 190, Jason's answer 1b: a week whose only problem is a file that is not a document opens with UNUSABLE_ONLY - the quiet week's first sentence, then UNUSABLE_ONLY_NOTE ('One file you sent could not be used; please see the note below.'), or UNUSABLE_SOME with UNUSABLE_SOME_NOTE ('Some files you sent could not be used; please see the note below.') when more than one file is listed (the port review's S1) - never NOTHING_OWED's 'Nothing further is needed', which the ask below would contradict; a week with a request outstanding keeps its staged letter. Decision 200: SIDES (Client, Us, Decide) name triage()'s three lists, and sides() gives each outstanding row its side and its own sentence. The staff footer and the CLI name the Us and Decide sides and each row's status label. HELD_BACK_HEADING, HELD_BACK_LINE and HELD_LINE are retired; the letter body is unchanged. Each Stage gains a short name (Heads up, Checking in, Deadline near, Final notice) for the app's rows (SPEC-shell 11.6); the letter keeps the full name. The app-only sentences (HELD_SUMMARY, INBOX_HELD_SUMMARY, LAST_DRAFTED_LINE, EDITED_BY_HAND, COPIED_NOTE, SET_ASIDE_LINE, REMINDER_NOT_YET) were reworded to the approved short words (P84); the letter reads none of them.

It writes no artifact at all: no sidecar, no status, no move, no lock, and no client document is opened - the index's Evidence column is already the store, and a second one could disagree with it the moment somebody filed a row by hand. It reads the manifest and the index (read_index over the engagement folder, which since decision 102 answers from the store and moves nothing at all); a caller that already loaded either passes it in. rank sorts ascending as (identity, strength, catalog): identity is a slot reserved for a later step and constant today, strength is RULE_STRENGTH before PLACE_STRENGTH so a required keyword said deep outranks an any-keyword in a title - the way the router already weighs the two rules - and the manifest's own order breaks a tie as a tie. Evidence only: the request list's Missing/Received state is deliberately not a tiebreaker and never fills a shortlist (owner, 2026-09-18), because a nudge with nothing behind it is how a tired reviewer files the wrong document into the last open row. So a row whose evidence says nothing - matched no request, a scan whose name says nothing either, a record carrying only a refusal - gets an empty shortlist and keeps the router's own reason, and a row set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE is never suggested - it is NAMED instead (decision 116): Triage.set_aside carries each such row the evidence pointed at with its year's label, said in SET_ASIDE_NOTE on the review card and the Status Report, so the person who set it aside decides and the machine never files under it. Since decision 92 an unreadable scan whose name DOES carry a row's keyword arrives here with RULE_FILENAME evidence and is offered as 'A01 - the file name says W-2' at the bottom of the ranking: the one piece of evidence the client wrote rather than the form, so it starts a person reading and can never outrank a word the document itself said. A RULE_REFUSED entry is never a suggestion by itself; beside content evidence its cause is said in that suggestion's sentence, in the words reasons.py gives it. PLACE_WORDS is the one mapping from an evidence place to the words for it, so api._vocab() can expose it rather than the app typing a word of its own. Nothing below it imports it, and it imports neither runner, scheduling, settings nor api; genre and group are reserved for later steps. Decision 128 filled the rank's first slot, reserved for identity since C5: a row whose page confirmed one of the return's spellings (records.RULE_NAME evidence) ranks IDENTITY_AGREES and sorts above every keyword tier, and the sentence behind each suggestion says which of the three the name check answered. The name then stays OUT of the strength slot: it is on every candidate of the row and at the strongest tier there is, so counting it there too would give them all one minimum and leave the keyword tiers ordering nothing. A veto is told from a confirmation by the row's code (entry.code == NAMES_ANOTHER_RETURN.code, decision 190) - because on a vetoed row the RULE_NAME evidence carries the OTHER return's spelling and a missed veto would say the page names this return's person; the other return's label is then read back off the row's own reason through records.as_pattern, anchored on the escaped spelling and greedy to the sentence's fixed tail so a return name holding a parenthesis is read whole, as filer.moved_to reads a path back off one: the spelling is the evidence and a label is not evidence of anything. Decision 190: _name_said tells a veto and an absent name by entry.code, and _refusals_for adds the row's own refusal by entry.code (reasons.BY_CODE); _label_of still reads the other return's label off the firm's sentence, once the code has said it is that sentence.
- **`tracker/rollover.py`** — Builds a returning client's next-year request list from their prior engagement's record. Prior-year data always wins; the template may only fill blanks. The rows it builds are recorded into next year's engagement by manifest.create_engagement() - the API's rollover and this module's CLI both do that - and last year's unfiled files are reported once, in the reply and on the command line. Since decision 142 the catalog rows the client never had are added as not asked (they were offered, not added), whether a row is asked and whether it is named both carry, and a not-asked row that received a document is asked next year. Since decision 126 it also rolls a whole household: roll_household() takes the household's one open year (open_year_returns()), rolls every ReturnPlan into the target year one at a time and retires every open-year return nobody ticked with one details edit, answering with a HouseholdRollover of what rolled, what refused and what was retired.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.rollover`

Nothing was rolled.', `ROLLOVER_NOT_RETIRED` = 'Rolled into {year}: {rolled}. Retired: {retired}. Not retired: {left} ({why}); retire those in the editor (Active: no) so the household has one open year', `LINK_NOT_CARRIED` = "The link '{link}' was not carried into the new year: it is not a web address (http:// or https://). Paste the inbox's link into the household's or the return's details."

  - note: Years shift as a set so relative periods stay right. Counts learn from what arrived and never shrink. Override.NOT_APPLICABLE carries forward under its own origin (ORIGIN_NOT_APPLICABLE) with NOT_APPLICABLE_NOTE - last year's label and 'decide afresh' - printed by the CLI after the carried and new rows under PREVIOUS_NOT_APPLICABLE_HEADING and grouped by the app's returning-client page, never back in the active list (decision 116; decision 10 stands); Accepted does not, and neither does its reason. The CLI's form template comes from tracker.templates, so this module and tracker.api do not import each other. Derived year checks are left blank on the rolled rows; the shifted Period derives them again when the list is validated. Decision 67: a template row is the prior's row whatever its case, as validated() compares identifiers. Decision 69: roll_forward() refuses a target year not after the prior's. Decision 72: and one outside YEAR_MIN..YEAR_MAX, through manifest.check_tax_year(), as the wizard's box does. Decision 86: carry_engagement_info() carries the form the prior was cut from into next year's details - a returning client files the same return - and carries a blank as a blank. Decision 103: last year is read from the record (load_manifest() lays the keywords a filing taught over the row's typed ones), so a taught keyword reaches _carry() as a keyword like any other and lands in next year's list as an ordinary Any Keyword - the one moment a taught word becomes something typed, and a learned row would be invisible in the editor. Decision 104: the Carried Forward sheet is not written - the workbook it was written into is gone, and the writer is set aside outside the tree; an offer a person wants is added later in the app's editor. The prior year is read and never written. Decision 108: the command line takes page.tolerant_console() first (its report carries an arrow a cp1252 console cannot encode, and it used to die after the record was written and before the folders were made, with a second run refused), and does all of its work - create_engagement(), then scaffold_engagement() when asked - before it prints a line, so nothing about the report can leave a folder with a record and no scaffold. Decision 123: with_default_dates() lives here, beside the carry rule that clears the two dates, so both ways of building next year's engagement fill them - the command line wraps carry_engagement_info() in it (the form the prior recorded, else the one asked for, and the target year) and tracker.api imports it for create and rollover; the defaulting used to live in the API alone, and the command line's engagements came out with no Due Date at all. Decision 126: roll_household() is the household's loop and roll_forward() stays the primitive it calls, so one return still rolls on its own; each rolled return is created under its own lock by create_engagement() and a refusal on one (an existing target, the path limit through filer.refuse_a_path_past_the_limit(), a year not after the prior's) lands in HouseholdRollover.skipped with its sentence and undoes none of the others. A return that was ticked is never retired by the loop - rolled, its successor's Rolled From retires it; refused, it is still this year's work. The client's side is laid out once at the end (scaffold_household()), so the inbox README lists the new year's lists the day the firm rolls. The CLI carries both forms in one __main__, told apart by store.kind() - a household folder takes --year with --all or --only and prints ROLLED / NOT ROLLED / RETIRED, a return folder is the per-return form unchanged. Decision 137 (L5): carried_link() drops a household link that is not a web address with LINK_NOT_CARRIED (RolloverReport.link_dropped), rather than refusing the roll; the API carries it to the app. Decision 144: _carry() carries short_title (years shifted); a blank one takes the template row's only while the document is still the template's. Decision 177: a return rolls forward where it sits - _roll_one and the command line compute the target from the household being rolled and the prior's folder name, never from the names its record carries, and write those names into next year's record; the command line prints the prior's NAME_DISAGREES as a WARNING line. Decision 188: a rolled return is unique by the layout's key in the target household-year (households.return_name_taken), and the command line's --only reads a return by name_key. Decision 188: the CLI reads its folder through door.household_dir, else door.return_dir, so a folder in the client tree is neither whatever journal is in it. Decision 188 (part 3): roll_household and both forms of the command line refuse a paused household (households.household_pause) before anything is written. Decision 159 (part 2), amending 126: roll_household() is all-or-nothing - every ticked return is planned and validated, every lock taken first (an ExitStack), one refusal rolls none (NOTHING_ROLLED) and a failure part-way undoes what rolled. Retirement comes last and re-reads rows and details under the held lock; a failed retirement after every roll raises RolledNotAllRetired (ROLLOVER_NOT_RETIRED, heading NOT_ALL_RETIRED_HEADING), because the next roll cannot finish it. Scaffold and README refresh run whenever anything rolled. save_rules is called with lock_held=True under the held locks. Ported onto decision 188: roll_household's plan (_plan_one) asks 188's uniqueness by the layout's key (households.return_name_taken) and the path limit, so a taken name or a path past the limit refuses the whole roll in 188's sentence before any lock or write; two ticked returns into one name are one by name_key. A name the layout refuses (LayoutError) is the plan's refusal too, with 'Nothing was rolled.'. Decision 190 (C-13): _unfiled_last_year keys each never-filed row by pbc_location (then digest), not by the client's file name, and quotes a Reason that no longer carries the subfolder.
- **`tracker/router.py`** — Decides which single manifest row a dropped file belongs to. Evidence order: required keywords, then any-keywords/period, read off a text layer or off OCR (OCR routes on required keywords only). There is no third tier: a file name is never evidence for a filing (decision 92), and a document nothing could be read out of parks. The router knows no person (decision 128): whose document this is is asked by the household pass against the return's own people list, not here.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.router`
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/reasons.py`, `tracker/records.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tracker/filer.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/door.py`, `tracker/layout.py`, `tracker/page.py`
  - enforces: `rule:nothing-is-guessed`
  - tested by: `tests/test_router.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_records.py`, `tests/test_review.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`
  - note: Reads the document through content_check.extract() - the scanner's reading - and leaves its per-row verdicts among the engagement's verdicts in the store (content_check.ContentCache) keyed by content, so the scan finds them under the working copy's name. Every scan with no text layer is OCR'd, whatever its name says, and OCR text routes only on required keywords - an any-keyword match on OCR text is OCR_ONLY, a lead for a person, because a misread word is how a document lands under the wrong request. One PdfVerdictCache per file (or the caller's) so a PDF is parsed once, not once per row. The CLI (python -m tracker.router <engagement> <files>) says where each file would go and why, moving nothing. Extension alone never routes. A document matching one row's required keywords but failing its other rules is contested and blocks its own filing — misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it. When nothing routes, the reason is the most useful one available: a document whose content fits a row that refused the file (size floor, type, unreadable PDF) is reported as CONTESTED_PREFIX, and a file every row refused for the same reason carries that reason. A file name is read the same whole-token way a keyword is, run-together spelling and all (W2 for W-2), but only ever as evidence for a person. Eligibility is has_routing_rules(): keywords or a typed year; a year derived from Period only checks a document a keyword already matched. Decision 55, as decision 92 left it: a text layer extract() marked needs_ocr is no text at all, so a multi-page scan is read no further than a one-page one - and where 55 then filed it on its name, it now parks. Decision 58: no run-together fallback; the keyword pattern already reads a dash or space as optional. Decision 73: a row whose any-keywords all matched and whose year alone failed is remembered as a lead, and a file that would otherwise be parked with 'matched no request' is parked as 'looks like J01 (expected period not found ...)' with J01 as its candidate - the sentence a contested file gets, so the reminder asks the client about the period. A lead pre-empts no filing, unlike a required-keyword match, so the decision is exactly as it was; only the reason and the candidates improve. The Routing record and EVIDENCE_CONTENT live in tracker/records.py (decision 100) and are re-exported here for one release: the decision is a record, this module is the deciding. Decision 82: Routing.evidence_record is why, beside Routing.evidence, the tier the decision rested on - EVIDENCE_CONTENT or nothing, since decision 92 removed EVIDENCE_FILENAME (nothing rests on a name; content_check.RULE_FILENAME, the word an index row actually carries, is untouched and still produced). Keyed by candidate identifier: the content check's own Evidence tuple for a row that was read, _filename_evidence() for what the name said (a name is all title and has no page), and _refusal_evidence() for a tier-2 refusal, which travels as reasons.Reason.code rather than the sentence a person reads. _recorded_for() cuts it down to the identifiers the decision names, because every row considered leaves something behind and one index cell must not carry the whole manifest's workings. It decides nothing: every verdict is reached exactly as it was before there was a record. Decision 84: a blocked file - content fits a row, the same row's tier-2 rules refused the file - keeps the verdict's evidence beside the refusal in record, because the refusal alone says which rule said no and never which request the document looked like. The verdict was already read there to decide the file was blocked, so nothing is computed twice and no placement moves. Decision 117: a tier-2 refusal on a file nothing could be read out of - a locked PDF, an empty upload - is asked what its NAME says, exactly as an unreadable scan is, and the name's evidence is recorded beside the refusal for the person who has to open it (and for the reminder's hold, which reads the review shortlist). The decision does not move an inch: no candidate, the same reason, nothing filed on a name. Decision 92, the owner's (2026-09-18): A DOCUMENT NOBODY CAN READ IS FILED BY NOBODY. The by-name tier is gone - when no word of the file could be read (a scan with no text layer OCR could not rescue, an image-only PDF, an empty sheet) no row is a candidate, and the file parks with reasons.NO_READABLE_TEXT (router.UNREADABLE), which is deliberately not UNMATCHED: nothing was matched against anything, and the fix is OCR or a person, never another keyword. _filename_evidence() stays and is recorded on the parked row, so review.triage() offers the request the name points at at RULE_STRENGTH's weakest tier and the app's card and the Status Report show it - a place for a person to start reading, never a filing. _read() no longer skips OCR for a sensibly named scan: nothing is filed on a name, so OCR is the only thing that can still file one, and the scan whose name says W-2 is exactly the one whose content must be read (the _filename_hit shortcut went with the skip). The cost was stated and accepted: until OCR was installed every scanned PDF parked (since decision 169 the reader ships in the app) - twelve rows of the firm's own corpus moved from filing to parking, and two the name had been misfiling now park instead. Decision 93 (a row per issuer): an issuer row is an ordinary row carrying the entity's name in Required Keywords, and which row wins needed no new rule - a required keyword is the strongest tier and the generic K-1 row has none, so the issuer row takes the K-1 that names it. The one rule added is the park: when any row narrows the row that accepted a document (manifest.narrowing_rows over the rows this pass considers, so an issuer row set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE is nobody's issuer) and none of the narrowing rows matched, nothing is filed - reasons.ISSUER_NOT_NAMED, the narrowing rows named, shortlist led by the row that did accept it. Filing on the generic row would put two entities' K-1s in one folder; taking the row left over would be guessing by elimination. Decision 107: whether a page counts two forms as its own is content_check.own_forms(), the same reading the scanner's miss path makes; computed once in route_file() and handed to evaluate_rules() for the ordinary reading and to the split alike, so a page that prints two forms' own names never files on a third form it merely mentions (decision 94's rule, by construction); the forms are then taken in first-mention order (self_named_forms) for the filing order, and _multi_form() decides exactly as before. Decision 105: the split's verdicts are remembered too. _multi_form() takes route_file()'s keep closure and calls it for every row it files a copy under, with the second reading's verdict, after the ordinary reading has left its own refusal - the verdict the router files on is the one the scan must find, or the second copy fails validation on the next pass and the client is asked for a form they already sent. A page that parks keeps nothing new. Decision 128 gave route_file() a `reading` argument in place of `text`: the household pass reads each drop once (read_once()) and routes that one Extraction against every return it feeds, so a two-return household costs one reading rather than two, and from_ocr travels with it so decision 50's stricter rule still applies. Decision 127 changed no rule here: a photo arrives with from_ocr set, so decision 50's stricter reading applies to it unchanged, and route_file() only became two functions - itself, which makes the two refusals that must come before any reading (a cloud placeholder is never read, a Google stub is never a document) and then stamps Routing.seconds on whatever _decide() returns, and _decide(), which is the whole decision as it was. The seconds decide nothing; they let the pass name its slowest documents. Decision 137: route_file() parks a file past validators.MAX_READ_MB before any reading, with reasons.TOO_LARGE as its whole reason, and a parked file read from a cut text says so (reasons.TEXT_CUT). Decision 141: a signed return of the wrong year - a row asks_for_a_return() whose required keywords matched and whose only failure is its period - contests and parks even when another row matched strongly (this year's 1065 with its K-1s, a 1040 with a W-2G stapled behind it); return rows only, checked before the ordinary contested rule. DECISION 140: a read document that reaches the last exit (UNMATCHED) still points somewhere when a row's own form number is shown on the page - a RULE_REQUIRED/RULE_ANY evidence whose term content_check.form_key() reads as a form, said in the title, or on the first page (dominant) AND beside at least one more of the row's own keywords - dominance alone is not enough, a misread K-1's two 'W-2 wages' lines make W-2 dominant (_shows_its_form_number) - or, where no row's is, when the file's name says a row's keyword (_filename_evidence, the unreadable scan's hint): _near_miss() parks it with reasons.SHOWS_ITS_FORM_NUMBER (or, on the name's path, reasons.NAME_POINTS_AT - its own sentence, 'file name', because the page showed nothing) and those rows as the evidence record, NEVER as candidates, so a list where that row is the only one still parks. Only rows whose tier-2 rules let the file through are asked. A01's three required phrases were deliberately not loosened: every looser rule filed the W-3 family and the W-2c as W-2s. The split's self-named forms are self_named, no longer a reuse of the file-name list named. Decision 146: a broker's consolidated 1099 that several rows accept on their any-keywords files whole under the one row accepted BECAUSE OF its 1099-B section (_explained_by over the evidence, never an identifier; content_check.carries_a_1099b_section says the page carries one), after the issuer rule and never on OCR's word; two such rows or none and it parks. The other asked rows that accepted it ride on Routing.answers - no copy - and become the filed row's Also Answers cell. Reads no word of a document since decision 189. read_once(path, questions) is the router's one judge_bounded call per drop, asked about every considered row (questions_for) plus the filer's name questions. _decide and _multi_form read the Judgment (row verdicts, required_matched, any_matched, own, self_named, carries_1099b, has_words) where they read words; _required_matched moved to content_check as required_matched. route_file takes judgment= from the pass or reading= from a tool, which it judges in-process with judgment_of. A stopped or crashed judgment is kept under every considered row's fingerprint and the open-test fingerprint (_keep_the_stop, ruling 3.4), as the scanner already kept it; a transient one never is. _filename_evidence still reads only the file's name. Decision 190: 'could not read it (...)' carries Extraction.error, which is a class or a firm sentence, never a parser's words. Decision 190: every Routing carries code - a Reason's, or reasons.*_CODE for its own sentences (UNMATCHED etc. are now aliases of reasons'); a contested row's is the most specific refusal's (first_of); the 'matched no request; <refusal>' row takes the refusal's code and 'could not read it' the reading's. _refusal_evidence takes the tier-2 code; the reading exits, the HEIC cache skip, the period checks and the one-type sentence compare codes.

Reads each document through content_check.extract(), the same reading the router made of it as a drop, and usually finds the router's verdict already among the engagement's verdicts in the store; one PdfVerdictCache per scan. _resolve_status() is the status rule and _received_date() the Received-Date rule, named so _scan_item() reads as the three tiers and then the two decisions. A Received row whose Expected Count was raised says so instead of REGRESSION_FILES_CHANGED - decided on the pass the row leaves Received, when the record's count is still the Received one, and carried from the last note by _regression_why() on every pass after, because the regressed count would call every lost file a raised count (decision 108); a note with no regression sentence reads as REGRESSION_FILES_CHANGED. An Accepted row is written Received with a date (decision 33); ScanReport.summary is the one count. No Unfiled sheet: the index records parked files; ScanReport.warnings names loose files and unrecognised folders in Prepared/, and ScanReport.summary is summarize() over the rows as the scan leaves them. Decision 54's claim now rests on the record: the Received Date the last scan stamped is carried, not re-stamped, and a regression is measured from the status the record holds, because that is where a status is. Decision 103: _record_the_statuses() is the one write - one call, one transaction, and nothing at all when the pass found the engagement as it left it (ScanReport.recorded says how many). The scan calls filer.ensure() first, inside its own lock, so the store holds the engagement it is about to record to and the rules it works from are the ones the record holds (decision 104: the ones the app's editor last saved). Nothing but the record is written by a pass. Decision 58: a working copy the index says a person filed (ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON) is counted without the content rules (ACCEPTED_NOTE); the scan reads the index for that, and writes only the record and the engagement's verdicts in the store. Decision 60: a person's acceptance is the newest row for the location and its recorded bytes. Decision 62: a person's filing waives tier 2 too. Imports the filer's index reader at call time; the filer imports this module at call time inside _rescan() - the deliberate cycle, stated on the filer's node. Decision 109: the scan reads the index once (_the_index()) and acts on what the filer's sweep decided under the same lock - it writes no row of its own. _wandered() is the paths FILE_MOVED rows name as their copies' whereabouts, and _scan_item() drops those from a request's files before the tiers, because a mislaid copy is not the request's whatever its bytes say; _claimed_paths() is every working copy the record names, newest row per location, and a claimed path holding other bytes is _a_stranger_at(), written as reasons.COPY_CHANGED on the row and by _changed_copy_warnings() on ScanReport.warnings (decision 3 extended; since decision 155 such a copy is NOT counted - a working copy whose bytes disagree with its original is treated as not there, so a torn copy never makes a request Received and the firm-side note keeps the letter from asking the client). A FILE_MOVED row whose home is a place this request's copies sit (directly in Prepared, named for it) writes reasons.FILE_MOVED. Both facts go in before the failures, so the note's cut can never take a firm-side marker off the end, and neither is a failure - a moved copy leaves the request Missing, not Failed Validation. _filed_by_a_person() and the de-duplication hash through ContentCache.digest_of() now, so this module holds no sha256_of at all, and prune() keeps every file under Prepared/ rather than only what a request claims - a memo dropped for a parked copy or a stray was a file read again every pass. the pattern helper moved down to tracker/records.py as as_pattern(), where both readers of a written sentence share it; the regression read-back of decision 108 is unchanged. Decision 119: _interrupted() is the second thing the scan keeps out of a request's count - where a step that died half way was putting a working copy, and the sentence the row it parked carries. The wreck of a copy the power cut in half is nobody's document, so it is not counted and the row's own firm-side sentence goes on the request instead, which is what makes the request read Missing rather than Failed Validation for a document the client sent perfectly well. Decision 146: _answered() reads each Filed / File Moved row's Also Answers cell, and a request a consolidated statement answers counts it as one document per section that answered it (records.answer_count), with reasons.IN_CONSOLIDATED on its notes and no file of its own read; a person takes one back with filer.mark_missing_again (one answer_withdrawn_by_person row event). Decision 168: a request's files are assign_files()'s - the files directly in Prepared whose names belong to it - checked by validators.check_files(); NO_REQUEST_FOLDER and FOLDERS_NOTE are gone and a request with nothing is simply Missing; the warnings are UNCLAIMED_FILE (a file whose name begins with no identifier) and reasons.PERSONS_FOLDER (each folder other than the review folder, once per pass). Decision 157: _scan_item says reasons.COPY_MISSING of a claimed copy under the request's name that is absent on a row that is not File Moved (the sweep could not make it again this pass), and reasons.COPY_AND_ORIGINAL_GONE instead of reasons.FILE_MOVED for a filer.both_gone() row - both firm-side, so a missing copy is never a client ask by itself. _answered(engagement_dir, rows, cache) carries why a consolidated host is not counted (_host_not_counted: its copy missing, not the one filed, nowhere, or gone with its original; a wanderer or a placeholder still counts), and an answer from such a host counts nothing and says reasons.ANSWER_NOT_COUNTED (ANSWERED_BY, the ANSWER_WHY_* words) in place of IN_CONSOLIDATED. Decision 189: scan_engagement() saves the verdict cache after each request (a no-op when nothing changed), so a pass killed mid-scan reads again only what it was killed on. Decision 189 (the bounded household, ruling 2.2): scan_engagement(deadline=) sets it on the scan's ContentCache for the loop, and only a cache miss past it stops the scan (content_check.OutOfTime, raised before a judgment starts): a request whose verdicts are all kept is scanned whatever the time; from the first request that would read, no further request is scanned or recorded - each keeps the status the record holds - and ScanReport.unreached counts them. Decision 189 (the judgment worker): the open test on a cache miss (content_check.open_verdict(path, cache, item)) judges the working copy's own row in the same child job; the content check that follows takes the held Judgment, so a working copy costs one trip to the child, and the scanner holds no document text (it held up to 8 whole texts before). Decision 190: each failure travels as (note, code), the firm-side-first sort reads the code, and the StatusUpdate carries note_codes - the codes of the facts that say a cause, in the facts' order; an interrupted row's note is Said with the row's own code. A person's filing (_filed_by_a_person) is read from the row's code (reasons.ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON_CODE), not the start of its Reason (decision 190's Part 2 review, S-1); _regression_why is one of the firm-tail readers tests/test_reasons.py names in TAIL_READERS. P219 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): a scan works out each name's owner once (an owners dict per scan behind belongs_to), and its progress line's step is progress.SCAN_STEP.

The review fixes: schedule_decision returns UNNAMED_HOST (HOST_UNNAMED) before reading the file when this computer's own name is not a HOST_NAME; every comparison with this computer is locking.is_this_host; _host_name() is private and each caller says its whole sentence; claim() creates the file with O_EXCL and answers a file made meanwhile by what it says; move_here() returns Moved(before, unreadable) so a move over garbage says MOVED_FROM_UNREADABLE. Not in resolve_data_home or default_data_home: the suite always names a data home and the tripwire must still learn the real place without a probe. Rejected: asking Windows for package identity (the redirected process has none) and comparing file IDs (blind until a redirected write has made the copy). R2: redirected_copies() lists every existing Packages\*\LocalCache\Local\<DATA_HOME_NAME> (Windows, read-only, none with no Packages folder or with ENV_DATA_HOME set) for api._machine_warnings' REDIRECTED_COPY sentence; the app never removes one (client-derived, decision 186), and it is not runner.left_behind's 'beside the program'. Combined review (S2, N3): R1's refusal is its own class, DataHomeRedirected (a SettingsError), so api._machine_warnings says R1's sentence alone, with no REDIRECTED_COPY line calling the folder the process sees 'never used'; a Packages folder Windows will not list (any OSError but absent or not a folder) is a SettingsError with PACKAGES_UNREADABLE from _package_names, naming the folder and errors.error_class (imported at call time, so the load-time imports stay layout and fsio), never a raw PermissionError: the probe then refuses the data home (it cannot rule a redirect out) and still removes its file, and _machine_warnings says the sentence once and shows the rest. P207 (pilot/SPEC-scale-1000.md): one_household() holds the same answers for one household of a pass while the pass writes; _HOLDING says which hold is under way (HOLD_READING refuses a write, HOLD_HOUSEHOLD does not); inside a household resolved(path) holds only a path that is there (os.path.lexists), and _write refuses inside a household's hold (WRITE_WHILE_HOLDING), so a setter never writes back the held copy over a save the app made meanwhile. Nested holds are the outer one. P215 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): held(key, answer, *, there=None) replaces _held - an answer kept for a reading, and for a household's hold only once there resolves to a held answer; never an error. Its callers: app_dir, the program folders and data_home here, and the store's engagement key and held_read.
- **`tracker/store.py`** — The store: one SQLite file per account, every row keyed by its clients root (STORE_FILENAME) in the tracker's data home on the designated machine (decision 186), holding engagements, requests, statuses, learned_keywords, documents and events for every engagement under that root, all folded from the journal and from nothing else - and, since decision 107, the two tables of the tier-3 verdict cache, VERDICTS_TABLE and FILE_MEMOS_TABLE, which are NOT the record's: derived from the bytes and the rules, never journalled, left empty by a rebuild and never compared by check(). Owns the file name, the schema and its user_version (bumped by decision 104 when the workbook digest column left, by 107 when the cache's two tables arrived, by 116 for override_reason, by 117 for the Filing Deadline column and by 119 for the intents table), store_path(), open(), connect() / close() (one connection per process, to the file TRACKER_STORE names or the one in the data home), documents(), rules(), statuses(), learned_keywords() and engagement_info() (what the readers answer from), record() (the journal first, then one immediate transaction), sync(), catch_up() and follow_the_journal() (replay the lines the store has not applied, building the engagement from the journal alone where it has none; catch_up() is filer.ensure()'s, by count, and a look that finds nothing to apply takes no lock), rebuild_engagement() (delete and build again from the journal), cached_verdicts() and remember_verdicts() (the verdict cache's one read and one write - the write is its own immediate transaction under the engagement lock, never record()), forget() (drop a failed create's row), check() (every disagreement with the journal, as sentences), state() (current / behind / unknown, from the journal's head alone), export() (three CSVs on demand, every cell text, a cell that begins like a formula behind an apostrophe) and the CLI that rebuilds, checks, exports or states a whole clients root - its first argument read by store_named(): the app folder, the settings file in it, or the store file itself, and anything else refused so a typo never creates a store; a store open() refuses is said in its one sentence with exit 1, never a traceback (decision 107).
