WHERE IT LIVES IS THE POINT: in the data home (decision 186: settings.data_home(), never beside the program, in a checkout, on removable media or in the temp folder; path_for() is gone and store_path() is the one answer), never under the clients root and never in an engagement folder, because those sync and a synced database file is a corrupted one - decision 87's finding, kept, with the owner's 2026-09-19 decision adding the local database the other side of that line. The journal stays in the folder and travels with the engagement; the store is local and disposable, and the arrow only points one way - the store is rebuilt from the journal, never the reverse. THE GUARANTEE is journal-then-apply: record() refuses outside the engagement lock and refuses a retired event name by sentence, appends each event through append() and only then folds them in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a machine that dies between the two leaves the journal ahead and sync() replays the difference. The fold has one owner, apply() in tracker/ledger.py, so a line-at-a-time replay and a whole-file fold cannot differ. ONE CONNECTION PER PROCESS: connect() opens it on first use and every writer deep in the package asks for it by name; close() lets it go, which Windows needs before a database file can be deleted. TRACKER_STORE overrides where it is - the suite points every test at its own file. It imports records, ledger and locking and nothing else of the package at load time - narrower than its layer allows, so the database the readers answer from never depends on the modules that walk folders and move files; connect() reads tracker/settings.py at call time and the CLI imports the registry at call time to find the folders. The gate is check(), run by the autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py over every engagement the suite leaves behind: the documents and the rules are compared with ledger.replay() over the journal, always - an engagement with no rules event has none on either side - and the statuses and taught keywords with the same lines folded by the store's case rule (decision 136). Decision 104: the requests table is the fold of rules_changed (and of the rules_imported lines older journals carry, which _apply_rules_event folds the same way); rules() returns [] for an engagement the store holds and None only for one it does not; has_rules_event() is what a save is a difference from; rebuild_engagement() takes nothing but the journal (the workbook-fed fallback, the sequence number workbook rows were marked with, the digest column and its bookkeeping all went, and the schema guard that refused a request row whose fields had moved is a test in tests/test_store.py now); state() has one stamp, the journal's head, because a rules edit is an event; forget() is what a failed create leaves behind - nothing - and writes nothing to any journal. A version-1 file is refused by the sentence open() has always had, and is deleted and rebuilt: the store is disposable and no store at the office predates this chain. key_root() is the one rule for the key an engagement is stored under (root_for() is its name for a caller with no root in hand): the root the settings file names whenever the folder is under it - the record's own root, which wins over the root a caller typed, so a pass run on one client's folder and a check given the drive key the engagement as the app does - else the caller's root, else the root a return's position names (decision 134: four levels up, when its parent is a year folder and its household sits in the private tree, asked of layout at call time - so two years of one return are two rows on a machine or in a reader with no root in hand), else, only for a folder outside that layout, the folder's parent. _engagement_row() answers by that exact key, and under the recorded root by nothing else: a folder there with no row is one the store has not met, never another engagement whose key its path ends with (decision 106; the pre-integration audit found Clients/Archive/Smith 2025 answered as Clients/Smith 2025's row). The tail - the one stored path the folder ends with, longest wins - answers only where no recorded root covers the folder, which is decision 103's end-to-end finding on a machine with no settings file. Decision 107: the verdict cache's two tables are per engagement and cascade with it; cached_verdicts() returns the memos and the verdicts at the CACHE_VERSION the caller names as plain dicts and JSON text (this module never learns the verdict's record - test_layers pins that it imports nothing above it); remember_verdicts() deletes the rows at other versions, the paths and digests pruned, and upserts what was learned, refusing outside the lock and for an unknown engagement by the two sentences record() uses (_held_under_the_lock()). A version-2 file is refused by the same sentence a version-1 file was. RULE_COLUMNS is built from records.RULE_FIELDS; _rule_from_sql() hands the list fields back as lists and the flag as a boolean, the shape the API hands the editor. Decision 115: last_event() answers the newest event of a name for an engagement (or the newest carrying a key) from the events table - what the reminder compares this week's draft with, and what the runner reads the last draft day from. Decision 112: document_seqs() reads back what _apply() has always written - which journal line last wrote each index row - keyed through the recorded root as documents() is, {} for an engagement the store does not hold, no lock (a read). It is the freshness handle the app carries out with the row and a person's action carries back; per row rather than the engagement's head, so a scan between the card and the click refuses nothing. A rebuild numbers the same lines the same way, so the mapping survives it. Decision 113: _apply() deletes a learned_keywords row on a keyword_unlearned event, keyed by identifier_key and the keyword exactly, as the insert keys it; _check_learned() holds the table to ledger.Folded.learned - the table's words in seq order against the journal's fold, both sides folded through identifier_key first, one sentence per request that differs - and check() appends it, so the one part of this database the record could not vouch for is in the gate. _refuse_a_malformed_line() checks a keyword event for the first time: both events must name a request and a word, both text and neither blank, because a keyword that is not text was written into the table as the text of whatever it carried while the journal's fold kept the value itself, which is a disagreement the check would now report and nobody could act on. Decision 119: SCHEMA_VERSION 6 and the intents table - the fold of the moving lines, one row per key, holding the whole line - written by _apply() as each line is met and deleted by any row event naming the key (or by move_abandoned); open_intents() reads them back oldest first for the filer's recovery and for the refusal a person's action makes while one is open; _check_intents() holds the table to ledger.replay()'s own fold, so a rebuild gives the same open set and the gate would say which key they disagreed about; _refuse_a_malformed_line() learns the moving shape, because a recovery acts on it with a file already half moved, and (decision 126) the sharing_confirmed shape, which is no shape at all: that event carries nothing but its stamp, so a line of it carrying anything is another version's or a hand-written one and is refused by name rather than kept where a reader would trust it. The store's version did not move for it - it is folded by nothing and read back out of the events by last_event(). Version 8 (decision 128) added the return's people to engagements as JSON text and the named mark to requests; _to_sql writes a list with sorted keys, as the journal writes a line, so the column and the fold of the same people are one text and check() compares like with like. A rules_changed line whose people this version cannot read - an unknown kind, a one-word spelling - is refused by name before a value of it reaches a table. Decision 129 put the household's feed list into the household columns as JSON text and moved the schema to version 9; the malformed-line guard learned the feeds' shape. Decision 132 moved the schema to version 10 with no column change, because the fold changed: a released line (ledger.RELEASE_EVENTS) deletes the row under its key and closes its intent in _apply(), exactly as ledger.apply() does, and a version-9 file may hold Handed Over rows this version never produces. The guard requires a released line's key and refuses a row on it, and refuses a moving line carrying decision 129's also_in by name (ALSO_IN) - an intent whose second half this version cannot write must not be recovered as if it had none. Decision 134 moved the schema to version 11 with no column change, because the key changed: a version-10 file may hold two years of one return as one row, keyed by the return's name alone. DECISION 135, A READ NEVER OUTRUNS A WRITE: readers take no lock and the app's process and the pass's share the store, so every function that applies journal lines reads the row, the lines and the head inside its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE and takes the lines and the head from ONE read (ledger.read_with_head()): sync(), catch_up() (follow_the_journal()'s slow path and filer.ensure()'s) and record()'s apply through one helper, _catch_up(), and rebuild_engagement() through the same one read. A look that finds nothing to apply takes no lock: sync() and catch_up() first read the row and the journal outside any transaction and return when the applied seq already equals the journal's lines, and only a decision to write takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE and reads both again inside (_look_then_catch_up(); the look's parsed lines are reused there only when the file still digests to the look's head) - so the app's views, the Status Report and dry runs never queue a pass's record() behind the lock. A stored head therefore always names exactly the lines applied. record() applies what the journal holds past the store's applied_seq as it is inside the transaction, not the batch it was handed. follow_the_journal()'s head fast path stays outside any transaction and parses nothing; filer.ensure() calls catch_up(), which compares by count, so a store an earlier build left with a matching head and a short applied_seq (the stuck return: current by its head, every writer refused) is repaired by the next pass with no rebuild and no version change. Decision 136: check() folds the record's statuses and learned keywords from the journal's lines itself, keyed by identifier_key in journal order (_recorded_statuses, _recorded_learned), rather than taking ledger.replay()'s, which keys them by each line's spelling - so a request respelled by case is one request to the gate, as it is to the store. Decision 137 (L4): MALFORMED_LINE says "line N of the record is malformed"; _refuse_a_malformed_line() gained the ROW_EVENTS branch (a key that is text, a row that is a mapping, a was that is a location) and holds every rule's list fields to lists of words; _write_rule() and _rule_from_sql() hold them to the same shape where a row is written and read. Decision 137 (A3, store version 12): engagements.applied_digest holds the running chain over exactly the lines applied (ledger.read_with_chain / chain_at); _refuse_a_rewrite() proves that prefix in _look_then_catch_up's no-lock look (equal counts with a different chain refuses, never 'nothing to do'), in _catch_up, and in record() before it appends, with REWRITTEN; check() names it; the rebuild computes it. It never repairs itself: the check, then a rebuild. Decision 138: _apply() writes a batch's statuses from _recorded_statuses(events) - one row per identifier_key, the last scan's status, the seq from status_seqs - not from ledger.Folded.statuses, which is keyed by the exact spelling and, written in insertion order, left the second of A01, a01, A01 standing on a rebuild, a sync()/catch_up() top-up or one record() of several scans. The writer and check() now read the one rule; Folded.statuses is unchanged (ledger cannot fold case) and nothing written or shown reads it. SCHEMA_VERSION 14 (decision 143): the documents table gained container. Decision 189 (A-9): open() hands SQLite a connection factory, _Connection (with _Cursor), the one choke point every statement goes through, so every sqlite3.Error leaves the module as StoreUnavailable(StoreError) with code = the SQLite error's name (SQLITE_ERROR when it has none) and the fixed sentence STORE_UNAVAILABLE; the engine's text stays on __cause__ and is never quoted. Decision 187: _refuse_a_malformed_line(event, seq, where, *, kind) is the one admission - every value by the records value rule (stamp_problem on 'at', rule_row_problem, info_problem, entry_problem, status_problem, household_problem, digests, the drafted stage) and every location by layout.place_problem (asked at call time), labels by layout.segment_problem, a moving line refused in a household's record (kind), and each 'also' event admitted by the same rule. Its phrases name the field and the class, never the value. record() runs it on every event before the first ledger.append ('; nothing was written'), _apply() on every line read in (kind from the engagements row) and check() over every line of every journal, so a line applied under the old gate is named without a rebuild. SCHEMA_VERSION is not bumped: a bump would discard the verdict cache for what check() gives. Decision 187's review: a removal is placed with removes=True (M4); keys, 'was' and locations use records.name_problem (M5); an event name this version does not know is said as UNKNOWN_EVENT and a sharing_confirmed line's extra fields are not named (S2). Decision 188: engagement_path and _recorded_root_over use layout.parts_below and _positional_root asks layout.place_of (all at call time, so store still imports only records, ledger and locking at load); the CLI reads its root through door.checked_root and --engagement through door.return_dir or household_dir. Decision 188 (part 3): the admission gate admits ledger.ACCEPTED_KEY only on RULES_CHANGED and HOUSEHOLD_CHANGED and only with FOLDER_NAME_ACCEPTED, refusing any other use without quoting the value. Decision 188 (part 4, SPEC-162 rulings 5 and 6): a truncated journal is refused with TRUNCATED (restore from Drive's trash or version history first; what a rebuild would discard); check() of an engagement whose journal is gone is one JOURNAL_GONE sentence and gone_journals(conn, root) names every stored engagement under the root whose journal is absent - the CLI's check adds them to the one report beside decision 187's re-judging; only_in_the_store lists the applied lines the journal no longer holds, from the events table, and rebuild_engagement(..., discard=False) raises WouldDiscard (WOULD_DISCARD, with the lines) unless discard, returning what it discarded; the CLI's rebuild lists them and exits 1 until --discard. SCHEMA_VERSION 17 (decision 204): the documents table gained waits_for, and it is the store's FIRST IN-PLACE STEP - _IN_PLACE maps a from-version to the statements that bring it to the next, and open() runs them in one transaction each (16: ALTER TABLE documents ADD COLUMN waits_for TEXT), so a version-16 file keeps its verdict cache. The rule, worded once in the module docstring: only new additive columns that no earlier journal line can carry, each added with no default - NULL, exactly what a rebuild writes for a line without the field, so store check finds nothing after the step (204's original DEFAULT '' did not, and decision 190 made it NULL; a file 204's old step already upgraded keeps its '' cells, so check holds NULL and '' as one value in the columns an in-place step added, _ADDED_IN_PLACE read off _IN_PLACE, and in those only - the port review's S3); every other mismatch is refused, deleted and rebuilt. Decision 159 (part 3): imports checkpoint at load time (tests/test_layers.py). Every catch-up and record() is proved against this machine's checkpoint (_prove_against_checkpoint, which formats _judge(); verify() asks the same _judge(), no copy) before anything is applied - SHORTER, REWRITTEN_SINCE, CLAIMS_THIS_MACHINE, NO_WRITER (and FOREIGN only if checkpoint.foreign_lines_refused() is ever True); before any writer is trusted _judge() asks the admission's rule of the line keys (_line_keys_problem, part of _refuse_a_malformed_line; a refusal is decision 187's MALFORMED_LINE). Carried onto 187: record() admits each event as ledger.line_of() will write it, writer included, at 187's one door; SHARING_CONFIRMED admits LINE_KEYS; verify() runs the admission over every line before it looks at a place or judges a writer (V_MALFORMED); open() and open_read_only() keep 189's _Connection factory. rebuild_engagement() refuses what the checkpoint vouches for and the record no longer holds, and - whatever the checkpoint says, no row included - any line the store holds that the record lacks or holds differently (_only_the_store_holds; REBUILD_WOULD_LOSE), unless recover passes accept_loss; decision 137's REWRITTEN and truncation refusals end with ledger.RUN_RECOVER (replacing decision 184's hand copy of the store: recover exports it first, and conflict copies are never deleted and are named every pass). recover() exports into RECOVERED_DIR beside the store (no export when the store holds nothing; an unreadable record is said on the first look, and the export is named as a restore source only when it covers every line the record still reads - RESTORE_FROM_EXPORT, else NO_USABLE_COPY), lists the differing lines by seq, side, event, time and host (no payload values), and replays only when the return's folder name is typed exactly. verify() is the same comparison firm-wide, read-only (mode=ro), with call-time imports of registry, filer.holds_the_row, layout.locate and validators. record() says its intent from ledger.intended_heads() - the very bytes append writes - and trims it to the lines that reached the file when an append raises. forget() clears the checkpoint's key whether or not the store holds the return. prove_the_root() is the one root proof: only the settings' root claims (the final review's SF1): the runner proves the settings' root (claiming on a real pass) and then the root it walks with claim=False, and the API proves the settings' root (ROOT_NOT_CLAIMED). A checkpoint that will not open is a StoreError naming it (_beside). Hosts compare through locking.is_this_host (any case). An older store is set aside as tracker.db.v<N>.old and rebuilt; the store's version is unchanged by 159. Ported onto 188 and 204: one upgrade policy in open() - _IN_PLACE steps first (16 -> 17), an older version set aside, a newer refused; the checkpoint beside it untouched. rebuild_engagement has one word for an accepted loss, 188's discard (WouldDiscard lists a shorter journal's lines; 159's REBUILD_WOULD_LOSE stands behind it; recover passes discard=True after its export; the CLI's rebuild --discard runs recover's first look first). TRUNCATED is said before the checkpoint's SHORTER and ends with RUN_RECOVER. prove_the_root asks layout.parts_below; the CLI's root and --engagement come through the door for every command, recover and verify included. The port review (M1, S1, S2): rebuild_engagement's discard is passed only by recover after the typed name; the CLI's rebuild --discard needs --engagement and --accept-loss and is recover's path, else refused. WOULD_DISCARD ends with RUN_RECOVER. A recover whose export cannot be written raises EXPORT_NOT_WRITTEN (class and folder), nothing discarded. Decision 192: households(conn) - every household row as it stands, for the card's fed_by; a display, never a writer's source; no schema change. Decision 186: store_named() takes the app folder, its settings folder or its settings file to mean this account's store in the data home, and refuses the old store beside the program by name (OLD_STORE_NAMED) - never opened, so a rebuild can never recreate it; the store in use is never 'old', wherever TRACKER_STORE puts it. A copy inside the app's own folder is refused (COPY_INSIDE_APP), and TRACKER_STORE is held to the data home's checks - a whole path, not inside the program, on a fixed disk - with a SettingsError (STORE_OVERRIDE_*; the review's N4). SCHEMA_VERSION did not change: the location is not the schema, and the new home starts empty. SCHEMA_VERSION 18 (decision 190): documents gained code and subfolder, statuses gained note_codes, in place by the same rule (17: three ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... TEXT), so a version-16 file steps to 17 and then 18 where it stands; tests/test_store.py compares each upgraded file with a rebuild from a journal written before the step, cell for cell. A row's subfolder is admitted only when each backslash-separated part comes back from layout.recorded_subfolder_part unchanged - the one rule the filer writes it by, so '.', '..', a part holding '/', ':' or a control, or one with nothing visible is a name no writer wrote and is refused (decision 190's review of the port, S2: the filer once wrote 'Q1: bank' raw and the admission refused the pass). Not layout.segment_problem: since decision 188 that household-name rule refuses a client's '2025' or '_old' folder.  Decision 209, R3b: SCHEMA_VERSION 19 adds engagements.admitted_by in place (_IN_PLACE[18], default 0, after decision 190's 17->18 step; bookkeeping store check does not compare); ADMISSION_VERSION (2 since the merge with decision 190's refusals) names the admission a row's applied lines were judged by. _catching_up judges every applied line again (_judge_the_applied_lines, from the record's lines) when admitted_by is older, before anything is written, and records the version in the same transaction; the no-lock look in _look_then_catch_up and follow_the_journal's head fast path both fall through to it while a row is not admitted, and record() judges before appending ('nothing was written'). A refusal is MALFORMED_LINE, so the household waits as for a new malformed line. First builds and rebuilds insert admitted_by = ADMISSION_VERSION. A change that makes the admission refuse more raises ADMISSION_VERSION in the same commit; tests/test_store.py walks, by syntax tree, every package function the admission reaches (records, layout, ledger, call-time imports included) and every constant they read, and pins each part's digest to the version, naming the parts that moved. holds() has its owner test. P118: _recorded_root_over, engagement_path and _positional_root resolve through settings.resolved, so inside a reading each spelling is resolved once. Version 20 (pilot P170) adds engagements.household_related in place with the record's own default '[]' (what a rebuild writes), and admission 3 refuses a related list that is not a list of folder names. Speed round (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): P214 - the checkpoint is one connection a command, _held_checkpoint(where) (with _CHECKPOINT, _CHECKPOINT_PATH and _CHECKPOINT_FILE, the per-connection answer of _checkpoint_file), yielded by _beside and used by prove_the_root, foreign_lines and acknowledge_foreign; any CheckpointError drops it (_drop_the_checkpoint) and the next question opens it again; close() closes it first, a failure a warning; record()'s two transactions are unchanged. P215 - _engagement_row asks its key through settings.held, and held_read(conn, engagement_dir, what, build) answers a record's read from memory for one hold only while its token holds: the row's id, path, ledger head, seq, digest, built_at and _REPLACED (a process count of deleted engagement rows, bumped by forget and rebuild_engagement, because a rebuild from the same journal can reuse the id). P219 - has_rules(conn, engagement_dir) says whether a return has a list without building it (registry.engagement_from asks it). tests/test_store.py's admission closure follows a remembered rule through __wrapped__, so the cached layout rules stay in decision 209's pin (ADMISSION_PIN[3] re-pinned, ADMISSION_VERSION unchanged). Pilot P227: read_token(row) is the one definition of a record's read token (id, path, ledger_head, applied_seq, applied_digest, built_at), used by held_read (with what is read and _REPLACED) and the practice page's kept rows; read_tokens(conn, path=None) is every row's token in one SELECT, keyed by stored path; record_key(folder) is _engagement_key's answer under the recorded root, else None (a folder found by its tail is never kept by key).
- **`tracker/templates.py`** — The per-form request catalog (FORM_TYPES, FORM_TEMPLATES): what each return type asks for and the keyword rules that recognise each document. The ONLY source of truth for the checklists; the wizard and the rollover read it directly. Since decision 117 it also holds the dates a form implies: FILING_DEADLINES with filing_deadline_for() (the statutory day in the year after the tax year, weekends shifted forward) and ask_by_for() (TARGET_DAYS_BEFORE_DEADLINE before it, moved back off the weekend).
  - constants: `FORM_LABEL_PATTERN` = 'Form {form}', `BASE_YEAR` = 2025, `PERIOD_PATTERN` = 'TY{year}', `K1_CATALOG` = '1040', `K1_IDENTIFIER` = 'F01', `TARGET_DAYS_BEFORE_DEADLINE` = 5, `YEAR_NOTE` = "Defaults to the most recently ended year; the checklist's periods follow it", `KEYWORD_DEFAULT_NOTE` = 'Defaults to the Document Name'
  - imports: `tracker/manifest.py`
  - used by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`, `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_templates.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_after_install.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_irs_forms.py`, `tests/test_layout.py`, `tests/test_learned_keywords.py`, `tests/test_manifest.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_row_columns.py`, `tests/test_scaffold.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: item_from_spec() gives a rule-less request its own document name as the required keyword, because a request with no rule can never auto-file, and the safe extension default. default_tax_year() is the calendar's most recently ended year; template_items(form, year=...) shifts the catalog's base year to it, relative periods included. No date_pattern in the catalog: each row's Period implies its year check. Decision 60: a catalog keyword is the form's own title or a phrase only it carries, never a word other forms print about it (a 1040 says W-2; a 1095-C says Marketplace). Decision 62: every catalog row keys on the document's own title phrase; tests/test_catalog.py routes reconstructions of the real forms against every catalog. Decision 63: the prior-year return rows require their form number and title, so a return wins over its schedules' lines. Decision 64: the return rows require their title phrase, not their number; the K-1 row keys on the K-1's title; tests/irs/ (the IRS's own forms) and tests/test_irs_forms.py route them all. Decision 65: every prior-year return row requires the jurat; schedule rows key on their titles, not on account names. Decision 66: no row keys on a line every return prints (dividends and distributions, ownership percentage, donation) or the organizer asks (child care provider); the receipt, list and childcare rows key on those documents' own titles. Decision 67: the receipt row does not key on contribution statement (an IRA's, a 529's); the childcare row knows the provider's statement; the estimated tax row keys on a voucher's own lines (its numbered heading, the amount line), not the booklet's prose. Decision 68: the receipt row keys on receipt wording only (a pledge, a thank-you and the firm's letter are not receipts); the estimated tax row knows the state voucher; the childcare row does not take an FSA administrator's statement. Decision 69: the receipt row keys on words only a charity prints; no form 540-es; L01 has no tuition statement (a checklist's line, a university's bill). Decision 72: item_from_spec() reads a spec's lists through manifest.csv_tuple(), the one parser, rather than a copy of it. Decision 73: the shared estimated-tax row is two rows, because an individual's 1040-ES voucher is not a corporation's record (business_estimated_tax keys on corporation estimated tax, estimated tax voucher, estimated payments made); the December bank row does not key on statement of account (a credit-card issuer's and a broker's heading) and takes a workbook, as the reconciliation it asks for arrives; the property tax row keys on the bill's own titles, not on assessor, parcel number or property tax bill (an assessor's notice and a servicer's escrow analysis print those); D01 drops thank you for your donation (every fundraiser's salutation); I01 drops advance payment of premium tax credit (a marketplace notice's sentence); J01 keys on child care/day care spellings with the run-together copies deleted, since the matcher reads the space as optional; 1041 A01 names the kind of trust (an IRA custodian's paperwork is a Trust Agreement too), B02 drops year-end account statement (a bank's heading), C01 drops distribution schedule (a mutual fund's), E01 knows stepped-up basis; 990 C02 keys on the schedule's own title rather than compensation of officers (Part VII's line and the Statement of Functional Expenses', which is now a financial statement's title), D02 on grants made rather than a bare grantee (a letter the charity received) or grants paid (the 990-PF's line 25), E01 without program description (a grant proposal's); the xlsx-only rows and the loans row take the format a client really sends, and officer_comp drops form 1125-e with it (the blank IRS form parks). Decision 85: 1040 E01 knows the wording a broker actually exports - realized gain/loss and the run-together realized gain loss beside the firm's own realized gain and loss - and takes a workbook, since that export arrives as an .xlsx as often as a CSV; 1041 B01 takes the same two, because the trust's realized gain/loss export is its 1099-B by another name. No IRS form in tests/irs/ says either word, and decision 68's consolidated 1099 never prints them, so the composite's placements are untouched. Decision 90, the owner's catalog: _prior_return() writes every prior-year return row's required keyword, with JURAT as the one owner of the line decision 65 added, and a state return's own printed title as an alternative inside that keyword - a standalone CA 540 or NY IT-201 files 1040 B01 on 'resident income tax return', a CA 568 or NY IT-204 files 1065 A01 on 'return of income + limited liability company' (both 568 heading lines, since decision 141) or 'partnership return', a CA 100S files 1120S A01 on 'franchise or income tax return', and another state is one more phrase, not a rule. The alternative lives inside the required keyword rather than in Any Keywords so the row's required set stays required: the prior-year return still outranks a row that matched on any keyword and one that fails another rule is still contested. The 1040 catalog gains A03-A06, one row per 1099 a person receives, keyed on the form's number - 'nonemployee compensation' is said by the IRS Attention page ahead of every information return and 'certain government payments' by the 1040-ES package, so neither is a keyword; 'miscellaneous information' and 'payment card' are, the second because the 1099-K's title never lands on one line and 'payment card' begins it, where a checklist's menu rule can see it. 'depreciation' joins SHARED - the 1120's C02 unchanged, 1120S F02 and 1065 D02 new - so the schedule behind Form 4562 has one set of words; a fixed-asset register that never says depreciation stays on fixed_assets, which all three catalogs already carry. Decision 93: the catalog keeps ONE K-1 row (1040 F01, K1_CATALOG/K1_IDENTIFIER) and it asks for the state K-1 too - California heads Schedule K-1 (568) "Member's Share of Income" - because which partnerships a client is in is a fact about that client, not about the 1040. issuer_row() cuts a row per issuing entity from k1_row(): same Any Keywords, same period and extensions, the normalised entity name in Required Keywords and in the Document. The 1065's F01 is Special Allocation Support; decision 141's H01 closes decision 85's F1 there. Decision 117, the owner's table: each form's statutory filing date lives here because it is a fact about the return type, like the checklist itself, and a form the table does not name gets no default date at all - a guessed deadline would be read out to a client in the firm's name. The weekend shift is the IRS's own rule; a holiday is a person's edit, because the federal and state calendars differ and move. Every catalog row carries a name mark since decision 128 - 61 of the 107 are named - and an issuer row is named because the K-1 row it is cut from is. Decision 141, the owner's rows: 1040 A07 (SSA-1099 / RRB-1099, required on the statements' own headings so it outranks E02, whose 1099-r the SSA's revision code 'SSA-1099-R-OP1' says), A08, A09, L02, L03 (required on the form number), M01 (the client's Schedule C sheet, any keywords on its own vocabulary) and N01; the business catalogs' K-1s received (required on the partner's, beneficiary's and member's K-1 titles, never the S corporation's, which no business can hold and whose title the S-corp return prints), 1099-K / 1099-NEC received and 1042-S rows; the 1041's G01 carries the estimated_tax title but files only a 1041-ES (an individual's 1040-ES parks there), the one row tests/test_templates.py lets carry a shared title with rules of its own; A08 wants the 1099-C's words beside its number, since OCR reads 1099-G as 1099-C; M01 keys on the summary's shape (gross sales + ending inventory + total expense), never a mileage line; and Z01, the notices row, last on every catalog, keyed on the current IRS notice header (notice date with tax year or tax period, with the agency) and narrow on purpose. The 1042-S, K-1-received, business 1099 and notices rows are SHARED entries. Decision 144: every row carries short= (the owner's approved list of 2026-09-24), as short_title in the spec; a SHARED row has one short name on every catalog; issuer_row() sets manifest.issuer_short_title(), K-1 <issuer> cut to twenty characters at a whole word (the owner's Q-B); ISSUER_DOCUMENT now lives in tracker.manifest (read from there, re-exported here) because the derivation of a blank short name recognises an issuer title and gives a hand-added K-1 row the same name. Decision 201: next_issuer_identifier() (the first free identifier in K1_IDENTIFIER's block, without case) and issuer_item() (issuer_row read as a request and shifted to the return's year).

  - tested by: `tests/test_validators.py`

  - note: DECISION 127 - A PHOTO IS A SCAN: IMAGE_EXTENSIONS (jpg, jpeg, png, heic, heif, tif, tiff) is accepted by every request that accepts a PDF, through extension_allowed() (public since decision 147, for the backtest's collect), so no catalog row and no stored rule changed and a request list recorded before the decision admits photos the day it lands; a row that names an image type itself is taken at its word, and a row listing xlsx/csv alone refuses a photo with the sentence it always refused it with. DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS is untouched. At tier 2 a photo gets from _image_error() what a PDF gets from _pdf_error(): Image.open() + verify(), no pixels decoded, nothing written - a file Pillow will not open is reasons.UNREADABLE_IMAGE (the client's to resend), and a HEIC on a machine whose decoder is missing is reasons.HEIC_NOT_SUPPORTED (firm-side, never an ask: they sent an ordinary photo). pillow_heif.register_heif_opener() runs once at import inside a try, and HEIC_READABLE says whether it did; there is no PdfVerdictCache-style memo because verify() reads a header. Never downloads a cloud-only placeholder — a stub must never be filed as if it were the document. A file that vanishes between listing and stat is reported pending_sync, never raised — a scheduled scan must not die on one replaced file. PdfVerdictCache is a run's memo of PDF readability (the router asks once per manifest row for one file; the scanner asks again): the filer and the scanner each make one and pass it down, so nothing is shared at module level between runs that might one day be concurrent. UNFINISHED_SUFFIXES is the one list of transfer-in-progress names (decision 56). Decision 137 (M5): MAX_READ_MB (250) and TEXT_READ_CAP_MB (20) sit here as constants, not settings; too_large_reason() is what the router and the reader ask before a file is opened. Decision 150 (the review's ruling): open_test(path) is the open test alone, for any row, and it runs in the reading's child; check_file() and check_files() take its verdict as open_test= and open nothing themselves then - only a caller that hands none in (the CLI, a tool) opens the file here. Decision 190: the PDF and photo open tests and VANISHED name a failure by errors.error_class() - the class, never pypdf's or Pillow's message, which can quote the file - and hand the message to errors.keep(). Decision 190: FileResult carries code, set where each Reason is said or taken from the Said a helper returned (reasons.code_of). PROGRAM_EXTENSIONS is the one list of programs and is_program(name) reads the real last suffix (decision 190; a guard in test_single_source forbids a second spelling under tracker/ or app/); bears_macros(path) says whether an Office file can carry macros, reading only a zip's directory, and answers True when it cannot look. Since the review of 190: is_program answers True when either the raw name or layout.recorded_name of it has a program suffix (an invisible character after the suffix hides nothing), and bears_macros reads the recorded extension too; said_extension(path) is the extension a sentence quotes (the recorded one), while the rules still judge the raw suffix. PROGRAM_EXTENSIONS gained the installer packages, shell types and Access databases, MACRO_EXTENSIONS xlsb and the legacy templates and add-ins; html/htm/mht/svg/xhtml and one/onepkg are deliberately not programs (a saved web statement is a document; adding them would change routing unmeasured). P219 (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): pypdf is imported when a PDF is first opened (_pdf_reader(), and a module __getattr__('PdfReader') so a reader a test puts in place is the one used), fetched outside _pdf_error_uncached's catch so a reader that cannot be imported raises and never refuses a client's PDF; importing the API loads no PDF reader. pillow_heif stays registered at import, so a HEIC photo never reaches Pillow before it knows the format.
- **`tracker/view.py`** — The page a person opens: VIEW_FILENAME, regenerated in the engagement folder at the end of every real pass from the readers (load_manifest() for the request rows and their statuses, read_index() for the originals, review.triage() for what each parked file might be), in four sections - Summary, Requests, Index, Needs Review. Owns the file name, the Summary's labels and their meta names, the three words a view's state is said in (CURRENT / BEHIND / UNKNOWN), the chip's label and the button's, render_page(), write_view(), view_state(), read_stamp(), the two row builders (request_row(), index_row()) and the CLI that redraws one engagement and prints its state.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.view`
  - constants: `VIEW_FILENAME` = 'Status Report.html', `SUMMARY_SECTION` = 'Summary', `REQUESTS_SECTION` = 'Requests', `VIEW_NOTE` = 'This page is redrawn whenever anything on it changes - Generated is when it last changed - and holds no facts of its own: every value on it comes from the record, the request list and the index.', `LABEL_ENGAGEMENT` = 'Engagement folder', `LABEL_GENERATED` = 'Generated (UTC)', `LABEL_GENERATED_LOCAL` = 'Generated (this machine)', `LABEL_RECORD_DIGEST` = 'Record SHA-256', `LABEL_REQUEST_ROWS` = 'Request rows', `LABEL_INDEX_ROWS` = 'Index rows', `LABEL_PARKED_ROWS` = 'Parked for a person', `LABEL_LAST_WRITTEN` = 'Last written', `LAST_WRITTEN` = 'on {host} {at} by {by}', `LAST_WRITTEN_UNKNOWN` = 'before this version recorded a writer', `LAST_WRITTEN_NOTHING` = 'nothing yet', `VIEW_LABEL` = 'Status Report', `VIEW_OPEN_LABEL` = 'Open Status Report', `NEEDS_REVIEW_FIELDS` = ('received', 'original_name', 'subfolder', 'pbc_location', 'reason', 'candidates', 'evidence'), `BADGE_CLASS` = 'badge', `NOT_APPLICABLE_CLASS` = 'not-applicable', `NOT_ASKED_CLASS` = 'not-asked', `SET_ASIDE_SECTION` = 'Set Aside ({n})', `SET_ASIDE_GROUP` = '{label} ({n})'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/errors.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/fsio.py`, `tracker/layout.py`, `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/page.py`, `tracker/records.py`, `tracker/review.py`
  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/runner.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/door.py`
  - writes: `artifact:Status Report.html`
  - reads: `artifact:Status Report.html`, `artifact:_ledger.jsonl`, `artifact:tracker.db`
  - follows: `tracker/reminder.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_view.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_errors.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_row_columns.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Decision 89, stage A step 3, as decision 91 settled it: the owner's rule is that every file staff open only to READ is a web page. IT HOLDS NO FACT, and that is the whole design: no fact is read back - only the stamp in its meta tags, by read_stamp(), for the current / behind / unknown chip - so the one failure every other file must survive costs nothing here. A page whose replace does not land is not replaced, the run carries view_stale and SUCCEEDS, the older page stands and the next pass lands one. Written through manifest.write_text_atomically(); there is no read-only attribute (a browser holds no write lock). On Windows a plain open() read handle still refuses the replace, so view_stale has a real trigger there. Every value goes through page.esc() and the page fetches nothing. The stamp lives in meta tags in the head and read_stamp() reads it with one regular expression - no HTML parser in production. Decision 104: view_state() compares ONE digest - the record's head (ledger.head()) as it was when the page was drawn, against the head now; a rules edit is an event, so an edit moves the head and the page is honestly behind, and the workbook's digest that used to be the second stamp is gone with the workbook. Section headings come from their owners (REQUESTS_SECTION here, filer.INDEX_HEADING, filer.NEEDS_REVIEW) and the review shortlist's sentences from tracker/review.py. Imports downwards only - ledger, manifest, filer, review, page - and only runner and api import it; writing the view is the last thing a pass does. tests/conftest.py draws the page again from the live readers through render_page() after every test and requires the same bytes, with only the clock excluded. Decision 103: this page is where the statuses and the Validation Notes are READ: REQUEST_COLUMNS is the manifest's ten plus the four the record holds, side by side, and a keyword a person's filing taught the row is in Any Keywords beside the ones they typed. Decision 152: the stamp's digest is read BEFORE the rows - _readers() reads ledger.head() first and hands it to _stamp(), for write_view() and render_page() alike - because the page takes no lock and a line appended between the rows and a head read after them would name a line the rows never saw, so view_state() would call a behind page current. Read first, the error runs toward one redraw (BEHIND). A caller handing in items/entries also hands in the head it read before them (head=); the pass hands in nothing (runner.write_view(engagement) reads all three here), so its single reading is unchanged. ledger.read_with_head() is not used: the rows come from the store's readers, not from that read of the file. Decision 159 (D-7): the Summary stamp carries 'Last written' - who and when the record's last line was written - through view.last_written(), and the page's meta carries it for the app. It reads that line without the store, so it shows a writer and a time only inside the admission's two rules (records.host_problem, records.stamp_problem), else LAST_WRITTEN_UNKNOWN. Decision 190: the Index table gains Code and Client's Subfolder from INDEX_LAYOUT, and NEEDS_REVIEW_FIELDS shows the subfolder. DECISION 190: the head carries page.policy() of _STYLE and _SORT_SCRIPT (_POLICY), before the style block; the sort script adds listeners only, so a hash-only policy runs it and nothing else. Decision 200: badges show STATUS_LABELS' label and are classed by the record's word. One Set aside fold (SET_ASIDE_SECTION, SET_ASIDE_GROUP) replaces NOT_ASKED_SECTION and NOT_APPLICABLE_SECTION. P210 (pilot/SPEC-scale-1000.md): write_view() with no now first draws the page at the time the page on disk says it was generated (_kept_stamp) and, when that is the page on disk word for word (_says, read as text so CRLF compares by what it says), writes nothing and returns ViewResult.unchanged; any difference is written as before. The digest is the head either way, so view_state() stays CURRENT; VIEW_NOTE says the page is redrawn whenever anything on it changes.

### tooling

- **`tools/backtest.py`** — Routes the firm's own already-sorted documents at the office and scores the router against them: the agreement with where a person filed each one, the confusion pairs, the per-row table, the parked and no-text shares, and the time a real pass takes.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.backtest`

No file name, no folder name and no word of any document is recorded here.", `BASELINE_NOTE` = "The agreement the firm's own sorted documents scored, measured at the office. No routing change may lower it.", `UNMEASURED_NOTE` = "No backtest has been run against the firm's own documents yet, so there is no agreement to hold a routing change to. Run the backtest at the office and record it.", `NO_BASELINE` = 'No agreement is recorded: the owner has not yet run the backtest at the office. There is no baseline to hold this report to, and an unknown baseline is not a passing one.', `NOTHING_ROUTED` = 'This report routed no document at all, so it cannot be held to the recorded baseline.', `BELOW_BASELINE` = 'Agreement is BELOW the baseline: {agreement} now, {baseline} recorded.', `AT_BASELINE` = 'Agreement holds: {agreement} now, {baseline} recorded.', `RECORDED` = 'Recorded {agreement} over {documents} document(s) in {path}.'

  - documented in: `CLAUDE.md`

  - note: Decision 74. The measure the fifty blank IRS forms and the typed cases cannot be - decision 70's report leaves most keywords and most rows defended by nothing - and the only corpus made of documents a client actually sent. Each document is routed through a hard link (a copy where the file system refuses one) under one neutral name, so the router's by-name fallback can never read the client's name off the file and the score is the routing rules' rather than the firm's naming discipline; the link is the same bytes, so every tier-2 check still sees the real document. A document with no text layer is its own category, because the only evidence left for it would be the name being hidden - unless OCR is allowed, when nothing is handed over and the router does its own reading under its own stricter rule for OCR words. Catalogs are built the way tests/test_irs_forms.py builds them, with the size floor and the year check lifted. Nothing identifying comes back: counts, catalog identifiers and a row's number in the expectations file, never a file name, a folder name below the corpus root or a word of a document; the corpus, its expectations file and the report stay outside the repository and the tool refuses to write into the tree. Decision 127: route_one() also says which of READING_KINDS each document got - text, ocr or image - and the report's timing carries readings_by_kind, so the reader benchmark can say what a photo costs without a folder of text-layer PDFs flattening the number. The rule is unchanged: an image needs OCR_FLAG, exactly as a scan does. Decision 147: collect lists a document wherever the pass would take it - accepted() asks validators.extension_allowed() row by row (a row with no whitelist takes anything), so a photo is on the skeleton wherever a row takes a PDF and a .bmp still is not; no copy of the extension list is kept here. Decision 185: the out-path refusal asks settings.inside_the_app(). F-7 (a copy in the machine's temp folder when a hard link fails) is decision 186's placement. Decision 186: route_corpus() keeps its catalogs and links in this process's own scratch in the data home, and - since the review's N5, because with ocr=True it reads in its own process - points TMP, TEMP, TMPDIR and tempfile.tempdir at that scratch for the run and puts them back.
- **`tools/gpu_pack.py`** — Makes the graphics card pack (decision 169, ruling 2): one flat gpu-runtime folder of the NVIDIA libraries (CUDA 13, cuDNN 9) copied out of an environment holding requirements-gpu.txt, for Build GPU Pack.bat.

Test edges are three-way on purpose: `tests` (the test file owning the module by name) is coverage, `exercises` (any other test importing it) is not, and a test importing another test is a plain `imports`. That refusal is why the resolved files are `git add`-ed before `update`. tools/vocab_report.py hashes its inputs with the same function.

The committed report reads no client document: the corpus is the IRS's own blank forms and text the suite typed. Decision 71: when TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names the firm's own redacted documents, `build` reads those too (kind `real`) and the counts name them; that report is a local reading, never the committed one, and `check` refuses a committed report that names them.
