The report was rebuilt at the same numbers. Decision 185: build refuses while TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names a corpus, and writes that reading only into an --out folder outside the repository; a real document is labelled by its row.

### ci

- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — Dependency updates (decision 191): pip at the root, npm in app/, github-actions, each weekly, each grouped into one pull request with open-pull-requests-limit 2.
  - note: A pip update bumps a requirements*.txt pin and the lock check then fails until a person moves the same pin in its .lock and runs tools/lockfiles.py hash - the intended stop: no hash enters the repository without a person running the tool that fetched it.
- **`.github/workflows/audit.yml`** — The weekly supply-chain audit (decision 191): on a schedule and by hand only, on ubuntu-latest, runs `python tools/lockfiles.py audit` with no install at all.
  - runs: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - note: Never on a push or a pull request, so it adds no CI to any change (the cost rule). Scheduled workflows run from the default branch. Detection, not prevention: the hashes stop a replaced file; this finds a known advisory in a file we chose, and a stale native engine.
- **`.github/workflows/build.yml`** — Builds the portable package from a `v*` tag and nothing else (decision 191) by running Build App.bat itself on a Windows runner, proves the frozen executable answers in both of its modes, prints the build-info file, zips the package, publishes its SHA-256 beside it and on the run's summary page, and uploads the zip and the .sha256 as the run's artifact for seven days.
  - runs: `Build App.bat`, `api_entry.py`, `tests/samples.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_build.py`
  - note: Decision 78. It runs the batch file rather than re-implementing the build, because a second copy of the build is the one that drifts; tests/test_build.py refuses a workflow that names PyInstaller, the packager or the copy itself. The batch file pauses for a person at every exit, so it reads one documented switch that skips the waits, named in its own header and set here. The two smoke checks run the frozen executable, not the source: `list` with the shell's two environment variables set, which must answer JSON rather than a traceback on an install with no clients root yet, and one dry pass over a scratch clients root tests/samples.py builds, which walks filing, routing, scanning and drafting. Since decision 169 the root holds a scan only the reader can file (SCRATCH_SCAN), and the step compares the package's engagement line with the source's own dry pass and reads the run log's first line for reader=processor, so a package missing the reader or a model fails here. It installs the tree in the two steps every install makes (R-11): requirements.lock then rapidocr with --no-deps from requirements-nodeps.lock, both hash-checked (decision 191). Where the package landed is read back out of the batch file's own OUT/PLATFORM/ARCH and app/package.json's two names, so no path here is a second copy of one. Not on push: a freeze, an npm install, an Electron download and a few hundred megabytes of artifact are not what a commit should cost. Decision 191: no workflow_dispatch - v* tags are protected, so a package is the build of reviewed code - and a job guard `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`; the checksum step runs after both smoke checks, and the runbook compares the summary page's hash with certutil -hashfile before a stick is written (transport, not provenance). Its checkout keeps no credentials (F-12). Decision 186: a step right after the dependencies gives every run of the tracker in the job a data folder under the runner's temp (TRACKER_DATA_HOME through GITHUB_ENV, since a job-level env cannot read the runner context), and a step before the zip fails the build when the package holds any name the data home or the settings folder holds (the store and its side files, runs.log, pass-order.json, tax-tracker.xml, ocr-scratch, the data home's own name, settings.json), each pinned to its constant by tests/test_build.py.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — CI: the triggers, the concurrency rule and two jobs that both call .github/workflows/gate.yml — `linux`, a matrix of the floor interpreter and the office's, and `windows`, the office's interpreter on a pull request labelled `windows`. Since decision 211 (revising 207) it runs on a push to main (Linux only) and on a pull request into main marked ready (`ready_for_review`); Windows also on `labeled` for the `windows` label; never on `opened` or `synchronize`, and both jobs skip drafts. It has no steps of its own.
  - calls: `.github/workflows/gate.yml`
  - note: The map check is the point. docs/repo-map.md is what agents read instead of re-scanning, its freshness is guarded by test_the_committed_map_is_current, and this workflow is what makes that guard run without anyone remembering to. Every step always reports, so a stale map and a failing test surface in the same run. Windows is checked because the firm's machine is Windows and the held lock, the atomic replace and the Windows-only tests behave differently there; the python-version lines are pinned to pyproject's floor and to [tool.office] by guards. Decision 78: the matrix carries the interpreter the office runs beside that floor, because the package is frozen on the office's Python and a suite that has never run there proves nothing about it; the rows are written out one at a time rather than crossed so the floor stays one readable literal for the guard that pins it. Decision 122: a Windows minute is billed at twice a Linux one, so the two Windows rows were four fifths of the price of a run, and a series that pushes three to five times per pull request re-ran them every time — while the gate that precedes every push already runs on Windows, so those jobs repeated a check just made. Under 122 a pull request ran Linux only, Windows ran on every push to main and on a labelled pull request, and `labeled` was a trigger (history). Decision 207 (revising 122) made CI one final check before a merge and dropped the push-to-main run (history). Decision 211 (revising 207, Jason 2026-09-26: CI never fires per commit): every session runs the whole local gate before it pushes; CI runs on a push to main (Linux, the net under what merged) and once when a pull request is marked ready (the run branch protection needs); no `opened` or `synchronize`, so a push to a pull request re-runs nothing; Windows only on a ready pull request with the `windows` label (`ready_for_review`, or `labeled` for `windows`), never on main; Linux never on `labeled`; a draft runs nothing. A pull request based on another branch runs nothing until it is retargeted onto main, and retargeting (`edited`) is not a trigger, so a stacked pull request stays a draft until retargeted and is marked ready then. Windows on the floor interpreter is run nowhere, because the floor is a language-version check and Linux makes it. The steps moved out to gate.yml in decision 122: a job's own `if:` is evaluated before a matrix is expanded and cannot see the `matrix` context, so this could not be one matrix with a condition on its Windows rows, and two jobs that each wrote the steps out would be two copies of the gate. Windows is now skipped as a whole on a pull request that did not ask - never started, never billed, and reported as skipped rather than as a check that passed. Since 207 (and 211) there is no Windows run on main, so a Windows-only regression in an unlabelled pull request is run on Windows nowhere before it merges unless the office PC ran the tests it touches - which is why the label is put on anything touching the lock, the atomic replace or paths, and why no Windows check may be made a required status check (a skipped job reports only as "Windows", so a required gate name would wait forever); the gate and the package build both carry a timeout, so a hung job stops costing after it instead of after GitHub's six hours.
- **`.github/workflows/gate.yml`** — The gate's steps, written once: the test suite, the linter, `repo_map.py check`, `vocab_report.py check` and `node --check` on the three Electron files, on whichever runner and interpreter the caller names. Called by both of ci.yml's jobs.
  - runs: `tools/repo_map.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - called by: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
  - note: Decision 122. `on: workflow_call` with two required string inputs, os and python-version; the job carries timeout-minutes: 60, the ceiling that stops a hung job (decision 207: the Windows suite measured 26 to 28 minutes on main on 2026-09-26, 159's tests took a healthy run past the old 30 and near 45, and a cut-off run is billed in full; Jason set 60). It exists because a job's own `if:` cannot see the matrix, which makes ci.yml two jobs rather than one conditional matrix - and the steps written out in each of them would be two copies of the gate, the second one to drift. Its job is named for the runner and the interpreter it was given, so the check names read as they did before the split. Every step after the suite reports whatever the suite did, and keeps its point: a stale map and a failing test are separate problems, and seeing both in one run beats finding the second after fixing the first. Decision 137 (B3): every action is pinned by a full commit SHA with its tag beside it (tests/test_build.py holds every workflow to it). Decision 191: it installs requirements.lock then requirements-nodeps.lock with --require-hashes, using the runner's own pip (no --upgrade pip), caches on the lock files, and its checkout keeps no credentials (F-12).

### desktop-app

- **`app/main.js`** — Electron main process. Spawns the Python API (`-m tracker.api` under the checkout's .venv interpreter, by its full path, or the frozen executable package.json's config.apiName names in the portable build) and relays its JSON to the renderer over IPC. Since decision 193 it passes each progress line a pass prints (tracker.progress's format) to the window on the tracker-progress channel, keeps the last non-progress line as the reply, follows the kill to the limit_seconds the pass reports and says where it was, answers every failure of its own in the API's envelope, and puts no stderr on screen - a failed command's goes to the error log the API names, else to the shell's fallback error.log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\<productName> (local, non-roaming; Electron's userData off Windows).
  - imports: `app/package.json`
  - writes: `artifact:tracker-errors.log`
  - spawns: `api_entry.py`, `tracker/api.py`
  - launched by: `Start App.bat`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: This is the cross-language boundary: everything the UI can do is a tracker.api command. The renderer is untrusted here: a command must be in vocab.commands (before the vocabulary arrives, only BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND, pinned to tracker.api.COMMANDS by a guard) with the one argument shape the renderer uses; open-path opens only a path the API reported in state.paths, and the error log vocab.shell.error_log names, as a file (an optional second argument "reveal" on the same channel shows a reported file selected in File Explorer through shell.showItemInFolder after the same lstat check; a folder still goes to shell.openPath); the tracker's exit code is read, not discarded, and a plain command that outlives TRACKER_TIMEOUT_MS is killed and reported, and a pass at the limit its own first line states (decision 203). The window is sandboxed, cannot navigate and cannot open windows. Decision 160: the shell takes app.requestSingleInstanceLock(); a second launch quits before any window is made, and the running one restores and focuses its window on second-instance - two windows were two editors, and the earlier one's save took the later one's back. Decision 176: devTools is off when packaged, and runTracker() serialises the payload before the tracker starts and writes it as UTF-8, which is how tracker.api._read_spec() reads it. Decision 191: from source it runs .venv/Scripts/python.exe (or .venv/bin/python), never a bare python, and answers with the lock tool's NOT_SET_UP sentence when that is missing; buildMenu() runs before the window is made in both builds, and the app's own menu (SPEC-shell 5.1) has no reload, zoom or developer-tools item or accelerator (E-7). Decision 188 (E-14): learn() keeps each reported path with its kind from vocab.path_kinds, and openPath lstat()s it and opens it only when it is no symbolic link (Node reports a junction as one) and still a directory for 'folder' or a regular file for 'file'; otherwise vocab.shell.not_opened. No path.relative( and no startsWith( (tests/test_layers.py). Decision 186's rebase review (MF2): keepInLog() appends (appendToLog, fail-safe: a failed write is dropped, never thrown) to the error log the API named and builds no such path - no ERROR_LOG_FILENAME in the shell. Jason's ruling of 2026-09-29: with none named (no data folder yet) it appends to a fallback error.log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\<productName> (process.env.LOCALAPPDATA, else the profile's AppData\Local; off Windows app.getPath('userData'); FALLBACK_LOG_NAME; not the data home, which the P19 deny list and the package check keep out of a package, and not the roaming %APPDATA%; capped at FALLBACK_CAP 256 KB, one .1 copy, never written through a link or a folder, a folder at error.log.1 drops the old log instead of stopping writes), a failed command's reply adds just vocab.shell.no_log (api.SHELL_NO_LOG, 'Tracker failed'; SPEC-shell 11.2), the stderr is never on screen, and a renderer error is kept there too. The menu bar stays hidden until Alt (autoHideMenuBar, Jason 2026-09-29). Decision 203: the command named by vocab.pass_command (learned, never typed) is a pass: runTracker resolves the click at its 'started' progress line, streams its later lines on tracker-progress and sends {reply, code} - its final line, or the shell's own failure when it gave none or was killed - on the same channel when it closes; a pass is killed only at the limit its own first line states (limit_seconds, locking.RUN_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS), while every other command keeps TRACKER_TIMEOUT_MS; each running pass is kept in 'passes' and will-quit destroys its stdout, which the runner takes as Stop. Decision 209: at whenReady the shell runs the API's after-install command itself (LAUNCH_COMMAND, through spawnTracker, outside the renderer's allowlist) in the background: no tracker-cmd waits for it (the review's S7), and when its reply says ran the shell sends LAUNCH_DONE_CHANNEL ('after-install-done', one of three main-to-renderer channels, with tracker-progress and MENU_CHANNEL) so the page asks list again for the notice. SPEC-shell 5: the menu bar is built from BAR with the API's words (DEFAULT_MENU_WORDS, word for word tracker.api.MENU, replaced by vocab.menu when a word differs), items are enabled from the page's {enable} list (ALWAYS need nothing), and a chosen item goes to the page on MENU_CHANNEL as {id, token}; onMenuMessage() treats the one 'menu' channel as untrusted (unknown ids, popups and long tokens are dropped) and pops the six native right-click menus of POPUPS; Open error log is the shell's alone (openErrorLog: the named log, else the fallback if it exists, through openChecked's lstat test, the one openPath uses). pageBackground() reads --window-light / --window-dark from pilot-ui.css for the system theme (none under a contrast theme) and nativeTheme 'updated' repaints the window. Pilot P46: flushes the page's storage to disk as the window closes, since Electron lets go of the single-instance lock before it closes that storage. The rename (P155, pilot/SPEC-rename.md R4): productName is now the new name, so the window title, the fallback log's folder and the scheduled task follow it, but Electron's userData folder (the page's column widths and cached terms and tour answers) keeps the earlier name: main.js calls app.setPath('userData', appData + package.json's config.userDataName) at the top, before anything asks for a path and before requestSingleInstanceLock, which Electron keys on that folder. config.userDataName is held equal to settings.EARLIER_PRODUCT_NAME by tests/test_pilot_installer.py and tests/test_single_source.py. The screen defaults say 'App', not 'Tracker' (P155 Q3). P197: the View menu's Show Under Construction is a native check item (CHECKABLE), enabled from the first frame (ALWAYS) and ticked until the page speaks; the page's {enable, checked} message sets the tick, a `checked` id that is not checkable is dropped and a message without `checked` leaves it, and the menu is rebuilt only when the enable list or the tick changed. Speed round (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): P220 - one spare (SPARE_FLAG, held equal to api.SPARE_FLAG by tests/test_single_source.py): startTracker(args) is the one spawn every command and spare uses (same env, cwd, windowsHide); learn() starts the first spare once the allowlist is set; spawnTracker hands it any command that is not a pass - JSON {argv} and a newline, then the payload, then the end of input, the kill timer armed at the hand-over - and starts another (also after any command when none waits); programStamp() (the packaged API's size and mtime, or the newest tracker/*.py from source) marks a spare stale, which is killed and the command spawned fresh; will-quit kills it. The stdout reader searches each new piece for a newline and joins a line's pieces once. HELD_READING_COMMANDS (held equal to api.HELD_READING_COMMANDS by tests/test_single_source.py): a read-only command handed to a spare that closes having printed nothing (one that died while it waited) is run once more in a fresh process (spawnTracker's fresh option); a write is never run twice. P221 - EARLY_COMMANDS (BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND and 'firm') may run before the allowlist: decision 176's early allowance widened by one read-only command, each in api.HELD_READING_COMMANDS and none in api.WRITING_COMMANDS.
- **`app/package-lock.json`**
- **`app/package.json`**
  - used by: `app/main.js`
- **`app/preload.js`** — Context bridge exposing only the calls tests/test_single_source.py checks against main.js.call(args, payload), tracker.open(path, how) (how = "reveal" or absent), tracker.pickFolder(), tracker.logError(text) on 'log-error' (kept only in an error log: the API's, else the shell's fallback) and tracker.onProgress(listener), which hears 'tracker-progress', and tracker.onAfterInstallDone(listener), which hears the shell's 'after-install-done' and passes nothing across, and tracker.menu (onCommand hears {id, token} on 'menu'; send posts the page's {enable, checked} or {popup, enable, token, x, y} on it). Nothing else crosses.
  - called by: `app/renderer/app.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
- **`app/renderer/app.js`** — The desktop UI's data and writes: the New household dialog (form type, then request list), the request-list editor - the only place a rule is entered - every write, the notices, the lock and the pass. It draws no page: the shell (shell.js) and the pages (pages.js) do. Talks only to window.tracker from the preload bridge.
  - loaded by: `app/renderer/index.html`
  - calls: `app/preload.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: Every node is built with el() and placed with replaceChildren; there is no innerHTML and no escaper, so a client's file name, a keyword somebody typed into the request list or a folder name is text whatever characters it carries (a guard checks the sinks are absent). Every word it shows or compares comes from the API's vocabulary (applyVocabulary); it owns no label. Decision 76: the Needs Review card asks one question of a parked and a set-aside document alike - which request does this belong to - so reviewRow() builds both, and only an open question carries the note box and the button that sets one aside; what a person has set aside is folded under its own count, never removed from the page, because the list is the only way back. Decision 77: the way back for what is already filed is the right-click menu of a Received row (Unfile, Mark missing: unfileDocument() and withdrawAnswer(), each taking the row's handle and record version) - there for the one row that is wrong, so nobody corrects a filing in Explorer, which the index never learns of. Decision 84: the side sheet shows the shortlist. sheet.js maps state.review by handle and hands the parked file its triage; reviewRow() puts the shortlist at the head of the picker under the 'suggested' heading, every other request under 'other_requests', and lists the sentence behind each suggestion beneath the row - an <option> carries no second line, and the reason is what is read before anything is picked. The picker starts on the best suggestion, falling back to the router's own first candidate. A parked file the evidence says nothing about shows the vocabulary's nothing_suggested rather than a guess, and a set-aside row is not triaged at all, so it gets no shortlist. Every word of it - the two headings and the File it label as well - comes from vocab; the renderer still types none. Decision 89: a chip beside the engagement's name says whether its own page still describes it. The word and the label are the API's (vocab.view), the chip's class is derived from the word the same way a status chip's is, and the button opens state.paths.view through the same whitelisted opener the Open Status button uses. Decision 91: that button's label is the API's too - applyVocabulary() fills #view-label from vocab.view.open, exactly as it fills the scan button - so the page carries no word for it, and the path it opens is now an .html file the shell hands to the default browser. Decision 104: requestRows() is the one row component - a table of inputs built from vocab.columns (each column's key, header and help; the two numbers as number inputs whose minimum comes from vocab.editor.minimums, the override a pick of vocab.overrides), used by the custom-request section of Add a return / New household (three columns, identifiers assigned as rows are added) and by the editor (all ten). openEditor() opens on state.rules - the person's rows as stored, a derived date pattern shown blank, the file types shown as '*' when any - with the engagement's details laid out from vocab.editor.engagement_fields (a text box, a date or a yes/no box for the editable ones, plain text for the rest) and the keywords filings taught shown beside each row as taught (vocab.editor.learned_note), never as typed. pasteRows() appends rows pasted from a spreadsheet by position - tab-separated if any line holds a tab, otherwise CSV through a small RFC 4180 reader, a first line that repeats the headings skipped - and records nothing. saveEditor() is one edit call: a refusal is shown inside the editor with its row and column and the modal stays open; a save renders the state the API returns, closes, and says what changed or that nothing did, with the warnings under vocab.editor.warnings_heading. Every heading, label, hint and button of the editor is vocab.editor's or vocab.columns'; the Check Manifest button and the button that opened the workbook are gone with the workbook. Decision 112: both row builders put the row's sequence number on the <li> (dataset.seq, from state.index[].seq and state.review[].seq) and assignParked(), dismissParked() and unfileDocument() send it back as seq; assignParked's banner shows the API's overrode_shortlist sentence as a warn note beside left_in_review. A refusal goes through refused(): the API's sentence is toasted, the button re-enabled and showReturn(active) re-reads the state (one `state` since decision 194), so the card shows the row as the record now holds it. The renderer types no sentence of its own here either. Decision 113: the learned cell is a list rather than a line - learnedCell() draws the API's learned_note and then one span.ed-learned-word per taught keyword, each with its own button.ed-unlearn carrying the identifier and the word - and a click calls the unlearn command, then re-draws only the learned column from the state that comes back (renderLearnedCells), because unlearning is its own event and lands at once while the rows may hold edits the person has not saved. The note area says the API's unlearned_note, and its scan_note under it when the re-scan could not run; the renderer types no word of it. Decision 110: movedRow() builds the sheet's row for a moved working copy of state.moved, with restoreMoved (the restore command) and keepMoved (assign, with the request the picker was left on and the keyword typed) behind two buttons, delegated on #sheet; sending it to review is gone (SPEC-shell E65) and its home and where it is now are paths, so neither is drawn. The picker and the keyword box are shown only where the API said which request the copy's name belongs to (in_request, decision 168), and the picker starts on it; every word is vocab.review_labels', including the word for a copy that is nowhere. Decision 114 (the deck, Cards/List) is gone with the shell (SPEC-shell 13): the side sheet places one row built by reviewRow() at a time, and its Next moves on without writing. fileRow() is the one place the assign call is made - assignParked() and keepMoved() reach it, and a guard in tests/test_single_source.py keeps it the only one, so the review rows and a moved copy cannot drift apart. Decision 118: renderReminder()/loadReminder()/drawReminder() are the reminder in the side sheet - the record's last word on the draft as one caption, the four stages as a toggle coloured from the API's palette, the letter drawn from its own shape with el() (never from the clipboard's markup, which would be an HTML string), Copy for Outlook putting text/html and text/plain on the clipboard with the same words, Approve sending back the fingerprint of the text on screen, and no Open the draft file (SPEC-shell 7.2); the letter's parts sit in the side sheet from the start with the ids drawReminder() looks up. The stage a person picked is the only thing the page holds of its own and is dropped when the engagement changes. It types no colour: every hex it draws with is looked up in vocab.reminder.palette by the key a stage carries, and a guard reads the file for one. Decision 129 added the household card's two feed lines, the editor's feed list with its picker and its warning, and File under another return on both renderings of the queue - every word of it from the API's vocabulary, as always. Decision 160: the editor sends state's list_head with every save, and a Rename fold (renameChoices(), renameRequest()) calls the rename command, renames the row in place, adopts the version the rename returns and keeps what the person typed and not saved. Decision 157: movedRow() draws a gone row (its copy and its original both gone) with the one answer left, Mark <identifier> missing (vocab.review_labels.mark_missing on the .r-withdraw button), and the sheet's delegate sends it to withdrawAnswer(). Decision 189: runScan() shows the reply's pass_warnings and each other return's error, skip and warnings under its own label, in the same banner and the same way as the asked return's warnings, on the skipped and failed paths too. Decision 188: the household card shows the API's pause sentence and, where there is something to accept, the one 'Accept the folder's name' button, which sends accept-folder-name with the seq and scope the card was drawn from; misfits are drawn from the API's 'where' (the path below the root), never worked out here. Decision 194: one process per click. A switch is showReturn -> one `state` (193's generation drops a late reply). The Reminder card is drawn from state.reminder_card (drawReminderReply draws either source); `reminder` is called only for the stage toggle, a refused approve, or to keep a toggled rung after a write. The list and vocab arrive once from `list` (bootstrap: start and set-root) and are replaced by the `list` a list-changing write carries (adoptList). The editor opens on lastState (D13); its save is judged by list_head. The review's fixes: call(args, payload, { ofAnother }) says the warnings of another return's state (the hand-over picker's) under its label (vocab.notices.about, labelOfState); unlearnKeyword redraws through renderFor, so D13's lastState is never behind an unlearn. Decision 196: there is no wizard and no household choice outside the household on screen. openRoll() opens the roll dialog (#roll-modal; renderRollFold fills it) only when state.household.roll_year is set, and Add a return; rollFromCard() gathers the ticks and form picks (rollChoice, kept for the household on screen across a redraw) and rollHouseholdCall(hh, choice) - a pure function a test runs under node - builds the one roll-household call from the household on screen. openAddReturn(hh) sets addingTo, the only household a create sends by path; openNewHousehold() clears it. A refused create stays in #ne-note. On decision 194's model the create and the roll adopt the list their reply carries (adoptList) and draw its state through renderFor; the roll fold's people button is reviewPeople() - showReturn, which says whether its read drew the page, then openEditor only when it did and the clicked return is still active, so a failed read is one notice and a switch during the read opens no editor; bootstrap loads the catalog once for the roll fold's form pick; openEditor reads state only when lastState is another return's and says vocab.editor.not_this_return when a switch landed during that read. Decision 200: a row's status is vocab.labels[item.status_key].label in pages.js (pagesItemStatus), one word in its colour with no sentence (SPEC-shell 2.5 E58); setAsideGroups() builds the one Set aside fold (not asked first, then each Not Applicable year) that renderEditorRows() draws, each group headed by setAsideHeading(). Not Applicable rows leave the working table; no 'override:' is typed. Decision 201: every dialog is in DIALOGS and goes through openDialog (remembers the opener, focuses a control, Tab trapped by trapTab) and requestClose (Cancel, Escape and an overlay click alike) to closeDialog (focus back to the opener); a dialog with a model is compared with its snapshot and, when dirty, raises its unsaved bar - Keep editing focused, Discard the only way out, Escape keeping; rename and a form picked move the snapshot. keywordBox() and noteBox() build the labelled review boxes. requestRows takes a fold option: the editor's plain part (vocab.editor.plain_columns, and a custom row's Document per state.items[].catalog_row) and a per-row Routing rules fold (routing_columns), hidden never dropped; a refused save opens every fold. addIssuerAndFile() is the one call site of add-issuer-and-file. DECISION 190: the Reminder card's status and each return's household line say vocab.reminder.approved_then_edited when the state's `lapsed` is set, after approved and before last drafted. tests/test_layers.py scans this file, main.js and preload.js for any network call. The review list groups parked rows by the API's bucket under review_labels.buckets (decision 190); a not-a-document row and card offer no Open and no File it and say the true type; Open is offered only where the API named row.open_key (never a container or a refused reading - decision 190 following 184) and opens state.paths[row.open_key], never a path of its own. Since the review of 190 every row is keyed on the API's handle, never pbc_location: data-original, the triaged map, the triaged map, so two programs from one zip (no location) are two rows. Decision 203: runScan() sends withEng(vocab.pass_command) and is answered once the pass has begun; onPassMessage() takes that pass's progress lines (drawProgress) and its ending (passEnded): the final line's pass_warnings become notices, the asked return's run and the household's other runs draw the banner through scanSummary(run, others, summary) - a notice under its label when that return is no longer shown - and the page is redrawn with one `list`, then one `state`, behind renderFor. P131: that answer is not a window-wide notice: keepSortAnswer() keeps it under the asked return (sortAnswers), showSortAnswers() shows it as keyed 'sort' notices only while a page of that return's household is on screen (appRouteChanged calls it), the next pass replaces the answers of every return it ran, a dismissed line is forgotten with its keyed-notice key, and every returned pass clears its returns' keys first, so the same failure met again is said again (forgetSortLine, review M1); the pass failure is kept whole, lock and identifier included (review S1) and F5 forgets all (forgetSortAnswers, from shell.js's shellRefresh). P132: createEngagement goes to the new return's page (shellGo(pagesRoute(...))). P134: scanSummary says 'Nothing Done: {why}.' with vocab.scan.skipped's word for an inactive, rolled-forward or roomless return (P199: a pass in which no return of the household filed, sent to review, failed a file or was stopped says vocab.scan.nothing_to_sort - a Sort that filed into another return did something, the screen review's M1 - or 'Nothing Done: {n} Still Syncing.' when a file is still arriving; another return's line keeps its bullet and names the return by year, taxpayer and form, sortReturnSaid; the schedule dialog's next run is written in the app's clock style, scheduleClock), and drawReminder lists card.unsorted_files under the inbox hold line. The household's returns are greyed by the lock the pass holds, which state reports (193); scanDone() gives the button back through applyLock()'s mark (the review's M2), and a final line that does not name the asked return is vocab.scan.not_in_pass (S2). - **`Build App.bat`** — Builds the portable package: freezes the API with PyInstaller from the committed api_entry.spec inside a virtual environment holding exactly requirements.lock, requirements-build.lock and requirements-nodeps.lock, installed with --require-hashes, packages the Electron shell with @electron/packager, copies the frozen API into resources/ and writes BUILD-INFO.txt.
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - freezes: `api_entry.py`
  - note: Reproducible from the commit (decision 46): the freeze runs in its own venv because PyInstaller follows optional imports and the machine's Python would otherwise leak unrelated packages into the package (decision 53). The packager runs through its entry script under `node`, not the `npx` shim, for the ampersand reason Start App.bat states; the copy into the package is `robocopy` with its exit code checked and the executable's presence asserted, because `xcopy` gave up on the package's long paths while the script still reported success (decision 53). Guards pin OUT to .gitignore and the resources path to app/main.js. Decision 55: the venv is made fresh each build; no parenthesised value is expanded inside the build-info block. Decision 78: every exit goes through one `:wait` label, which pauses for the person who double-clicked unless TRACKER_BUILD_NONINTERACTIVE is set - the one switch, named in this file's header and read nowhere else, and what lets .github/workflows/build.yml run this file rather than a copy of it. Decision 191: the installs read the locks in hash mode (a replaced file, or a package the locks do not name, fails the build), tests/test_build.py compares BUILD-INFO.txt's freeze with the union of the locks under the build's markers, NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is set before the first command and robocopy is called by its full path (E-10).
- **`Build GPU Pack.bat`** — Builds the graphics card pack (decision 169, ruling 2): installs exactly requirements-gpu.lock (--no-deps, --require-hashes) into its own environment and runs tools/gpu_pack.py on it.
  - runs: `tools/gpu_pack.py`
  - note: The only reader of the GPU lock (tests/test_build.py). Build App.bat never runs it: the app is one build and the pack an optional folder. Decision 191: hash-checked, NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath first (E-10).
- **`Setup.bat`** — The one-time setup for running from source (decision 191): makes the app's private Python in .venv, installs requirements.lock then requirements-nodeps.lock (--no-deps) with --require-hashes, runs npm ci in app/, and last stamps what it installed with tools/lockfiles.py stamp.
  - precedes: `Start App.bat`
  - runs: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - note: The machine's own Python only makes the environment and is never installed into, so no other program can break the app or be broken by it. --clear, so a package an older lock named does not survive. The stamp is written last, so a Setup that stopped part-way leaves none and Start App.bat says to run it again. It is where a machine's Python is first asked: the floor check and its 'Install Python <floor>+' sentence are pinned to pyproject.toml's requires-python (tests/test_single_source.py). Sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath first and calls where.exe by path (E-10). Decision 209: its fourth and last step, after the stamp, is python -m tracker.after_install --reason setup (registers the schedule on the computer that runs it, runs the record check); a finding does not stop Setup, and a failed step prints after_install.SETUP_RETRY and exits 1 with the stamp kept. Every .bat checks out CRLF (the Git attributes file, R7): cmd reads a batch file by byte offset.
- **`Start App.bat`** — Runs the desktop app from source, offline, and installs nothing (decision 191): refuses in one sentence when Setup.bat has not made .venv, when tools/lockfiles.py verify says the lock files changed since Setup ran, or when app/node_modules is missing; then starts Electron.
  - follows: `Setup.bat`
  - runs: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - launches: `app/main.js`
  - note: Electron is started through its own entry script under `node`, never the `npx` shim: the shim breaks when the folder's path contains an ampersand, which the firm's own checkout does (decision 53). Decision 191 replaced decision 55's install-every-start: a launch that installed ran a package's install code and reached the network at every start, into the machine's own Python. No pip, no npm ci and no npm install appear in it (tests/test_build.py); its not-set-up sentence is tools/lockfiles.py's NOT_SET_UP word for word. It sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath before its first command and calls where.exe by its full path (E-10). Decision 209: the app itself runs the after-install step at launch when the program changed, so a pull that left the locks alone still registers the schedule and checks the records.
- **`api_entry.py`** — PyInstaller entry point: the portable app's one executable, which is the tracker API by default and the scheduled job (tracker.runner.main) when RUNNER_MODE_FLAG comes first.
  - CLI: `python api_entry.py`
  - imports: `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/settings.py`
  - imports at call time: `tracker/after_install.py`, `tracker/api.py`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - spawned by: `app/main.js`
  - scheduled by: `tracker/scheduling.py`
  - frozen by: `Build App.bat`
  - tested by: `tests/test_api_entry.py`
  - note: PyInstaller needs a real script, not a -m module. Runner mode is dispatched before tracker.api is imported, because the API imports tracker.scheduling whose TASK_NAME needs the product name the Electron shell passes in the environment - and Task Scheduler passes nothing; the job needs neither of the shell's variables. api_entry.spec (committed; reads config.apiName from app/package.json) is how it is frozen. Decision 150: multiprocessing.freeze_support() is the first statement of the main block, so a reading's child - the frozen executable started again by multiprocessing's spawn - runs as the child and never as the API or the job. Speed round (pilot/SPEC-speed-round.md): P220 - given exactly [SPARE_FLAG] it runs api.spare(), waiting for its one command. Q1 / P218 - run_setup_step(argv) for runner.SETUP_MODE_FLAG (--after-install-setup --settings <folder> --product <name>, both required): it puts the settings folder and product name in the environment before tracker.after_install (and so tracker.scheduling) is imported, then runs after_install.main(['--reason', 'setup']). pilot/installer/setup.iss's [Run] starts it (StatusMsg 'Making the Overview ready...', runhidden waituntilterminated) before the launch entry, so the first Overview after a pilot install opens warm; a step that fails there runs again at the app's first launch. The setup mode exits with the pilot installer's codes (runner.SETUP_STEP_FAILED, SETUP_OVERVIEW_NOT_READY, via after_install's INSTALLER_CODES_FLAG), which setup.iss's [Code] turns into a small error window (Jason, 2026-10-08).
- **`conftest.py`** — Puts the repo root on sys.path so tests can `import tracker` without installing the package - explicitly now, beside pyproject's pythonpath, for editor runners and pytest's rootdir detection.
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**

## Tests, documents and data files with a stated purpose

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Agent entry point. Says to read the map instead of re-scanning, how to keep it current, and the standing rules that hold across every module.
  - documents: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/learned_keywords.py`, `tools/repo_map.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Points at docs/repo-map.md as the first thing to read in a session.
- **`README.md`** — What the system is, how to run each stage, and how to set it up. Who does what is docs/workflow.md.
  - documents: `tracker/runner.py`
- **`docs/ROADMAP.md`** — The build plan, the hard constraints and the decision log. Every component, all built and tested.
  - documents: `tracker/__init__.py`
  - note: The decision log is the record of WHY: read it before changing behaviour that looks arbitrary.
- **`docs/backtest-baseline.json`** — The one number the backtest commits: how often the router filed the firm's own sorted documents where a person filed them, the count it was measured over, and the day it was measured.
  - written by: `tools/backtest.py`
  - note: Decision 74. Owned by tools/backtest.py; `record` writes it and `check` fails a report below it. It ships with no agreement recorded, and `check` then says plainly that the owner has not yet run the backtest at the office and exits 0 - an unknown baseline is never reported as a met one. It holds a number and a date and nothing a client could be read out of.
- **`docs/repo-map.curated.json`** — The hand-written half of this map: roles, notes, artifacts, cross-language hops and the standing rules. Merged on top of the derived facts and never overwritten by a rebuild.
  - read by: `tools/repo_map.py`
  - note: Edit this, then run `python tools/repo_map.py update`. The generated docs/repo-map.json and docs/repo-map.md are NOT edited by hand.
- **`docs/runbook.md`** — The operator's page for one tax season: the designated machine and today's rule that only one may run a clients root, what a person does each morning and on the draft day, what every index reason and validation note means, and the thirty-minute move to another machine.
  - note: Written for a person, not an agent. Roles are docs/workflow.md and the reasons behind the rules are docs/ROADMAP.md; it links to both rather than repeating them.
- **`docs/storage.md`** — The storage plan in prose: the three words (the record, the ledger, the store) and what each means, why the journal syncs with the engagement folder and the database does not, the journal-then-apply order, the schema table, the edit as the event the rules travel in, rebuild as recovery, the check as the gate, what each of the four stages took away, and (decision 107) why the verdict cache is in the store and not in the record.
  - documents: `tracker/ledger.py`, `tracker/store.py`
  - note: Written with decision 101 and finished with 104. It is the page to read before touching storage. The migrations of decisions 102 and 103, which it described step by step, are gone from the tree and from this page; the History section says they existed and where their reading copy is.
- **`docs/vocab-coverage.json`** — The coverage report as data, with the SHA-256 of every input it was built from; `check` and the suite compare against these. Generated; never edited by hand.
  - written by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
- **`docs/vocab-coverage.md`** — The vocabulary coverage report as people read it: the unreached keywords, the keywords reached only by documents that file elsewhere, the rows nothing files into, then every catalog row by row. Generated by tools/vocab_report.py; never edited by hand.
  - written by: `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Rebuilt with `python tools/vocab_report.py build` in the same commit as a catalog, matcher or case change.
- **`docs/workflow.md`** — How the day-to-day workflow runs.
- **`pilot/brand/tax-document-console/README.md`** — Says what each file of the Tax Document Console artwork folder is and where it is seen (the app icon, the installer's icon and wizard images, the lockups, the packaged-app tiles).
  - note: Everything in pilot/brand/tax-document-console/ except this file and source/ is GENERATED by source/export.py and is never edited by hand: change source/mark.py and re-run `python export.py ..`. The app's copy, app/assets/icon.ico (committed because the unpackaged launch needs it; .ico is not a mapped suffix), must stay byte-identical to app/icon.ico here, which tests/test_build.py holds; Build App.bat (--icon), api_entry.spec (icon=), app/main.js (BrowserWindow icon) and pilot/installer/setup.iss ([Setup] icon keys) name these files.
- **`requirements-build.txt`** — What Build App.bat's freeze needs beyond requirements.txt: the pinned PyInstaller. Installed from requirements-build.lock (with requirements.lock), by hash (decision 191).
- **`requirements.txt`** — Runtime and dev dependencies, pinned exactly (a guard refuses a range), including the reader's runtime closure (decision 169) - rapidocr itself is in requirements-nodeps.txt. The human-edited list of direct pins: nothing installs it directly; every install reads requirements.lock, the whole tree by version and by SHA-256 (decision 191).
  - read by: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - note: requirements-build.txt adds the pinned freezer on top for Build App.bat; api_entry.spec is the committed freeze and app/package-lock.json the committed Electron install, so a build is made from the commit rather than from whatever was current that day (decision 46). olefile (decision 143) reads an Outlook .msg; pinned here and in requirements.lock, and frozen by the portable build. Decision 169 (R-11): rapidocr's metadata asks for the GUI opencv-python, so its real runtime dependencies are listed here with opencv-python-headless, and rapidocr is installed afterwards with --no-deps from requirements-nodeps.lock - by Setup.bat, Build App.bat, gate.yml, build.yml and the README's setup alike (tests/test_build.py pins both steps everywhere). Two pins carry markers: onnxruntime-gpu on Windows and the plain onnxruntime elsewhere (R-11b, CI has no card), numpy 2.5.3 from Python 3.12 and 2.4.6 for the 3.11 floor (R-11a). pytesseract is gone. Decision 191: constraints.txt is gone; four lock files (requirements.lock, requirements-build.lock, requirements-nodeps.lock, requirements-gpu.lock - not mapped, the map takes no .lock files) carry each pin with the hash of every file PyPI publishes for it, and tools/lockfiles.py check (run by tests/test_lockfiles.py) fails when a pin here and its lock disagree. A pin moves here and in its lock together, then `python tools/lockfiles.py hash`.
- **`tests/conftest.py`** — What every test pays for once: an app folder of its own (settings and store, via own_folders()), the tripwire's arming and its session verdict (decision 185), the store and view agreement checks, and the one way to make an engagement, sort an inbox and start a Python child (child_env()).
  - imports: `tests/tripwire/sitecustomize.py`
  - used by: `tests/test_after_install.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_api_entry.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_containers.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_errors.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_households.py`, `tests/test_layout.py`, `tests/test_learned_keywords.py`, `tests/test_ledger.py`, `tests/test_locking.py`, `tests/test_manifest.py`, `tests/test_ocr.py`, `tests/test_page_rows.py`, `tests/test_real_corpus.py`, `tests/test_registry.py`, `tests/test_reminder.py`, `tests/test_review.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`, `tests/test_row_columns.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_scaffold.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`, `tests/test_scheduling.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`, `tests/test_store.py`, `tests/test_tripwire.py`, `tests/test_validators.py`, `tests/test_view.py`
  - note: Decision 185: own_folders() is the one place a process is told where beside-the-app is - the session calls it in pytest_configure before collection, every test through an_app_folder_of_its_own (its own MonkeyPatch, so a test's undo cannot take it); real_places() is the one list of places a real settings file, store, scratch or client tree resolves to, from the constants that name them, and 186 adds the data home to both. pytest_configure installs the hook with the session's TRACKER_TEST_TRIPWIRE value and the session log, so this process also judges the Python children it starts by the routes the tripwire's docstring lists (and what escapes is listed there too); a process it forks writes its records to the log. pytest_sessionfinish fails the session on any tripwire record, the pytest process's or a child's (the session log, read_tripwire_log(): a line it cannot read, or a log it cannot read at all (any OSError), is itself said as a violation, never an internal error), and on any folder the session left in the checkout (checkout_folders(), which never lists a guarded place). office_shaped_copy is the checkout copied with fabricated real-looking files beside it, for the nested proofs. Decision 186: own_folders() also sets TRACKER_DATA_HOME to data_home_for(folder), a sibling of the folder holding the app folder (<tmp_path>-data for a test, <session>-data for the session, removed at unconfigure), so no clients root a test makes of tmp_path holds it (ROOT_HOLDS_DATA); real_places() guards the account's real data home (settings.default_data_home(), none on a machine without one) and one the shell names, and names the store by where.with_name(STORE_FILENAME) since store.path_for() is gone; run_in_copy() drops the suite's data home, as a fresh shell has none.
- **`tests/samples.py`** — The pile of client documents the suite starts from, built from nothing: text_pdf() prints lines to a real one-page PDF, sheet_xlsx() writes rows to a real workbook, and build_samples() assembles the drop folder a client would leave (a duplicate, last year's form, a Word file, a Google Sheets shortcut, a photo, a half-uploaded temp file).
  - used by: `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py`, `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_containers.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_errors.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_locking.py`, `tests/test_ocr.py`, `tests/test_registry.py`, `tests/test_router.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_shell.py`, `tests/test_vocab_report.py`
  - used at call time by: `pilot/wintest/make_samples.py`
  - run by: `.github/workflows/build.yml`
  - note: No fixture files in the repository and no client data, so every test starts from the same pile. It was the marketing demo's sample builder in tracker/api.py; the demo went (decision 41) and the suite still needed the pile. listing_denied() makes a folder really unlistable for the running account, because rglob and os.walk reach the file system by different calls and a monkeypatch of one proves nothing about the other. Decision 73: sheet_xlsx() is how tests/test_catalog.py routes its workbook cases - half of every catalog asks for a schedule a client keeps in Excel, and a sheet is read as rows of tab-separated cells (a phrase across two cells is one phrase, a phrase down two rows is two labels), so typing one as prose would prove the wrong reading. Decision 78: build_scratch_root() assembles the same pile into a whole clients root - one scaffolded engagement with the documents already dropped - which is what .github/workflows/build.yml runs the frozen package over; the fixture lives beside the pile rather than in a tool of its own so there is one pile and not two that drift. It records the engagement through manifest.create_engagement() directly rather than through the suite's helper, because the build workflow imports this module without conftest (decision 104). openpyxl is imported here to WRITE a client's spreadsheet for the suite to read, which is the one use of it the tree keeps. The pile's 'file nobody accepts' is a .bmp since decision 127: it was a .jpg until a photo became a document, and the claim it carries is about a file type no row takes. Decision 143 added cfb_bytes(), a compound-file writer to the letter of [MS-CFB] (version 3, a mini stream, one FAT), and msg_bytes()/msg_storage() over it, so the suite's .msg fixtures are built from nothing - olefile only reads. Decision 169: scanned_pdf() draws lines on a page and saves a PDF with no text layer, and build_scratch_root() drops one (SCRATCH_SCAN, a W-2 whose box labels and figures are drawn as separate lines) so the frozen smoke check proves the package reads.
- **`tests/test_backtest.py`** — Guards the backtest: a document is routed by its text and never by its name, a file with no text layer is counted apart rather than parked, the report and the console carry no file or folder name, the skeleton is blank with the request folder as the hint and is never overwritten, and an unrecorded baseline is said rather than passed.
  - imports: `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/samples.py`
  - note: Decision 74. The corpus it scores is built with tests/samples.py in a temporary folder, because no client document is in the repository or ever will be. It also pins the two things the hiding rests on: the neutral name reaches no keyword in any shipped catalog, and a whole pass writes nothing under the repository root.
- **`tests/test_build.py`** — Guards what only the build workflow could otherwise discover ten minutes into a release: that it runs the batch file the repository owns rather than a copy of the build, that the switch it sets is the one that batch file reads, that the flags it fires at the frozen executable are flags tracker/runner.py declares, that it passes the two environment variables tracker/settings.py names, and that both workflows quote the one interpreter pyproject.toml writes down.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`
  - note: Decision 78. It also asserts the fixture: a scratch root is one engagement discovery finds and a whole dry pass walks, because a smoke check over an empty folder proves only that discovery does not crash. Nothing here can prove the package runs - only the Windows runner can. Decision 137 (M5), on decision 191's locks: requirements.lock, requirements-build.lock and requirements-nodeps.lock pin the whole tree the portable build freezes, by hash; the suite holds requirements*.txt to them, "Build App.bat" to installing them with --require-hashes, and every BUILD-INFO.txt under build-portable/dist to freezing nothing else. Decision 191 also: every pip install in every batch file and workflow is --require-hashes from a .lock and none upgrades pip; the build runs from a v* tag only, with a job guard; the checksum step follows the smoke checks and the upload carries the zip and its .sha256; the launcher installs nothing and speaks the lock tool's sentence; every batch file sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath first and calls Windows' own tools by path (E-10); every checkout keeps no credentials (F-12); the audit workflow is scheduled, Linux-only and never on a push.
- **`tests/test_containers.py`** — Decision 143's claims: an email, a .msg (written by the suite's own compound-file writer) and a zip are opened and each attachment filed where it belongs with its row naming the container; a loose twin and a re-sent container are duplicates; a pass killed after the writes ends with each attachment once; nothing lands in the client tree; inline pictures and bodies are skipped and named in the opened line; every limit at its edge; locked, damaged and empty containers park; a name cannot leave its folder; an attachment never files into another household and the hand-over refuses it; a dry run writes nothing; the _Opened sweep; the store rebuilds with the new column.
  - imports: `tests/child_readers.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_content_check.py`, `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`
- **`tests/test_learned_keywords.py`** — Guards the learned-keyword report: two engagements that taught one keyword are one row with a count of two, a keyword the catalog already carries is not reported, a hand-added row is a custom row, an unreadable record is a problem line, the default output holds no folder name, nothing under the repository is written and a path inside it is refused, and a keyword an IRS form says is marked as one that would misfile it.
  - imports: `tests/conftest.py`
  - note: Decision 79. The clients roots are scratch trees under tmp_path, built the way tests/test_registry.py builds one: tests/conftest.py's make_engagement() records the shipped catalog through create_engagement() and a keyword_learned event teaches the keyword, so what the report compares is a real record rather than a stand-in. The corpus case reads the fifty IRS forms and takes about half a minute.
- **`tests/test_real_corpus.py`** — The harness for the firm's own redacted documents: every row of the expectations file beside them routed against a shipped catalog the way tests/test_irs_forms.py routes the IRS's forms, and asserted to file where the firm says or to park.
  - imports: `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`
  - used by: `tests/test_catalog.py`
  - used at call time by: `tools/backtest.py`, `tools/vocab_report.py`
  - note: Decision 71. The corpus is outside the repository, in the folder TRACKER_REAL_CORPUS names, and is never committed; with no corpus the routing case skips by name and the harness's own tests - the reading, the routing and the skip - still run on a scratch folder, so the file is exercised on every machine. It owns read_expectations() and real_corpus(), which tools/vocab_report.py imports, so the report and the test cannot disagree about what an expectation means. Decision 74: read_expectations() takes the file's path rather than its folder, because tools/backtest.py scores an expectations file a person keeps wherever they keep it and the contract has to have one reader. Decision 185: rows are test ids and messages by number (row-N, counted from one as tools/backtest.py counts), never by file name or folder; no other test sees the corpus, because the conftest hides the variable from every test after collection.
- **`tests/test_repo_map.py`** — Guards the map's trust contract: derived facts come from source, curated judgment survives regeneration, drift is detected, and the committed map matches the tree.
  - note: test_the_committed_map_is_current fails the suite if someone changed code without running `repo_map.py update`.
- **`tests/test_shell.py`** — The shell's renderer half: the tokens and their contrast in both themes, the shell stylesheet's discipline, the guards every renderer file keeps, the words the new files may not type, and the route, search, sort icon and menu enable list run in node against shell.js's own functions.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_pilot_ui.py`, `tests/test_runner.py`
  - used by: `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: SHELL_FILES and TITLE_FREE name the files a claim covers; S2 adds the menu half, S4 the pages' node tests and S5 the sheet's. The contrast table and the token values are the SPEC's section 10, copied as data.
- **`tests/test_vocab_report.py`** — Guards the coverage report: reach is says(), not a substring; the four headline lists are computed as claimed on small catalogs; the committed report matches its inputs by hash.
  - imports: `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_catalog.py`, `tests/test_scanner.py`
  - note: test_the_committed_report_is_current fails the suite if a keyword, a case or the matcher changed without `python tools/vocab_report.py build`. Decision 73: a workbook case must read the same to the report as to the suite, so the rendering and a real round trip through openpyxl are asserted equal.
- **`tests/tripwire/sitecustomize.py`** — The suite's tripwire (decision 185): an audit hook that stops and records any open, listing, folder creation, move, removal, copy, link or SQLite connection at a guarded place, and in the pytest process records a Python child started around it through a watched route; imported by conftest in the pytest process and found as sitecustomize on PYTHONPATH by every Python child that inherits the suite's environment.
  - used by: `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_tripwire.py`
  - note: In the pytest process (install(children=..., log=...)) it watches subprocess.Popen, os.posix_spawn, os.spawn, os.exec (also from a process it forked - fork then exec, POSIX os.spawn* - which writes the session log since its SEEN dies with it), _winapi.CreateProcess (multiprocessing on Windows) and, wrapped because it raises no audit event, multiprocessing.util.spawnv_passfds (multiprocessing on POSIX, the reading child): a Python child (this interpreter after realpath, or a program named python*) whose environment lacks the session's TRACKER_TEST_TRIPWIRE, whose PYTHONPATH does not begin with this session's tripwire folder, or whose flags carry -I, -E or -S is recorded as an unarmed Python child and fails the session - recorded, never raised. A nested session in the office-shaped copy is its own session and judges its children against the copy's folder. A verbatim Windows prefix (\\?\, \\?\UNC\) is stripped before comparing. It does not see non-Python children, a Python child started by a Python child, a Python child started through a non-Python launcher (a shell, env, the py launcher, a bare PATH name not starting with python), a direct _posixsubprocess.fork_exec outside multiprocessing.util, a native library's own opens, os.stat/exists, an alias that does not carry the place's name (an 8.3 short name, \\localhost\C$\... or \\.\C:\...), the clients root a real settings file names (guarded only because that file cannot be read), or deliberate evasion (ctypes): a guard rail in the suite, not a wall. And a relative name given to os.open (how shutil.rmtree walks with dir_fd) is not judged, since the event does not carry the descriptor. Standard library only, imports nothing of the package, so a child is armed before its first import.

## Artifacts (files the system reads and writes at runtime)

- **`artifact:.venv/tracker-lock.json`** — Setup.bat's stamp, inside the checkout's private environment (decision 191): the SHA-256 of each lock file and of app/package-lock.json as they were when Setup installed them. Start App.bat compares it at every launch through tools/lockfiles.py verify and refuses to start, naming Setup.bat, when it is missing or differs. Not client data; .venv is gitignored.
  - written by: `tools/lockfiles.py`
  - read by: `tools/lockfiles.py`
- **`artifact:Prepared/`** — The firm-side working set: renamed copies sorted per request, plus 00 - Needs Review for anything that could not be identified. The client never sees this.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
- **`artifact:Status Report.html`** — The page a person opens (decisions 89 and 91), in the engagement folder beside the record, and the only file there without a leading underscore because it is the one staff are meant to open. One self-contained HTML file - inline style, no image, no font, nothing fetched - with a sticky navigation and four sections: Summary (the record's head, when it was drawn in UTC and in local time, the counts, and the sentence that says it holds no facts of its own), Requests (statuses as coloured badges; since decision 116 the rows set aside as Override.NOT_APPLICABLE are not in the table but folded below it in one page.details() block per year, headed NOT_APPLICABLE_SECTION with the label and the count, dimmed, in the same columns - and Override Reason is a column), Index and Needs Review (the parked rows, each with the shortlist review.triage() computes and one line per set-aside row it names). Every table sorts on a click through a few lines of inline script and is a plain table without it. REGENERATED BY EVERY REAL PASS from the readers, never on a dry run. It HOLDS NO FACT - every value on it is the record's - so no fact is read back (read_stamp() reads only the stamp) and there is nothing on it to edit. The stamp is in meta tags in the head (tracker-record-sha256, tracker-generated and one per Summary field), which view_state() reads with a regular expression; since decision 104 the stamp is the record's head alone, because a rules edit is an event and moves it. A page whose replace does not land - on Windows an open read handle is enough to refuse it - is simply not replaced: the run reports view_stale and succeeds, and the one on disk stays honestly behind. The app says current / behind / unknown beside the engagement's name (tracker.view.view_state) and opens it with the Open Status Report button; `python -m tracker.view <folder>` redraws one.
  - written by: `tracker/view.py`
  - read by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/view.py`
- **`artifact:_Opened/`** — What was taken out of the emails and zips a client dropped (decision 143): J Park & Associates/<household>/<year>/_Opened/<container's stem>/<attachment>, layout.OPENED_DIR_NAME, beside the year's returns in the private tree and never in the tree the client is shared. Each file is an attachment's original - its row's pbc_location - written atomically before the container's row exists. Synced like the rest of the private tree, a named exception to decision 107 by the owner's decision of 2026-09-23, because a recovery and a move to another machine must reach it. Skipped by discovery (the underscore), never a return (no journal), outside every return's working set; a file there no row names is a warning every pass and is never re-sorted or deleted.

  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:_Scheduling computer.txt`** — One line in the firm's private tree (layout.designation_file, DESIGNATION_FILENAME) naming the computer that runs the schedule for this clients root, as locking.this_host normalises it (decision 209). Written by scheduling.claim (the first Windows computer to run the after-install step with a root set) or scheduling.move_here (--move-schedule-here); read by scheduling.designated_machine, the one reader decision 210 will ask too. Checked when written, read and acted on; a file that is not one computer's name is DESIGNATION_UNREADABLE, a failure naming the path and never the content. A file, never a folder, so discovery never lists it as a misfit. Detection, not a lock: two desks claiming before sync carries the first can both claim.

  - read by: `tracker/scheduling.py`
- **`artifact:_ledger.jsonl`** — The engagement's own append-only record (decision 87), in the engagement folder beside the client's files: one JSON event per line, in the order the writers wrote them - what was preserved, filed, parked, called a duplicate, decided by a person, had its bytes recorded, taught a keyword, the statuses each scan applied, and (decision 104) the request list and the engagement's details as the app's editor saved them, one rules_changed event per save carrying exactly what moved. Written only under the engagement lock, with O_APPEND and fsync, one line per event and never rewritten; a torn last line is ignored by the reader and truncated by the next append. Since decision 102 it is the whole of the index, since 103 the whole of the statuses, and since 104 the whole of the person's rules: filer.read_index(), manifest.load_manifest() and manifest.load_engagement_info() all answer from the fold of these lines (through the store, which keeps the fold so no reader pays for it twice), and there is no other copy. Its presence is what makes a folder an engagement (tracker/registry.py). A journal from before decision 104 may carry rules_imported and migrated lines; both are folded and neither is ever written again. A record that does not read as one is refused by name and the line, for every reader. A person never edits it, and `python -m tracker.store <store> check <root>` is how a person checks the database against it.

Disposable all the same - delete it and every fact it held is still in the journals - so it is never backed up, never synced and a person never opens it. One connection per process (connect(), close()), to the file in the data home unless TRACKER_STORE names another; the suite sets that per test. At the user_version `tracker/store.py` declares as `SCHEMA_VERSION`, raised by decisions 104 (the workbook's digest column went), 107 (the verdict cache's two tables), 116 (`override_reason`), 117 (the Filing Deadline column) 119 (the `intents` table) and later decisions, 143 the last (the documents' `container` column); a file at any other version is refused by name rather than opened, and an earlier one is deleted and rebuilt from the journals.

## Rules that cut across the code

- **rule:no-AI-on-client-documents** — No generative AI ever reads a client financial document. Every routing and status decision comes from deterministic rules in the manifest.
  - enforced in: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-ever-sent** — Nothing is ever sent. The system drafts client emails and stops. There is no SMTP, no mail client and no network call in the reminder or scheduling path.
  - enforced in: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scheduling.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-guessed** — Nothing is guessed. A document is filed only when exactly one request accepts it - or, when one document names several forms as itself, when each of those forms is accepted by exactly one request, or, when a broker's consolidated statement is accepted by several requests, when exactly one of them accepts it for its 1099-B, which then holds the whole statement. Ambiguous, contested and unrecognized files go to 00 - Needs Review for a person - misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/review.py`, `tracker/router.py`
- **rule:originals-are-never-altered** — Originals are never altered. Files are moved byte for byte under their own names out of Drop files here into the client's folder for the year; all work happens on copies, and every move is recorded in the record.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`

## Updating this map

```
python tools/repo_map.py update    # after any code change (incremental)
python tools/repo_map.py check     # verify it matches the working tree
```

Derived facts (imports, exports, CLIs, tests, hashes) are parsed from the source — never hand-edit them. Descriptions, artifacts and cross-language hops are curated in `docs/repo-map.curated.json`; edit that file and re-run `update`.
